         folded into its CTA's clocks) is known to the next grid on its GPU at its *largest*
         final clock over the terminal states (`Meet::finish`). Knowing an actor's final
         clock means knowing all of its events, whatever their numbering in one execution or
         another: dispatch's receivers issue a schedule-dependent number of bulk copies, so a
         minimum would name an event that is not the last one. Partial knowledge (other
         threads' clocks, synchronization sources) stays the minimum.
       - *Exit checks.* Completed async operations of finished CTAs leave `completed`, folded
         into their CTA's clocks: their exit checks ran at the group's end.
     - A group whose terminal states differ in any global byte, that is incomplete, or that
       has findings stops the procedure (later groups would need one continuation per final
       memory: not implemented).
- Argument. Let E be any execution of the whole case. We show that E is equivalent (same
  per-thread steps, findings and final memory) to E1 · E2 · ... · En, where Ei is an
  execution of group i from the state the earlier groups leave. Equivalently: for any
  conflicting accesses x of group i and y of group j > i, x precedes y in E. Then
  non-conflicting steps of different groups commute, and the only other contacts are
  excluded: synchronization objects are per CTA, and a later group's launch gate depends
  only on its own GPU's earlier launches, which are in its group or earlier (stream
  closure); without PDL those cannot wait on later groups.
  - Why x precedes y. The check runs on y in the continuation of group j and compares it
    against the shadow and the obligations.
    - The race shadow of a byte (`Sh`) holds its last write, the reads since, and every
      earlier access that write does not *cover* (`Sh::hw`, and reads kept in `Sh::r`; see
      E-WELLSYNC "Detector precision"). Every earlier access of the byte is in the shadow,
      HB-before a write in it that covers it, or is an obligation:
      - plain accesses are ordered with every write, else the group reported a race. Until
        2026-11-05 a strong write replaced the shadow outright, so a plain write followed by
        its own thread's atomic was dropped while another thread's atomic was still
        unordered with it (soundness-harness miss 1); now such an access stays in the
        shadow, is demoted with it and checked against the later groups;
      - strong reads need not be ordered before a later write (a poll that read an earlier
        value), so they are obligations;
      - unordered strong writes are obligations.
    - For an explored group, the shadow and obligations together cover the frontier (the
      shadow's writes and reads) of *every* terminal state. Under E-DRF the reduced search
      reaches every terminal state of the full one: equivalent executions end in the same
      state, the shadow included.
    - Any access x of group i in E either is in the frontier of E's projection on group i, or
      precedes that frontier's last write in time. y happens after the frontier, so y
      follows x.
    - Clocks: the continuation's clocks are lower bounds of every terminal state's (a
      certified run's clocks are lower bounds of every schedule's, C-WAIT), and propagation
      is monotone. An epoch (actor, clock) in an obligation comes from one terminal state.
      If the continuation proves y knows it, then in executions whose projection is that
      terminal state, y really knows it. In the others the obligation is vacuous or covered
      by their own frontier.
  - Values. Group j reads, for every byte an earlier group wrote, the earlier groups' final
    value: every conflicting earlier write precedes the read. That value is unique: a
    certified group's final memory is schedule-independent, and an explored group must
    agree in all terminal states. So exploring group j from the meet is exploring all of
    group j's behaviours in E.
- Multi-grid partial-order reduction. Several grids live at once (one per GPU in a
  collective's group) used to switch the synchronization reduction off (`sync_por_state_ok`,
  E-PDL). It now runs once nothing is left to launch and no live PDL grid waits on a running
  predecessor. The state is then a closed set of CTAs whose only contact is global memory:
  named in the footprints (strong accesses, spaces 10/11) or a race (E-DRF), as between the
  CTAs of one grid. `PTXV_NO_MULTIGRID_POR` restores the old rule. Effect: DeepEP
  `notify_dispatch` on 2 GPUs went from > 8M states (incomplete) to 24,329 (complete).
- Status: **argued**. Evidence below (docs/rung4.md, rung 4b "Launch groups").
- If wrong: *miss* of a cross-group interaction that the obligations do not cover.
- Where: `groups.rs`; `exec.rs` `access_x` (`xg`); `explore.rs` (`terminal_sink`,
  `sync_por_state_ok`); `wellsync.rs` (`certify_keep`, `carry`).

### E-LAUNCH-ORDER · code
**A case's launch list is the order the GPU enforced only when its `launch_order` says so:
"recorded" (written by a capture that records streams, events and graph edges) or "declared"
(a hand-written case, or a capture whose order other evidence establishes). Launch-order
exclusions rely on the list only then, and an unknown order orders no grid after another
(the strict reading, the default since 2026-11-12).** The list is one
ordered list per GPU: each grid's predecessor is the previous launch on its GPU, or `after`
(-1: none), with `pdl` for a programmatic edge, plus `waits` (further grids it starts after
they completed). Before 2026-11-11 every list counted as enforced, but the capture tools did
not record what would make that true (MISS 113): tools/capture.py and the in-process
ptxv.capture listed the launches of every stream in API order, tools/capture_dist.py
serialized a rank's streams even at a stream switch without an event (it warned "may overlap
... the case serializes them"), launches made during stream capture were listed in API order,
and the ProgrammaticEvent / LaunchCompletionEvent attributes, which make a waiting stream's
kernel start before the event's kernel completes, were not recorded. An exclusion could then
treat grids that ran at the same time as ordered: a wrong clean (repros, clean before the gate:
fixtures/e_launch_order UNKNOWN, e_ld_nc_pdl UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN_DONE, e_launch_order_l1
UNKNOWN).
- Recorded order (docs/capture.md, "Launch order"): an edge is written only where CUDA
  enforces it [doc, CUDA 13.0 cuda.h and runtime API]:
  - the previous launch on the same stream (with PDL, a programmatic edge);
  - an event: `cuEventRecord(e, S1)` after launch A and `cuStreamWaitEvent(S2, e)` before
    launch B: B starts after A completed (the event covers all work submitted to S1);
  - stream capture: the same rules among the launches of one capture (the graph's edges), and
    no edge between a captured launch and an uncaptured one (the graph runs when launched);
  - ProgrammaticEvent without triggerAtBlockStart: a programmatic edge ("the dependent
    launches can choose to wait on the dependency using the programmatic sync"); with
    triggerAtBlockStart, or LaunchCompletionEvent ("blocks of B may begin before all blocks
    of A have begun"; "not visible to cudaGridDependencySynchronize()"): no edge.
  A join (several predecessors) keeps one as `after` and the others in `waits`. An event's
  record ends at cuEventDestroy (the driver hands the handle to the next new event, and a wait
  on an event never recorded orders nothing; before the capture recorded cuEventDestroy, such a
  wait took the destroyed event's edge: a wrong clean, and GB300 overlapped the two kernels in
  99 of 100 runs) and at any graph launch (a graph's event record nodes); an event shared with
  another process (cuIpcOpenEventHandle, cuIpcGetEventHandle) orders nothing until destroyed;
  after cuStreamUpdateCaptureDependencies a capturing stream's next launch has no edge from
  what the stream was given before. Order the capture does not record (host synchronization,
  the legacy default stream's implicit synchronization, stream memory waits and copies, host
  functions, graph launches whose graph was not captured) is left out: it only removes edges,
  with one exception at the strict level. After a wait for a ProgrammaticEvent, an unrecorded
  operation on the waiting stream does not stop the programmatic edge from reaching the
  stream's next launch, which CUDA orders only after that operation (itself started at the
  primary's trigger), not after the primary's later writes [argued]. On GB300 the waiting
  stream's next kernel never started before the primary ended (0 of 100 runs directly after
  the wait, 0 of 100 with a memset between, 100 of 100 overlapped without the wait) [GB300
  measured], so there the edge is weaker than the hardware. A launch issued into a graph
  capture has no edge to any launch outside its capture: the graph runs when launched, maybe
  more than once, so a graph's kernels are unordered with the program's other kernels (a
  false alarm where the program orders them, e.g. an eager kernel after the replay on the
  same stream).
- What "recorded" needs from the records (python/ptxv/_order.py): every launch issued outside a
  capture names its stream by cuStreamGetId's id (a handle may be reused after the stream is
  destroyed; stream 0 is the legacy or the calling thread's stream depending on the entry
  point, and the id is queried through the call's own flavour); a launch inside a capture
  carries the capture's id and is named by handle within it (cuStreamGetId, cuStreamGetDevice
  and cuStreamGetFlags on a capturing stream fail with CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED and
  invalidate the capture, GB300 measured with the CUDA 13 driver; cuStreamGetCaptureInfo,
  cuStreamGetAttribute and cuStreamGetCtx are legal); no launch between the kept ones is
  missing from the records (ptxvcap injection mode with a filter writes
  `unrecorded_before`); the kept launches are in issue order; every record comes from a call
  that succeeded (each call is written once it returned); the kept launches of one process are
  on one GPU (a case written by one process has no per-launch device); and every record names
  its host thread, with the calls of different threads apart in time: each record's `t0`
  (before the call) after the `t1` (after the call returned) of every earlier record of another
  thread, so the records are in the order the driver took the calls (probes/launchcap keeps
  the launch being recorded per thread; before that, two threads launching at once gave launch
  records another thread's PDL attribute and stream, GB300 measured). Otherwise the capture
  writes `launch_order = "unknown"`.
- Gate (`Launch::order_recorded`, `Launch::order_completes_before`): with an unknown order,
  S-NC's stream-order exclusion and done-clock exemption, and E-L1-CORES's kernel-boundary
  exclusions (`grids_ordered`, the done-clock check of E-L1-HAVOC), do not apply. The S-NC
  message then names the gate. A recorded or declared case is checked for consistency: a launch
  without `after` must be on its implicit predecessor's stream when both name one (`stream`;
  crates/sim/tests/fixtures.rs `e_launch_order_stream_switch_needs_after`). The check reads
  only the case text: it cannot see an edge the capture wrongly derived (an event wait matched
  to the wrong record, launches of two GPUs listed on one).
- Unknown order, the strict reading (`Launch::order_recorded` false; crates/sim `launch_order`):
  every grid of the case loses its predecessors (each grid as `after = -1`, no `waits`), so any
  two of its grids may run at the same time, and a plain race between two grids that an older
  capture serialized is reported (fixtures/e_launch_order PLAIN_UNKNOWN: race; GB300 overlapped
  such a writer and reader on two streams without an event, the reader reading the bytes before
  the write in 199 of 200 runs). `PTXV_UNRECORDED_ORDER=ordered` keeps E-PDL's order for an
  unknown-order list instead (only the launch-order exclusions are gated), which misses that
  race. Until 2026-11-12 that was the default and the strict reading an opt-in
  (`PTXV_UNRECORDED_ORDER=concurrent`, MISS 127).
- Unknown order, the list's order checked for deadlocks (MISS 189, since 2026-11-12; crates/sim
  `serialized_order_deadlocks`): the strict reading lets every grid run alongside every other,
  so a grid that waits for a later grid of its list finishes there, while a GPU that runs the
  list in its order (one stream, as `ptxv hw` runs an unknown order) never starts the later
  grid and hangs: a wrong clean for a liveness bug. For an unknown order of several launches
  under the strict reading, `ptxv check`, equiv's and errdist's precondition and
  `ptxv compare`'s check also explore the list's order (E-PDL's order, the `ordered` reading)
  and add its deadlocks to the verdict (`list-order:` findings), nothing else: its schedules are
  the strict reading's with more ordering, so its races and stale reads are found there already
  [argued]. A deadlock whose signature the strict reading's verdict already has is not added:
  it is reported once, by the strict reading, and the note says the list's order adds none
  (probes/miss189_dupsig, fixtures/r5a_ibgda_putsig N6; until 2026-11-12 it was added again,
  under a note that the strict reading does not reach it [model]). A deadlock added removes
  E-WELLSYNC from the verdict's assumptions (no certificate); a pass that does not finish
  without one makes the verdict incomplete. Other
  serializations of the list (its grids in another order) are not checked: a deadlock that only
  they reach stays unreported [argued]. probes/miss189_order_hang (wait_flag spins on a flag
  that set_flag, the next launch, sets): good deadlock (clean before), DECLARED deadlock,
  CONCURRENT clean [model]; on GB300 (`run.sh`, `ptxv hw --no-num`) good and DECLARED were
  killed by the 20 s watchdog in every run and CONCURRENT (set_flag on a stream of its own)
  matched the expected output in 3 of 3 runs [GB300 measured]. Placement: strict (both fronts,
  every profile): the hang is the list order's on any GPU that runs it on one stream, a
  property of CUDA stream order [doc], not of GB300 timing.
- `waits` (E-PDL): a grid's CTAs launch once its predecessor allows it and every grid in
  `waits` completed, and join each one's done clocks; launch groups, slices and DPOR's
  footprints count them like a predecessor.
- `mem_sync_domain` (cudaLaunchAttributeMemSyncDomain and its map): S-SCOPE.
- Variants: a variant's launch-order edits (`after`, `waits`, `launch_order`;
  `Case::for_variant`) apply in `ptxv check` and `ptxv hw`, and since 2026-11-12 in the
  precondition and simulator runs of equiv and errdist, in `ptxv compare`'s check, in
  `ptxv num`, in the simulator runs that give `ptxv hw` its expected bytes and in
  `ptxv first-access` (the capture side's scratch suggestions). Before, those checked the case
  as loaded: a wrong clean for a variant whose edits break the order
  (fixtures/e_equiv_order UNK and UNORD gave clean preconditions;
  crates/cli/tests/launch_order.rs). The GB300 replays of equiv and errdist (hw-worker,
  errdist-gpu-worker) run it too since they get `--variant` (main.rs `worker_case`); before,
  they ran the case's own order. errdist's compiled models are of version 12 (MODEL_VERSION):
  an earlier one may hold a run of the case's own order, or of E-PDL's order of an unknown
  one, and is refused; the model key covers the reading of an unknown order. The certificate
  check's verdict cache (vcache.rs) keeps to the variants without such edits.
- Evidence: doc (the cuda.h text above; graph edge ports `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_*`);
  model: fixtures/e_launch_order (good clean; UNKNOWN race + violation, violation with
  `PTXV_UNRECORDED_ORDER=ordered`, clean before the gate; UNORD race + violation; PLAIN clean;
  PLAIN_UNKNOWN race, clean with `ordered`), e_launch_waits (good clean, NOWAIT race +
  violation, UNKNOWN race + violation, UNORD race), e_ld_nc_pdl UNKNOWN / UNKNOWN_DONE (race +
  violation; violation with `ordered`; clean before the gate), e_launch_order_l1 (UNKNOWN race +
  stale; stale with `ordered`; clean before), e_ld_nc_xgpu_unord (good, the order unknown:
  race + violation, violation with `ordered`; REC, recorded: clean on the PTX front through
  S-NC's launch-clock exemption, a violation at the SASS front's strict level; UNORD race +
  violation); source mutants lo-* (tools/mutate/srcmut.py). The capture side (docs/capture.md "Launch
  order"; argued from the CUDA semantics above, run on GB300): two streams with an event, the
  same without it (the race is reported; captured with the previous tools, it lists the
  launches in API order and is clean), a graph with a fork and a join, and two ranks through
  tools/capture_dist.py give the edges the semantics give; so do a wait on a new event that
  got a destroyed event's handle (no edge: the race is reported), one process with a kernel on
  each of two GPUs (unknown), and two threads launching through cudaLaunchKernelEx at once
  (every launch keeps its own PDL attribute and stream; unknown) or one after the other
  (recorded); python/tests/test_order.py. GB300 differential (`ptxv hw`, which since 2026-11-11
  runs each launch on a stream of its GPU with event edges across streams, and since 2026-11-12
  adds no stream order the case does not have and waits through an event for every predecessor
  but its stream's latest launch: docs/capture.md "Launch order"): with a 2 ms delay before the
  writer's store, e_launch_order UNORD, e_launch_waits NOWAIT and e_runner_after good differ from
  the ordered output in 200 of 200 runs, their ordered variants in 0 of 200 (e_runner_after good
  in 0 of 200 with the previous runner, which issued its reader behind the writer); without a
  delay, r4c_chunk2, r4c_dwrap and r4c_nowrap B37 differ from the capture in 199, 200 and 200 of
  200 runs (0 of 200 before), r4b_moe B37 in 0 of 200.
- kernel_db A/B (2026-11-11, model; builds before and after the gate): 119 records with two or
  more grids on one GPU and 10 one-grid-per-GPU controls, SASS and 4 PTX checks, 3000 states /
  300 s each. Of the 133 checks, 4 are complete in both builds, 69 stop at the budget with
  findings in both, 17 are inconclusive in both, and 43 time out or fail. No class in `got`
  changes; one record's S-NC findings include gated ones (DeepEP combine-reduce, a violation in
  both builds); 24 records gain a gb300 `latent-closed-world` stale read (the E-L1-HAVOC probe
  without the kernel-boundary credit, e.g. a grid reading what an earlier grid on its GPU
  wrote); the controls are unchanged. At 20000 states / 900 s the 30 records with `.nc` loads
  (10 of them with a class in both builds): no class changes, 3 records (DeepEP combine and
  combine-reduce) gain gated S-NC findings. The gate only removes exclusions, so a record
  without `.nc` loads keeps its strict-level classes at any budget [argued]; the 20 `.nc` checks
  still without a class at 20000 states are the precision cost not measured. The strict reading
  (`PTXV_UNRECORDED_ORDER=concurrent`) on the 90 decided checks (a verdict in both builds, 17 of
  them inconclusive): 38 time out at the same budget, and 19 of the other 52 change class. Of
  the 14 inconclusive ones that finish, 11 get races; of the 38 with a class that finish, 8
  change it (5 gain a race, 2 clean ones deadlock, 1 loses `divergent`).
- The 2 clean -> deadlock changes there (cute._rdma_barrier.i64.1 and cute._rdma_recv.i64.1,
  one case of two one-thread grids: _rdma_barrier polls a phase flag for RAIL_READY, which
  _rdma_recv resets) are the hang the strict reading admits, not a modeling artifact: on GB300
  (`ptxv hw --no-num`, the flag as output), with _rdma_recv submitted first and _rdma_barrier
  unordered on another stream, 5 of 5 runs hung (each killed after 20 s); in the order the
  capture declares (the barrier, then recv on one stream) 200 of 200 completed, and with recv
  unordered but submitted after the barrier 600 of 600 [GB300 measured]. The case meets the
  declaration evidence, and its declared copy is clean.
- kernel_db A/B of the strict default (2026-11-12, model; builds without and with it, 3000
  states / 300 s, no certificate): the 133 checks of the 2026-11-11 A/B, each on the declared
  copy of its case where the declaration evidence clears it (81 checks of 53 cases; the case
  store is unchanged) and on the stored case otherwise (52), plus the 42 re-captured records on
  their re-captures (recorded order). Declared copies and re-captures: no verdict changes (47
  and 27 checks decided in both builds, the others time out or stay inconclusive in both); the
