    undecided at the hardware level as well: a verdict is never clean while such a pair is
    unfenced. Case `alias_xspace = "race"` (or `PTXV_ALIAS_XSPACE=race`) reports
    `race:alias`; `"one"` treats them as one location (the model before 2026-11-10).
- Evidence, by class:
  - ISA / guide text (above): the rule for write-then-access pairs, the direction-free
    reading of 8.9.5, kernel completion as a fence.
  - GB300, measured: `probes/va_alias` (2026-11-10, results/litmus.txt), one allocation
    mapped twice in one process. A same-thread weak store through one mapping and a weak load
    through the other, with the second mapping's line in L1: stale in 200 of 200 runs
    (31,129,600 of 31,129,600 words); with `fence.proxy.alias` (`MEMBAR.SC.SYS; CCTL.IVALL`
    here): 0. Same shape inside a CTA across `bar.sync`: stale in 200 of 200 runs; a fence by
    the writer or by the reader: 0. Same-mapping controls: 0. Message passing across SMs with
    an acquire: 0 with or without the fence (the acquire's `CCTL.IVALL` drops every line). So
    GB300's L1 keeps lines by virtual address: the race is observable in these shapes.
    Cross-process (two ranks, peer mapping, release / acquire, no alias fence): 0 stale in
    131,072,000 reads (a bound, not a proof).
  - Argued, not measured: write-after-read pairs (a load through one mapping overtaken by a
    later store through another); the lenient strong rule; `griddepcontrol.wait` as a fence.
  - Model, fixtures: `r1h_nvls` (B66), `r1h_nvls_mp` (B67), `r1h_va_alias` (B68, B69, B74,
    B75), `r1h_va_war` (B76-B79, B84, B85; `rar` clean), `r1h_va_red` (B86), `r1h_va_async` (B80, B81; `same` clean),
    `r1h_nvls_l1` (B82 stale under the GB300 profile, B83 a race under it), `r1h_va_xspace`
    (the three modes), `r1h_va_wpoll` (internal tree; a blocked warp-level poll's reads keep their
    mapping).
- Model: the shadow is keyed by allocation (the physical backing): every mapping of an
  allocation reaches the same shadow bytes, and each access epoch records its mapping
  (`Epoch::view`: 0 primary, `MC_VIEW` multicast, k a view; part of the state hash). Reads
  since the last write keep one entry per (actor, strength, mapping), so a read through one
  mapping is not hidden by the same thread's later read through another. `resolve` notes the
  mapping of each global address a thread translates for the current instruction (per
  thread; cleared before and after the instruction); `access_x` looks it up; asynchronous
  units carry theirs (`Machine::async_view`).
- Capture (`tools/capture_dist.py`): a pointer that resolves through a mapping other than the
  owner's own (a peer import, a second map; matched by fabric handle, POSIX fd or IPC handle)
  becomes a reference to a `[[views]]` entry; each rank gets its own address space
  (`spaces`). A physical byte resolves through the owner mapping that covers it (an
  allocation may be mapped in pieces). The capture fails rather than guess the physical
  identity when a POSIX-fd import matches several exports of the same kind and size (unless
  `--allow-fd-guess`), when an IPC handle was taken from a pointer inside an allocation, when
  a multicast bind's range has no owner mapping covering it, or when a map, unmap, bind or
  unbind happens inside the captured window. A pointer into a mapping the recording does not
  know stays unresolved (a raw word: the model faults on a dereference). Cases captured before
  2026-11-10 collapse peer mappings onto the owner's buffer: their cross-process pairs were
  checked as one location.
- Hardware model (E-HW-L1): a multimem store or reduction neither updates nor drops the
  issuing SM's L1 lines of the unicast address, and counts as a write for the predictive stale
  check on that SM (lines are per virtual address, as measured for two unicast mappings; the
  multicast same-SM shape is not measured). Further mappings (views) share one L1 line per
  allocation in the model; their pairs stay `race:alias` at both levels.
- SASS: L-ALIAS-FENCE identifies the fence.
- Status: **argued** (PTX ISA text) for the rule; **measured** that GB300 shows the race for
  a second `cuMemMap` (above); multicast vs unicast read-after-write in the probed shapes
  needs no fence (E-MC-ALIAS-HW). Cross-address-space pairs: undecided.
- Where: `exec.rs` `resolve` (`va_note`), `access_view`, `alias_check`, `alias_self`,
  `launch_cta`, `Op::GridDepWait`, `Op::Fence { ProxyAlias }`, `complete_async`
  (`async_view`), `tmap_alloc`, `va_noted` (a blocked warp-level poll's race-detector reads,
  `spin::blocked_wpoll_read`, run outside the instruction with the mapping `wpoll_dry` noted); `machine.rs` `Epoch::view`, `Readers::insert_read`,
  `AliasPending`; `l1.rs` `l1_load`; `lib.rs` `build_launch` (views, spaces, `alias_xspace`);
  `tools/capture_dist.py` (`VRef`, `owner_addr`, `identity_errors`, `[[views]]`, `spaces`).
- If wrong: *false alarm* where hardware orders the mappings (E-MC-ALIAS-HW), for
  write-after-read pairs ordered by a control dependency on the read, and for a pair whose
  reads are all hidden behind another read of the same thread through the same mapping (not
  possible: kept per mapping); *miss* of a strong pair from two threads whose later
  accessor's fence precedes the earlier access (the lenient rule), in cases captured before
  2026-11-10 (peer mappings collapsed), under `alias_xspace = "one"`, and when the capture's
  physical identity is wrong despite the checks above.

### E-CPASYNC-PROXY · code
**cp.async writes and async-proxy reads.** The PTX ISA performs cp.async in the generic
proxy, so an async-proxy read of the bytes (TMA store source, `tcgen05.mma` operand) needs
a `fence.proxy.async` after the copy completed (cp.async.wait_group / wait_all) that
happens-before the read. ptxv reports a missing fence as a `contract` finding (the verdict
stays clean, "relies on E-CPASYNC-PROXY"), not a race.
- Where: `exec.rs` `proxy_check`: a shared-memory byte whose last write is a `cp.async`
  (`LDGSTS`; the copy lands as its thread's wait actor at the wait, E-CPASYNC). Before
  2026-11-06 it was a proxy race like an `st.shared` write.
- Fence after the completion (2026-11-10, MISS 34): while the copy's write ran in the
  issuing thread's name at its issue clock, a fence after the issue but before the wait
  counted. Now only a fence after the wait does, as the rule says. Triton's attention kernels
  fence between the issue and the wait for the second MMA group of their loop
  (`fixtures/r4_attn_triton` good: `cp.async.wait_group 2; bar.sync; ... tcgen05.mma` with
  the last `fence.proxy.async` before the wait; kernel_db triton parallel_attn_fwd): they
  get this contract finding now, at both levels (not in the gb300 profile), where the
  `sass_gb300` level was certified or clean. The read's issuer's fences are checked first,
  then the copy's own thread's, then those of every thread the read's clock knows; once per
  write epoch, a copy's later bytes with its first, and not again for a copy already reported
  against the read. `fixtures/e_cpasync_proxy_early` pins the rule: EARLY (the fence between
  the copies' issue and their wait) and NONE (no fence) are contract findings on both fronts,
  good (the fence after the wait) is clean
  (`cpasync_proxy_fence_must_follow_the_copy_s_completion`; source mutant
  `cpasync-proxy-fence-any-epoch`). A scan of every thread's fences per byte, in work in
  progress on the change, made the attention kernel 4x slower (5.5x in one A/B run of such a
  build) and kernel_db's triton fused_projection_rotary (54 CTAs of 128 threads; in its loop
  every thread fences after the barrier, so only the MMA issuer's fence happens-before the
  MMA) 20.8x (2323 s vs 112 s); now 0.4x the base's time (49 s vs 116 s, 2026-11-11).
- Evidence: none on GB300 either way. Triton kernels that fill shared memory with cp.async
  (LDGSTS), then `cp.async.wait_group; bar.sync`, then `tcgen05.mma` with no fence anywhere:
  mslk fp8 groupwise `.pinned` (two captures) and msl_ops `triton._wgrad.bf16.72x128`, 1000
  scrubbed runs each on GB300, every run bitwise equal to the simulator (F2, KA, 2026-11-06);
  nothing shows these runs could have failed. probes/proxy_cpasync (cp.async, wait_all,
  bar.sync, TMA store; variants with and without the fence) is correct in 1000/1000 scrubbed
  runs in every variant, its `st_none` variant (st.shared writers, no fence) included, while
  rung 1b B04 (st.shared writers) fails 1000/1000: probes/proxy_cpasync has no positive
  control, so it is not evidence, not even a measured null.
- probes/cpasync_proxy (2026-11-11, GB300, scrubbed shared memory, each variant against its
  own simulator run) puts cp.async writers into rung 1b's pipeline, where the st.shared
  writers without the fence fail. Launch shapes: grid 1, 152 and 608 CTAs of 192 threads. The
  epilogue fills the staging tile with st.shared or with cp.async: `cp.async.cg` 4 x 16 B or
  `cp.async.ca` 16 x 4 B per thread, retired by `cp.async.wait_group 0` or by
  `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive.noinc` and an mbarrier wait (with or without the bar.sync after
  it). `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` goes nowhere, before the wait or after it; the reader
  is a TMA store or a bulk store.
  - st.shared without the fence (B04): 1000/1000 runs wrong in every launch shape with either
    reader (10000/10000 at grid 1; 980 distinct outputs in 1000 at grid 1), so the probe sees a
    missing proxy fence after st.shared writes.
  - Every cp.async variant, the no-fence ones included, matches the simulator bitwise: 0/1000
    runs wrong per variant and launch shape, 0/10000 for the no-fence and before-the-wait
    variants at grid 1 (Wilson 95% upper bounds 0.0038 and 0.00038).
  - probes/cpasync_proxy/cpx.cu (standalone rounds into one reused buffer, 5 launch shapes up
    to 8 CTAs per SM, 1000 launches per cell): no variant fails, its st.shared control
    included, so it decides nothing.
  The positive controls a discharge needs, the cp.async variants without the fence, never
  failed. This is a measured null for cp.async writers in these shapes (GB300 measured, a
  bound), next to a st.shared control that fails in the same pipeline. It is not evidence that
  the fence is unneeded, and nothing is discharged.
- Placement: strict, and the finding stays in the gb300 profile: contract at both levels
  (kernel_db's triton parallel_attn_fwd reads contract at sass_gb300). Discharging it at the
  gb300 level needs a GB300 probe whose positive control (no fence) fails in a measurable
  fraction of runs and whose fence-before-the-wait variant does not (probes/cpasync_proxy has
  no such control: its no-fence cp.async variants never fail).
- Status: **unvalidated**: no cp.async failure seen in any probe, no mechanism argued.
- If wrong: *miss* reported only as a contract finding.

### S-INIT · code
**Initial state:**
- registers and shared memory hold garbage until written, and reading them first is reported
  (`violation`);
- the reserved first 1 KiB of shared memory (ptxas/driver bookkeeping) is initialized at
  launch, as zeros;
- a poll that reads never-written shared memory is a read of garbage, not a failed poll
  (MISS 40, E-SPIN: before 2026-11-10 such a spin blocked as if the value were 0);
- global buffers are initialized by the host. A captured case's buffer holds the bytes the
  first kept launch that references it saw (its pre-launch snapshot: tools/capture.py,
  `ptxv.capture`; 2026-11-12, MISS 173: before, a buffer allocated in the captured region and
  written by a copy, a host upload or a filtered-out kernel started as zeros). Where no snapshot
  covers a buffer allocated in the region, it is `init = "undef"` (a read of it is reported);
  a change between two kept launches that the case cannot express refuses the case.
- Where: `machine.rs` `Machine::new`; `exec.rs` `exec_thread` (registers) and `access_x`
  (smem).
- Status: **enforced** (2026-10-30), with these limits:
  - register reads are checked for operands that `Op::src_regs` lists (ALU, loads, stores,
    atomics). Address operands of mbarrier/TMA/tcgen05 ops are not checked yet;
  - the simulated value of an unwritten location is 0, so numerics on such a run are
    meaningless (the verdict already says so);
  - the zero contents of the reserved prefix are validated only by bitwise agreement;
  - conservative for tensor-core reads: a `tcgen05.mma` operand read of never-written (or
    undefined) shared memory is a sink, reported at the MMA (`uninit-smem`), even when the D
    lanes / columns it feeds are never read. TMEM keeps no undefined bits, so the value
    cannot be followed to a real sink. FA4's MXFP8 decode (8 query rows x 8 heads in an
    M = 128 MMA, `FlashAttentionForwardSm100DecodeMXFP8KeepsAb`): Q's TMA loads fill rows
    0-15 / 32-47 / 64-79 / 96-111 of the A tile, the other rows are never written, and their
    D rows (TMEM lanes 16-31 of each sub-partition) are never read (every `LDTM` is
    `.16dp32bit_t0_t15` / `_t16_t31`, lanes 0-15). Reported as 8 `uninit-smem` violations;
    value-dead (non-NaN fills of those rows leave the simulated output bitwise unchanged;
    GB300 with poisoned shared memory, NaN codes included, matches the captured output
    bitwise in 20 runs). A false finding, not a miss; following undefined A rows / B columns
    into TMEM would remove it.
- Evidence:
  - s_init B48 (partial producer): flagged on both fronts; GB300 is wrong in 200/200 scrubbed
    runs.
  - r0 B47 (deleted accumulator init): flagged on PTX. On SASS, ptxas reuses `%tid.x`'s
    register, so no unwritten register is read, but the numerics spec check fails. Outputs are
    bitwise those of the good kernel.
- **Undefined values propagate through register-only operations** (rung 4; predicates too
  since 2026-11-06, below): a written R / UR register keeps a mask of undefined bits. An ALU operation that reads undefined bits computes
  the undefined bits of its result, bit-precisely for moves, selects, byte permutes (`PRMT`),
  constant shifts, bitwise LUTs, low bits of adds and multiplies, and `F2FP` packing, and
  wholly otherwise; SHFL carries the source lane's mask. The read is reported only when an
  undefined bit reaches anything else: memory (stores), addresses, predicates and control
  flow, synchronization operands. Triton's cross-warp reductions shuffle and combine registers
  that only some lanes loaded, and ptxas's bf16 unpacking (`PRMT R9, R8, 0x7632, R9`) reads
  a register whose undefined half the next shift discards; both are correct code.
  (rung 5) Spills keep the mask: `STL` stores it with the data and `LDL` restores it
  (never-stored local memory is undefined). A compare whose combining predicate decides the
  result alone (`ISETP.NE.OR P6, PT, R18, RZ, P2` with P2 set) does not use its operands:
  torch's `where` loads R18 only under !P2.
- **Poison propagation to sinks** (2026-11-06). Undefined values are reported only where they
  reach a sink; register-only operations (moves, integer / float arithmetic, compares,
  selects, `PLOP3`, `P2R` / `R2P`, conversions) make their outputs undefined instead:
  - a predicate computed from undefined bits is undefined (`wp`): compares (`ISETP` /
    `FSETP` / `DSETP` / `HSETP2` / `FCHK`), carry-outs (`IADD3 R11, P0, PT, R2, R11, RZ` in
    Triton's `_philox_checksum_kernel`, where lanes that skipped a predicated `LDS` add
    undefined registers and the predicated store discards the result), `LOP3` predicate
    outputs, `PLOP3` outputs that depend on an undefined input, and an `ISETP` whose
    combining predicate is undefined. Before, each of these was reported at the operation;
  - an undefined guard on a register-only operation makes its destinations undefined (new
    value or old one);
  - `R2UR` and `HMMA` with an undefined input make their destinations undefined (`HMMA`
    mixes lanes: all of them);
  - packed f32x2 `FFMA2` / `FADD2` / `FMUL2`: each lane of the result is undefined only if
    the same lane of an operand is (2026-11-06; before, either lane tainted both: a false
    alarm on CuTeDSL FlashAttentionBackwardPreprocess, which packs two rows in one FADD2,
    `fixtures/e_uninit_f32x2`); PTX front (2026-11-08): a virtual register keeps undefined
    bits per bit (`Thread::vund`), `mov.b64 %rd, {lo, hi}` / `mov.b64 {lo, hi}, %rd` keep each
    half's, and `.f32x2` operations read each lane's. Before, a PTX virtual register was
    defined or undefined as a whole: FlashAttentionBackwardPreprocess 1x1x16384 repacks
    products of two rows into one 64-bit register, the out-of-range row poisoned the in-range
    one, and the PTX front reported undef-insensitive at ptx:647 where SASS is clean (a lowering
    imprecision, not an uninitialized read; `fixtures/e_uninit_f32x2_lanes`). Also on the
    PTX front (2026-11-08): a store of a virtual register marks undefined only the bytes
    whose bits are, and integer conversions of virtual registers (`cvt.u16.u32`,
    `cvt.s32.s8`, ...) keep the low bits' undefined bits (a sign extension takes the sign
    bit's). Before, Triton mxfp8 / nvfp4 quantize kernels stored the defined low byte of an
    `e4m3x2` / `e2m1x2` pack whose other byte came from an unwritten register, and the PTX
    front reported undef-insensitive where SASS is clean (`fixtures/e_uninit_cvt_lanes`).
    Conversions of a 16-bit or narrower source read only its bits (2026-11-08):
    `F2F.F64.BF16` / `.F16` (and FRND / F2F of 16-bit formats) the selected half, `I2F.S16` /
    `.U8` the low bits or `Ra.H1`. Before, `F2F.F64.BF16 R2, R16` after ptxas's
    `PRMT R16, RZ, 0x7610, R16` (zero into the low half, the high half unwritten) was
    undefined (`fixtures/e_uninit_half_cvt`);
  - lane by lane too (2026-11-06): `F2FP` narrow packs (`PACK_AB[_MERGE_C]`, `.RS` random
    bits taint both lanes) and unpacks (`UNPACK_B`), `HADD2.F32 Rd, -RZ, Ra.Hx_Hx` (one
    half), `HSETP2.BF16_V2` (the selected half of each operand); `FSETP` / `DSETP` / `HSETP2`
    whose defined combining predicate decides the result (`AND` false, `OR` true) are
    defined. msl_ops triton `_nvfp4x2_k_quant_kernel` (25 FCHK sites) and `_metrics_2d`
    were reported before (`fixtures/e_uninit_lanes`);
  - through memory (2026-11-06; generic and shared::cluster addresses, DSMEM included, since
    2026-11-07: BlackwellHistogramSelect's `ST.E.128` into a peer CTA): a shared or global
    store (or `atom.exch`) of undefined data
    marks the bytes undefined (`Sh::undef`) instead of being reported; a load or an
    `atom.exch` of them gives undefined registers (as for never-written shared memory); any
    other atomic of them (2026-11-09) returns undefined registers and stores undefined bytes
    (the new value depends on the old one: a carry, a compare; a failing compare-and-swap
    leaves them undefined); any other reader (TMA, MMA) reports; global bytes still undefined at a terminal state are reported
    (`uninit-gmem-exit`), except the tail of a used tensor map (S-TMAP-TAIL). Before, the
    store was the report (cute FusedRMSNormCombineFwdParallelTOPKStream's reduction
    buffer: clean now, `fixtures/e_uninit_smem`). Per byte (2026-11-07): a vector store
    marks only the bytes of its undefined registers (SASS: per byte of each 32-bit register;
    PTX `st.vN`: per element), and a store of the bytes a location already holds makes them
    defined unless an unordered store of undefined data may land after it. Before, one
    undefined register of an `STS.128` / `ST.E.128` marked all 16 bytes: msl
    BlackwellHistogramSelect rank 0 reads entry 56 of a vector store whose entry 59 is
    undefined (GB300 with 21 adversarial shared-memory fills: outputs bitwise equal to the
    clean run; `fixtures/e_uninit_vec`). Atomics: before, any atomic other than `atom.exch`
    on undefined bytes was the report, even with its result discarded and the word never
    read: histogram top-k kernels count out-of-range keys branch-free into a per-lane spill
    word nothing initializes or reads, a pool-select kernel adds 0 into a spare word
    (`fixtures/smem_spill_sink` good / add0 clean on both fronts; GB300, 1000 runs plain and
    1000 with scrubbed shared memory: outputs bitwise equal to the simulator). A later read
    of the word that reaches a sink (readspill) and a returned old value that reaches one
    (useret) are reported. The scratch-buffer rule is unchanged (a first access by an atomic
    keeps the captured bytes as defined input). A compare-and-swap's success result is
    undefined too when the compared old bytes are: the register of `ATOM.E.CAST.SPIN PT, Rd`
    was, the predicate of `ATOMS.CAST.SPIN[.64] P` is since 2026-11-11 (before, P was
    written as defined after the undefined-value tracking was reset). ptxas lowers a shared
    f32 or u64 add reduction to a load, the add and that loop; on a never-written word the
    loop's back branch now reads an undefined P, reported besides the CAS's undefined compare
    register (`fixtures/s_init_cas_spin` f32 / u64; test
    `cas_spin_success_predicate_of_undefined_bytes_is_undefined`, source mutant
    `cas-spin-pred-defined`). The PTX front's single read-modify-write with a discarded result
    stays clean.
  - `REDUX` (2026-11-07): an undefined bit in any active lane's operand makes the result
    undefined in every lane (a sum carries into all bits), reported where it is used. Before,
    the operand was a sink: Triton's cross-warp reduction (corpus pilot dash/5819, `_col_phase`)
    loads the warp partials only in threads tid < 32 (`@!P1 LDS R12`), every warp runs
    `REDUX.SUM.S32` on R12, and only thread 0 stores the result (`fixtures/e_uninit_redux`).
  - `STSM` data marks the shared bytes undefined like `STS`, and an `LDSM` of undefined
    bytes gives undefined registers (2026-11-07; their addresses stay sinks).
  - TMEM (2026-11-07): a `tcgen05.st` of undefined data leaves the words as never written;
    a `tcgen05.ld` of never-written words gives undefined registers (a `tcgen05.ld.red`
    result too), reported where used; the load itself is a `note` (`tmem-uninit-ld:<pc>`, was
    a violation). An MMA that reads never-written TMEM (accumulator with `enable_input_d`, A
    in TMEM, scale factors) leaves all of its D undefined (never written) and records a
    `note` (`mma-undef:<pc>`); before, an accumulator or scale-factor read was a violation
    (`mma-uninit-acc` / `-sf`) and an A read was not checked. Triton's pipelined attention prologue
    (corpus pilot dash/5713, `_t_causal_attention_kernel`) skips the first QK^T MMA when the
    loop runs zero times but its `LDTM` stays unconditional (GB300 with TMEM poisoned by a
    NaN tcgen05 matmul on every SM before each call: 0/20 wrong outputs, finite-fill control
    0/20; corpus pilot findings, 2026-11-07). `fixtures/e_uninit_tmem` is that shape with
    the scores unused: clean. dash/5713 itself stays reported: the scores feed the softmax
    (row max, `MUFU.EX2`), the O rescale factor (`FMUL R4, R111, R4` at 0x2eb0 on O loaded
    from TMEM) and P (`STTM`, then the PV MMA), and reach the output stores; that the result
    does not depend on them (O is zero there, m is reset by `FSEL R152, R152, -INF, P0`) is
    a property of the values, which this register-level propagation does not decide; the
    multi-fill rerun reports it `undef-insensitive` (S-INIT-FILLS).
  - Debug knob: `PTXV_UNDEF_TRACE=<thread>` prints each instruction the thread runs on
    undefined inputs (where a report's undefined bits came from).
  - sinks (reported): store data and addresses, every load / atomic / async-copy / TMA /
    tcgen05 / mbarrier / barrier operand that `Op::src_regs` lists, a guard of anything
    that is not register-only (branches, `EXIT`, memory, synchronization), branch conditions
    and `BRA.DIV` masks, `STSM` / `LDSM` operands, `SHFL` lane and clamp (its data keeps the
    source lane's mask), votes, `WARPSYNC` masks, `ELECT`, and every operation not
    listed as register-only. Anything not known to be register-only is a sink.
  - Where: `exec.rs` `undef_result`, `wp`, `reg_only`, `sinit_pre`, `poison_regs`,
    `exec_thread_inner`.
  - Evidence: `fixtures/e_uninit_discard` (`tests/fixtures.rs`
    `undefined_values_discarded_by_predicated_store_are_clean`): a predicated `LDS`, a 64-bit
    add with carry on the loaded registers, a store under the same predicate: clean on both
    fronts; variants that store unconditionally or branch on the carry are reported. The
    msl_ops `_philox_checksum_kernel` case is clean and matches its captured GPU output
    bitwise.
- **Loads of never-written shared memory** do not report by themselves: the loaded registers
  become undefined and a later read of them is the finding (`Machine::stale`). cuBLAS loads a
  try_cancel response's ctaid before testing its success bit, and never uses it when the
  request did not run. A multi-register `LDS` (`.64` / `.128`) makes undefined only the
  registers whose bytes nothing wrote: cuBLAS `gemmSN_TN_kernel`'s split-K reduction reads rows
  of 9-word slots with `LDS.128`, the 9th word of each slot padding nothing writes and nothing
  uses (fixtures/c_mm_f32_gemmsn_tn: clean, `hw --scrub` 1000/1000 = simulator with smem
  NaN-poisoned; before, all four registers were undefined and the output store was reported).
- If wrong: *miss* for unchecked operand kinds.

- `discard.global.L2 [a], 128` (PTX front, 2026-11-07, 3 SCALE corpus kernels): the line's
  contents become indeterminate (PTX: a weak write of an unstable indeterminate value),
  modeled as weak stores of a register nothing writes, so a later load gives undefined data
  and the write is race-checked. probes/discard_l2: write, discard, rewrite, read = GB300 50/50
  bitwise; `read_after` (no rewrite) is a violation, while GB300 returned the pre-discard
  values in all runs (the PTX contract allows either). SASS `CCTL.E.RML2 [Ra]` (2026-11-09,
  a CuTe combine-decode kernel): the same, as one 128-byte weak store of a register nothing
  writes (V255; the sim's undefined-store mask covers 128 bytes), so footprints, race checks
  and S-INIT treat it as any store. probes/discard_l2 (two warps: warp 0 writes, thread 0
  discards, warp 1 rewrites, warp 0 reads): GB300 50/50 scrubbed, both front-ends bitwise;
  `read_after` a violation and `race` (no barrier after the discard) a race on both fronts.
- **Scratch buffers** (2026-11-09, `fixtures/e_scratch_undef`). A global buffer declared
  `init = "undef"` starts with every byte undefined (`Sh::undef`; the simulated value is the
  file's or zero). A buffer declared `scratch = true` (capture writes it for buffers
  allocated inside the capture region) is resolved in `build_launch` (`resolve_scratch`): one
  run (`coverage::first_access`) records the first global access to it by any launch of the
  case. The buffer is produced inside the case, and becomes `init = "undef"` (note
  `scratch-undef:<name>`), when that access is a thread's plain write (not an atomic), or when
  it is a read and some plain write of the run is not ordered after it: not happens-before,
  or (`read_orders`) by another lane of the read's warp while the warp is diverged or has
  diverged since the read. The SASS front joins lanes of a split in whichever order the
  explorer runs the paths (E-LOCKSTEP), so that order is not one every schedule keeps.
  Otherwise the first access is a read (or an atomic, or an async actor's access: TMA, bulk
  copy or reduction, which may read) that comes before every plain write in every order, and
  the captured bytes stay an input (note `scratch-input:<name>`). The run stops once every
  scratch buffer is decided produced.
  Before, every buffer started defined with its captured bytes, so a consumer launch reading
  bytes no producer launch wrote read allocator garbage unreported (a backward chain's
  preprocess writes per-row sums at rounded offsets, the main kernel reads them at others).
  - Soundness: undefined bytes only add S-INIT reports (a read of them propagates and is
    reported at a sink); they never remove a finding or make a run clean. So a mis-declared
    buffer (a real input marked scratch or `undef`) cannot hide a read of captured input: if
    such a read happens after the first write in some schedule, it reads undefined bytes and
    is reported (a false report, never a miss). The classification does not depend on the
    resolving run's order: input means a read ordered before every write of the run, hence
    first in every order; anything else is produced. If the resolving run ends early (fault,
    step limit) without touching the buffer, it stays defined (the old behaviour). An input
    read of a buffer allocated in the region whose bytes nothing initialized (a kernel
    reading garbage before writing) stays unreported, as before.
  - Bytes of a scratch output no launch writes keep the captured values for the comparison
    with the GPU output (bitwise equal, as before); only reads of them are reported.
  - S-INIT-FILLS refills unwritten bytes of undefined buffers too (`fills.rs`), so an
    `undef-insensitive` verdict covers them.
  - Evidence: `tests/fixtures.rs` `e_scratch_undef_buffers`: good (the consumer reads only
    written rows) clean on both fronts; OFS1 (producer stride 24, consumer stride 32)
    reports the undefined rows reaching the output, and is clean with `scratch = false`
    (the miss); RDFIRST (warp 1 reads, CTA barrier, warp 0 writes) keeps the buffer as
    input; RACEW1 / RACEW0 (a copy of never-written bytes unordered with the writes, from
    warp 1 / from lanes of the writers' warp; RACEW0's first access is the read) are
    reported (`undef-insensitive`), never clean, and clean with `scratch = false`. Mutants:
    dropping the not-ordered-after check, or counting lanes of one warp as always ordered,
    make RACEW0 clean (both fronts / SASS) and fail the test.
  - If wrong: *false alarm* only, for an input written by something other than a case
    launch (a memset or copy inside the region) and then partly overwritten by a launch
    before the rest is read.
### S-INIT-FILLS · code
**Multi-fill rerun (an evidence class, not a certificate).** When every S-INIT report of a
verdict is undefined data left in global memory at the end of the launch
(`uninit-gmem-exit`), no undefined bit reached a branch, address, predicate, guard,
synchronization operand or non-load reader on the explored paths (those are sinks, reported
as `uninit-reg` / `uninit-smem` / `uninit-gmem`, and any of them refuses the rerun). The
launch is rerun on one deterministic schedule per fill, with every unwritten register,
uniform register, shared byte outside the reserved prefix, TMEM word and never-stored local
word holding the fill: 0, NaN (0x7fffffff), +Inf, -Inf, and two pseudo-random patterns. If
the output buffers are bitwise equal in all six runs (each run reaching every reported
undefined output, and no run reporting a sink), the
reports become kind `undef-insensitive`, with the note `undef-fills: 6 fills ... outputs
bitwise equal`; otherwise they stay violations and the note says which fill differed.
  Not run when the verdict has a race or several outcomes: undefined data from an
  ordering bug (a read before its write in some schedule) depends on the schedule.
- Where: `fills.rs` (`check`, called by `explore`, `explore_dpor`, `check_certified`);
  `PTXV_NO_FILLS` turns it off.
- Status: **argued** (2026-11-07). The gap: six fills are six points of a function of the
  undefined values; an output that differs only for other values (a compare against a
  specific constant, an exact cancellation that NaN and Inf break but random words do not)
  is missed. One schedule per fill: outputs that also depend on the schedule are compared
  on that schedule only. Undefined predicates are not filled (they would be sinks).
- Evidence: `fixtures/e_uninit_fills` (min(x, -inf) of an undefined x: undef-insensitive;
  x + 1: violation). Corpus pilot dash/5713 (Triton `_t_causal_attention_kernel`): Triton
  reads never-written TMEM (the scores of a QK^T MMA its peeled prologue skipped), and
  correctness depends on later value masking (O is zero there, m is reset to -inf, the PV
  result is overwritten): undef-insensitive in 6 fills, consistent with GB300 0/20 wrong
  under a NaN TMEM poison. The PTX good variants of `e_uninit_f32x2` / `e_uninit_lanes`
  were undef-insensitive too until PTX registers kept undefined bits per lane (2026-11-08;
  clean since, as on SASS).
- If wrong: *miss* of an output that depends on undefined values only at untried values.

### S-INIT-DEAD · code
**A buffer the case declares dead workspace is never read after the case** (2026-11-10). A
buffer with `init = "undef"`, `scratch = true` that is not an output (`ptxv.capture(scratch=
("ws",))`, capture's `scratch`) is a workspace whose contents nothing uses once the launches
end: a CuTeDSL kernel's L2-discarded workspace (`discard.global.L2`), a reduction scratch
written in part. Undefined data a store leaves in it when the launch ends is reported as a
note (`dead-undef-exit`), not the `uninit-gmem-exit` violation. Loads of its unwritten or
discarded bytes inside the case still give undefined bits, reported where they are used
(S-INIT), so a kernel that reads its workspace before writing it is still caught.
- Where: `build_launch` (`Alloc::dead`), `exec.rs` `undef_gmem_check`; listed in a verdict's
  assumptions when the launch has a dead buffer (`assumptions::for_machine`).
- Fixtures: `fixtures/s_init_dead` (good: undefined data copied within the workspace, a note
  and clean; LEAK: the same value stored to an output, a violation; READ: a branch on the
  unwritten workspace, a violation), `fixtures/s_init_dead_out` (the workspace also an
  output: no note, a violation). Mutant `dead-output` (an output counted dead) is caught.
- Status: **trusted**: declared by whoever captures the case. The capture side never applies
  it on its own (`scratch_suggestions` only lists buffers whose first access is a write or a
  discard, from `ptxv first-access`).
- If wrong: *miss*, for a later kernel that reads the workspace (outside the case).

### S-INIT-PRED · code
**Predicates start undefined too, and reading one before any write is reported** like an
unwritten register (`violation`, `uninit-reg:<pc>`). Until 2026-11-05 `Thread::preds` was
zero-filled with no undefined state, so a never-written predicate read as false in every
lane. The soundness harness (docs/soundness-harness.md, miss 2) NOPed the cuBLAS tile
scheduler's fast-path `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P4` in five nvjet kernels
(`c_mm_bf16_{mcast,nnt,ttn}`, `c_smm_nvf4`, `r2_cublas_gemm`): the `BRA !P4` after it read the
unwritten P4, every lane took the retry stub (the good kernel), and ptxv certified clean while
GB300 was wrong or hung in 198/200 runs. On GB300 the unwritten P4 is not false in every lane
(`tools/mutate/repro/uninit_pred` controls, 200/200 correct each).
- Defined: SASS `PT` / `UPT` (constants; `Reg::is_pt`: P7 / UP7 on the SASS front only, the PTX
  front's `%p7` is an ordinary register; until 2026-11-08 input coverage tested `idx == 7`
  alone and dropped the provenance of a PTX `%p7`, fixtures/e_cov_pt), and every predicate (per thread; uniform ones per
  warp) once an executed instruction writes it (`Machine::wp`: `ISETP`, `PLOP3`, `R2P`,
  votes, `SYNCS` results, ...).
- Reads checked: the guard of every instruction (the SASS lifter makes a branch condition
  the guard), in every member lane (`exec_inner`); predicate operands through `Op::src_regs`
  (`reg_umask` of `File::P` / `File::UP`), with S-INIT's rule that a register-only operation
  computes on undefined inputs and reports only where the value is used:
  - `SEL` / `FSEL` on an undefined predicate: an undefined result;
  - `PLOP3`: an output that depends on an undefined input is itself undefined, reported where
    it is used (ptxas's `PLOP3.LUT P0, PT, PT, PT, PT, 0x8, 0x0` constants do not depend;
    the uniformizing loop's first `PLOP3.LUT P0, PT, P0, P1, ...` reads the unwritten P0 and
    its result is overwritten by `R2UR P0` unread: probes/memhints). Until 2026-11-06 the
    read itself was reported. An operation computed from undefined bits leaves its predicate outputs
    undefined (`Machine::wp`). A `.SIGN` input is undefined when its register's bit 31 is
    (`pred_undef`); until 2026-11-11 (MISS 97) it counted as defined
    (`plop3_sign_input_with_undefined_bit_31_is_undefined`);
  - `P2R` keeps the undefined bits of the predicates it packs and `R2P` restores them (a
    spilled `PR`);
  - an `ISETP` whose combining predicate is undefined gives an undefined result (S-INIT's
    "decided" rule needs a defined combining predicate); reported until 2026-11-06;
  - since 2026-11-06 undefined predicates also arise from undefined register inputs, and
    are reported where they reach a sink (S-INIT, "Poison propagation"). The NOPed try-wait
    below is still reported: the `BRA !P4` is a sink.
- Where: `machine.rs` `Thread::pdef`, `Warp::up_def`; `exec.rs` `reg_umask`, `pred_undef`,
  `wp`, `exec_inner`, `undef_result`, `Op::R2p`; E-SPIN / C-PEEK state comparisons
  (`exec.rs`, `spin.rs`, `wellsync.rs` `reg_diff`) include the defined bits.
- Status: **enforced** (2026-11-05). Evidence: `fixtures/e_uninit_pred` (`tests/wellsync.rs`
  `branch_on_unwritten_predicate_is_reported`): the NOPed try-wait is reported at the
  `BRA !P4` (0x1b80); the good kernel and the three GB300-correct controls still certify.
  Every fixture keeps its verdict on both front-ends (full suite).
- If wrong: *false alarm* where hardware defines a predicate the model does not write (an
  unmodelled instruction's predicate output); *miss* only for predicates the lifter writes
  that hardware does not.

### E-WARPID · code
**`%warpid` is the warp's slot on its SM: fixed for the warp's lifetime, not determined by the
program.** The PTX ISA calls it volatile (a warp may be rescheduled) and points to `%tid` for a
logical warp index. Until 2026-11-08 the PTX front read it as the warp's index in its CTA
(`tid / 32`), so a kernel that used it as a warp index was clean while GB300 gave other values.
A register-only instruction that reads `%warpid` leaves its destinations undefined (every
bit, every lane); S-INIT reports any use of them that reaches a sink, and any other reader is a
`violation` itself (`warpid-use:<pc>`). S-INIT reports in a kernel that reads it say it may be
the source, and S-INIT-FILLS is not applied (the fills do not range over the slots).
- Where: `exec.rs` `exec_thread`, `report_uninit`; `fills.rs` `check`; `ptxv_ir::reads_warpid`.
  SASS: `S2R SR_VIRTID` (from which ptxas extracts `%warpid`) is the same register; its
  value is undefined, so the field layout does not matter.
- Status: **validated**: probe (1024 CTAs x 64 threads, `%warpid` read twice 200 us apart, GB300,
  CUDA 13.0, 2026-11-08): `%warpid != tid / 32` for 55808 of 65536 threads, 14 distinct values
  (0..13: several CTAs per SM), no warp's value changed between the reads, all lanes of a warp
  agree; `%laneid == tid % 32` in every thread. fixtures/e_warpid.
- If wrong: *false alarm* only (an undefined value stands for every slot).

### S-TMAP-TAIL · code
**GB300's TMA ignores bytes 0x40..0x7f of a 128-byte tensor map in global memory.** A store
that leaves undefined data there is a `contract` finding (`tmap-tail-undef:<pc>`), not an
S-INIT violation, when a TMA of the launch uses that map; a TMA reading undefined bytes in
0x00..0x3f is a violation (`uninit-gmem`). msl_ops dist_moe (`dm_combine_w2` / `w4`) copies
only the 64-byte template and publishes the rest of the map with lanes 16..31's undefined
registers (`ATOMG.EXCH` at 0x2790).
  The tensormap proxy fence (`fence.proxy.tensormap`, `UTMACCTL.IV`) reads the 128 bytes with
  the same exemption.
- Where: `exec.rs` `tmap_at` and `Op::TmapFence` (`undef_ok_from`), `undef_gmem_check` (from
  `exit_checks`).
- Status: **validated** (`probes/tmap_tail`, GB300, CUDA 13.0, 2026-11-06): 24 driver-encoded
  rank-2 maps (u32 / f32 with NaN OOB fill; swizzle none / 32B / 64B / 128B; boxes inside
  and across both tensor edges), each loaded through global memory with bytes 0x40..0x7f as
  encoded (the derived box-bytes / swizzle-repeat words are nonzero), zero, all-ones and
  random (3 runs each): every shared-memory tile bitwise equal to the first encoded run's (0
  of 216 loads with the tail altered differ, 0 of 48 repeat encoded loads). Library-built maps (cuBLAS packs maps 64 bytes apart) were already
  evidence that bytes 64..127 are not read (docs/tensormap.md). Not probed: rank > 2,
  im2col, sub-byte types.
- If wrong: *miss* of a TMA that depends on the undefined tail.
- Retire: NVIDIA documentation of the descriptor layout.

### S-DSMEM · code
**A CTA's shared addresses are `(cluster rank << 24) | offset`**, its window inside the
cluster's shared window. A `shared::cluster` access goes to the CTA named by the rank byte. In a
cluster launch, a `shared::cta` access whose rank byte is not the CTA's own is a fault (GB300
traps with *illegal instruction*: `probes/reserved_smem`, variant `cluster_untagged`). `mapa`
replaces the rank byte.
- Evidence: ptxas forms every shared address as `LEA R, SR_CgaCtaId, off, 0x18`, and lowers
  `mapa ..., 0` to `PRMT R, RZ, 0x654, R` (clear the top byte).
- `mapa` with a rank outside the cluster (2026-11-08): ptxas lowers mapa to `PRMT R, rank,
  0x654, a` with no check, and CuTe kernels compute a peer address in every lane (rank =
  %laneid) and use it only in lanes below the cluster size. The result is an undefined
  address (S-INIT), not a fault; an access through it is reported. Before, the mapa itself
  faulted (PTX front runs of CuTe 2-CTA GEMMs). probes/mapa_lanes: GB300 50/50 scrubbed, both
  fronts bitwise; variant oob (a lane stores through rank 2): reported on both fronts, GB300
  fails the launch.
- Outside a cluster launch (MISS 209, 2026-11-12): in a launch without cluster dimensions GB300
  traps ("an illegal instruction was encountered") on st.async (STAS, `.b32` and `.v2`),
  red.async into shared::cluster and cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster.shared::cta (UBLKCP.S.S),
  also when they address the CTA's own shared memory. ld / st / atom `.shared::cluster` through
  mapa, mapa, barrier.cluster, cluster fences, remote mbarrier arrive / expect_tx, try_wait
  `.cluster`, cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster.global (multicast too) and
  clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel (`.multicast::cluster::all` too) run either way
  (probes/cluster_launch_ops: 20 cases, `ptxv probe`). A launch is a cluster launch when the
  case gives `cluster` (the runner's launch attribute: `cluster = [1, 1, 1]` runs st.async,
  stasync_attr1) or the kernel carries `.reqnctapercluster` (cubin EIATTR_CTA_PER_CLUSTER) or
  `.explicitcluster` (EIATTR_EXPLICIT_CLUSTER): the directive alone makes one
  (`%is_explicit_cluster` reads 1; `.explicitcluster` without a shape: 1 x 1 x 1, and without
  the launch attribute GB300 fails the launch with "cluster misconfiguration").
  Model: st.async and UBLKCP.S.S fault when the launch has no cluster (exec.rs
  `needs_cluster_launch`); red.async into shared::cluster is not lifted. A kernel's compiled-in
  cluster (PTX directives, cubin EIATTRs: `ClusterDecl`) is the launch's cluster when the case
  gives none, and a case cluster that differs from it is a capture mismatch
  (`ClusterDecl::resolve`); the hardware runner passes it as the launch attribute, and also
  when the function requires one (`CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CLUSTER_SIZE_MUST_BE_SET`). Until MISS 209
  st.async outside a cluster launch ran as inside one (`ptxv check` clean where GB300 traps,
  probes/stasync_no_cluster), and the runner launched a kernel with `.explicitcluster` and no
  case cluster without the attribute (GB300: the launch error). `crates/sim/tests/fixtures.rs`
  `probe_cluster_launch_ops_match_hardware`: every lifted case and variant on both fronts has
  GB300's classes and, where it ran, its output; mutants cluster-launch-fault,
  cluster-decl-ignored and cluster-eiattr-ignored caught. kernel_db: the 170 case directories
  with st.async or UBLKCP.S.S all give a cluster [kdb scan]. Capture: launchcap and `ptxvcap.c`
  record the launch's cluster dimension attribute (`cluster_attr`), and `tools/capture.py` and

### S-SWIN · code
**The generic shared window.** A generic address whose high word is `SR_SWINHI` is the
shared::cluster address in its low word: `(SWINHI << 32) | (rank << 24) | offset`. ptxas forms
`cvta.shared` as `{SR_SWINHI, LEA(SR_CgaCtaId, off, 0x18)}` and a generic `mapa.u64` as
`PRMT R, Rrank, 0x654, Rlo` (replace the rank byte); `LD.E` / `ST.E` through such an address
reach that CTA's shared memory. The model's window is `0x7c00_0000_0000` (GB300's high word
was 0xfffa, near its global allocations); only its being one 4 GB window matters.
- `QSPC.E.S` (`isspacep.shared::cta`) holds for a window address of the CTA's own rank,
  `QSPC.E.D` (`isspacep.shared::cluster`) for one of any CTA of its cluster, neither for a
  global address (PTX ISA, isspacep: "shared::cluster will return 1 for every shared memory
  address that is accessible to the threads in the cluster, whereas shared::cta will return 1
  only if the address is of a variable declared in the executing CTA"; GB300:
  probes/qspc_window, own / peer / global addresses in clusters of 2, 128/128 words, SASS
  front bitwise). A window address of a rank outside the cluster, or past the CTA's shared
  memory, is reported as not modeled. Until 2026-11-12 any QSPC of a window address was
  reported as not modeled; the fallbacks never reached one, because the SASS front performed
  the generic f32 add there (MISS 142).
- Evidence: flashinfer's routing cluster kernel reads peer CTAs' shared memory this way.
- Where: `machine.rs` `SHARED_GENERIC_BASE`, `exec.rs` `sreg` (`SharedWindowHi`), `resolve`,
  `Cvta`, `Mapa`, `Qspc`, `Op::Atom` (a generic atom's predicate result).
- Status: **validated**: `fixtures/s_routing_forms` (cvta.shared, generic mapa, `LD.E` /
  `ST.E` / `LD.E.U16` into this and the peer CTA) = GB300 bitwise, 1000/1000.
- If wrong: *miss* / *false alarm* on generic DSMEM accesses; shows as a bitwise mismatch.

### E-PAIR · code
**`cta_group::2`:** the PTX paired `tcgen05.dealloc/relinquish` act on each CTA's own TMEM (both
CTAs of the pair issue them); the paired `tcgen05.alloc` is one allocation of the same columns in
both CTAs by a warp of each, together (a rendezvous, below). The pair MMA is issued by the even
CTA; CTA i supplies A rows and receives D rows 128i.., and supplies B rows (N/2)i.., all at the
same descriptor / TMEM addresses. A multicast commit becomes one commit per destination CTA in
the issuing pipe.
- Where: `ptx` tcgen05 lowering, `exec.rs` `Op::Mma` (pair), `complete_mma`, `Op::TcCommit`.
- Status: **validated** by `fixtures/r1c_2sm`: an fp64 reference first confirmed the operand
  split on GB300, then the PTX model matched GB300 bitwise (1000/1000, scrubbed). B12 (commit
  mask without the peer) hangs on GB300, as the model's deadlock predicts.
- Order of the pair alloc (2026-11-11, with MISS 119): each CTA's alloc marks its own TMEM, so
  the leader's pair MMA, which writes the peer's TMEM, must be ordered after the peer's alloc
  by synchronization. In `fixtures/r1c_2sm`, and `e_tc_handback` / `e_sttm_late` built on it,
  nothing does on the PTX front: the cluster barrier after the allocation arrives `.relaxed`
  (PTX ISA 9.5: "no memory ordering and visibility guarantees provided for the memory accesses
  performed prior to barrier.cluster.arrive"), and since MISS 119 the peer's TMA complete-tx
  releases only the copy's own writes (S-MBAR-SCOPE). Their PTX verdicts now include that race
  (model; good and B12, every variant of the other two). Until MISS 119 the complete-tx
  released the peer thread's whole clock, its alloc included, but to the leader's .cta-scoped
  wait only under the contract reading that it is performed in the mbarrier's CTA
  (S-MBAR-SCOPE), so the pair was already reported as a contract deviation; it is a race now.
  The ISA does not make the paired alloc a rendezvous: the first warp "could block until the
  second warp in the Peer CTA also performs the operation" (9.7.18.5). The SASS front stays
  clean: ptxas's handshake has the leader allocate in both CTAs (S-RESERVED). Open: whether the
  relaxed cluster barrier with the tcgen05 fences around it orders the pair (9.7.18.6.3 lists
  "barrier instructions" among the execution ordering instructions the fences compose with,
  though 9.7.18.6.1 lists tcgen05.alloc as synchronous and the fences' ordering clauses name
  asynchronous operations), or whether the paired alloc should be modeled as a rendezvous;
  either would clear these races. GB300 runs r1c_2sm good bitwise correctly (above): a measured
  null, which discharges nothing. The rendezvous (next bullet) clears them.
- Paired alloc as a rendezvous (2026-11-12, MISS 179): `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` is a
  collective of one warp from each CTA of the pair, "one warp from each of the peer CTAs must
  collectively perform the allocation", whose first warp "could block until the second warp in
  the Peer CTA also performs the operation" (9.7.18.5); TMEM allocation is not a memory-model
  location. The first warp to execute it arrives (`PairAlloc::Arrived`) and waits
  (`split_enabled`). The second allocates the first run free in both CTAs, marks the columns of
  both as one fresh actor's epoch 1 (an async id of the even CTA's warp, the same in every
  schedule) at the join of both warps' clocks, and writes its address; the first then takes the
  columns (`PairAlloc::Done`) and writes its address. Each warp's representative takes the
  marks' epoch, into its tcgen05 view too (the alloc is one of its tcgen05 operations), and
  nothing of the other warp: the rendezvous orders the allocation before both warps' later
  instructions and synchronizes no memory. So the leader's paired MMA, issued after its own
  alloc, is ordered after the allocation in the peer's TMEM: `fixtures/r1c_2sm` good and B12,
  `e_tc_handback` good and `e_sttm_late` good and STW no longer report the race on the PTX
  front: they are contract again, their remaining findings being S-MBAR-SCOPE's [model].
  `fixtures/e_tmem_pair_alloc`: good is clean (on SASS a contract at every level, the gb300
  profile's too: ptxas's dealloc overwrites the stored address's registers, cleared only by
  memory-queue orders that no GB300 probe measured, sb-unmeasured:war-nosb); ONESIDED (rank 1 does
  not allocate) deadlocks, rank 0's warp waiting in the alloc, where each CTA allocating on its
  own ran to the end (an S-INIT violation: rank 1 stored the address it never got) [model]; on
  SASS, ptxas's lowering has the even CTA allocate in both without waiting, and ONESIDED is a
  TMEM leak. A first warp
  that runs on before its peer comes would add only schedules in which its later instructions
  precede the peer's earlier ones; nothing orders those pairs either way (no memory
  synchronization is modeled), so a value passed between them is a race in both models (E-DRF);
  a peer that never comes is a deadlock here and a bug on hardware either way. The certificate
  logs one allocator event per warp, in its own CTA (C-ORDER): the second warp's allocation, and
  the first warp's taking of the columns, whose clock has not moved since it arrived. The SASS
  front is unchanged (ptxas's handshake, S-RESERVED). Test `tmem_pair_alloc_is_a_rendezvous`,
  source mutants `pair-alloc-per-cta`, `pair-alloc-first-runs-on` and
  `pair-alloc-marks-own-thread`.
- Block-scaled pair MMAs (N-MMA-BS): each CTA's D rows use the scale factors in its own TMEM.
  The pair `tcgen05.cp.cta_group::2` (SASS `UTCCP.T.S.2CTA.4x32dp128bit`, S-TCCP) is issued by
  the even CTA and copies each CTA's shared memory to its own TMEM, at the same addresses; it
  also writes the peer's TMEM, so the peer must observe it before exiting, as for the pair MMA.
  An odd CTA issuing either is reported as unmodeled.
- Status (block-scaled pairs, 2026-11-04): **validated** by `probes/tc_pair_bs` (MMA) and
  `probes/tc_pair_bs/cp` (copy). Every operand and every smem word differs between the two
  CTAs, and both front-ends equal GB300 bitwise. In the copy, CTA r's TMEM lane 32w + i,
  column j holds its own word 4i + j (rank << 16 | 4i + j); no word comes from the peer.
  End to end: cuBLASLt's NVFP4 kernel `fixtures/c_smm_nvf4` (M = N = 128 as an M = 256 pair
  tile, B split 64 / 64) equals GB300 bitwise (docs/equiv-mma.md §5).
- **M = 128 pairs** (PTX ISA "Layout B", `cta_group::2`, dense): CTA i supplies A rows 0..63
  of its own descriptor (D rows 64i..) and B rows (N/2)i.. ; its D row r, column c is at TMEM
  lane r + 64 (c / (N/2)), column c % (N/2): lanes 0..63 hold the first half of N, lanes
  64..127 the second, N/2 columns wide (`exec.rs` `mma_d_layout`, `MmaD`). Shapes: N = 16..256
  in steps of 16 for M = 128 and 256 (PTX ISA table 48); block scaling and sparsity with
  M = 128 pairs are rejected (not measured). **A in TMEM** (2026-11-07, KA: FlashAttention
  Bf16x6 forward / backward): every D lane reads the A row in its own TMEM lane, so lanes
  64..127 (the second N half, B rows of CTA 1) use lanes 64..127's A rows, not lanes 0..63's
  (`complete_mma` `arow`). probes/tc_pair_atmem (N = 64, pattern operands naming A row, B row
  and CTA in each exact result; both CTAs' whole TMEM dumped): GB300 20/20, both front-ends
  bitwise.
- Status (M = 128 pairs, 2026-11-05): **validated** by `probes/tc_m128` (kind::f16 bf16, N = 16,
  32, 48, 64, 128, 256; kind::f8f6f4 e4m3, N = 16, 32, 64; M = 256 N = 32 / 64 as controls).
  Each CTA's whole TMEM is sentinel-filled before the MMA and dumped after it; with operands
  that encode (A row, B row, CTA) in the exact result, exactly the cells above change, with
  the predicted rows. Both front-ends equal GB300 bitwise on every config
  (`crates/sim/tests/tc_m128.rs`; fixture `e_mma_pair_m128`). End to end: the cuBLAS 2-CTA
  nvjet kernels with M = 64 per CTA (`..._64x32_64x16_2x2_2cta_h_bz_NNT` for 512 x 128 x 512
  and 512 x 256 x 512, `..._128x64_64x10_2x2_2cta_...` for 1024 x 128 x 1024) certify
  (E-WELLSYNC) and equal their captured GPU outputs bitwise; before, their epilogue's reads of
  lanes 64..127 were reported as reads of never-written TMEM.
- If wrong: sparse M = 128 pairs ("Layout C") and other forms are rejected as unmodeled.

### S-RESERVED · code
**Reserved shared memory (0x0..0x3ff) starts at 0, except in `cta_group::2` cubins**
(`EIATTR_TCGEN05_2CTA_USED`), where the driver sets words `0x0 = 0x1ffe00`, `0x4 = 0x7ffff800`,
`0x50 = 1` in even ranks (the leader's handshake phase bit), and the word at `0x48` is a
**count-1 mbarrier in phase 0** (its sync-unit state is not visible through loads, which read
0). ptxas's paired-allocation handshake runs on these: the leader's `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA` allocates
in both CTAs, then `arrive.expect_tx(4)` + `STAS` hand the column to the peer's slot through
the peer's 0x48 barrier, and the peer arrives back on the leader's.
- Evidence: `probes/reserved_smem` (dump at kernel entry; zero without the 2CTA attribute),
  `probes/mbar_reserved` (try_wait / arrive.expect_tx / complete_tx on 0x48 behave as count 1,
  phase 0), `probes/mbar_zero` (a plain-stored zero word is *not* such a barrier: the arrive
  faults). There is no prologue code in the SASS.
- Where: `machine.rs` `Machine::new` (SASS front, kernels with a paired alloc or MMA).
- Status: **validated** by `fixtures/r1c_2sm`: SASS model = PTX model = GB300 bitwise.
- If wrong: the handshake would deadlock or race in the model; other reserved words are
  unknown and read as written-by-launch values.

### S-SCOPE · code
**Strong memory operations follow the PTX memory model's scope rules.** mbarrier scopes:
S-MBAR-SCOPE (until 2026-11-09 they were treated as sufficient). Since rung 1f:
- `ld/st.relaxed|acquire|release.<scope>`, `.volatile` (= relaxed.sys) and `atom` / `red`
  (default relaxed.gpu) are strong accesses. Two strong accesses are **morally strong** when
  each one's scope includes the other's thread (`.cta`: same CTA, `.cluster`, `.gpu`: same
  GPU, `.sys`: all) and, on the PTX front, they overlap completely (below). Morally strong
  accesses do not race; any other conflicting pair not ordered by happens-before is a race.
- Memory synchronization domains (2026-11-11, MISS 113): `.gpu` includes only the threads of
  grids in the same domain (case `mem_sync_domain`, captured from
  cudaLaunchAttributeMemSyncDomain / MemSyncDomainMap or the stream's attribute). CUDA 13.0
  cuda.h, CUlaunchMemSyncDomain [doc]: "Memory operations done in kernels launched in
  different domains are considered system-scope distanced. In other words, a GPU scoped memory
  synchronization is not sufficient for memory order to be observed by kernels in another
  memory synchronization domain even if they are on the same GPU." Kernel boundaries are not
  changed (stream order still joins done clocks). fixtures/e_mem_sync_domain: a .gpu release /
  acquire between concurrent kernels of domains 0 and 1 is a race, the .sys pair clean (clean
  before the domain was modeled). Older captures carry no domain (0 for every grid): they
  serialize a GPU's grids except PDL pairs, so only a PDL pair in different domains that
  synchronizes at .gpu scope could be missed.
- The NIC (MISS 193, 2026-11-12): a NIC actor is not a thread. Its accesses take the GPU of the
  thread that rang its doorbell, so that GPU's `.gpu` scope includes it, but it is in no CTA or
  cluster (`nic_apart`; PTX ISA 9.5 section 8.5: the `.cta` and `.cluster` scopes are sets of
  threads). Until 2026-11-12 it took the doorbell thread's CTA and cluster: in fixtures/e_nic_cta
  (one GPU, a loopback QP) a reader in the doorbell thread's CTA that polls the fetch-add with
  `ld.acquire.cta` (CTA) or `ld.acquire.cluster` (CLUSTER) synchronized with it on the PTX front,
  a wrong clean; now the poll and the fetch-add are not morally strong and race (model). The SASS
  front reports CTA as a race before and after (`LDG.E.64.STRONG.SM`, no `CCTL.IVALL`; the GB300
  profile re-run: a stale L1 read, nondeterministic) and CLUSTER as clean (`LDG.E.64.STRONG.GPU`,
  then `CCTL.IVALL`); GPU and SYS stay clean and OTHERCTA a race (model). kernel_db: no verdict is
  expected to change (argued). None of the 774 QPs of the 44 NIC records is a loopback QP (record
  data), so the only NIC writes a thread in a doorbell thread's CTA reads are the CQEs on its own
  GPU. DOCA's CQ poll reads the CQE owner byte with `ld.relaxed.sys` and acquires with
  `fence.acquire.sys` (static, cute.A2aHybrid.w2). Every CTA-scope load in the records reads one
  field of the QP state that GPU threads update with CTA-scope atomics: the 315
  `ld.relaxed.cta.b64` of the PTX records and the 165 `LD.E.64.STRONG.SM` of the SASS records, all
  at offset 184; the PTX `.cta` fences follow lock loops on that state (static). Source mutants
  nic-scope-cta and nic-scope-cluster. Placement: ISA text applied to the NIC, the strict level of
  both fronts (the hardware model treats every strong pair as morally strong, E-HW-L1).
- Complete overlap (MISS 80, 2026-11-11). PTX ISA 9.5 section 8.7: two operations are morally
  strong only if all of these hold: "The operations are related in program order (i.e, they are
  both executed by the same thread), or each operation is strong and specifies a scope that
  includes the thread executing the other operation"; "Both operations are performed via the
  same proxy"; "If both are memory operations, then they overlap completely." 8.2.1: "The
  overlap is said to be complete when both memory locations are identical, and it is said to
  be partial otherwise"; 8.2.4: a vector access is "a set of equivalent memory operations with
  a scalar data type"; 8.2.5: a packed access is "a pair of equivalent memory operations on the
  scalar data type". 8.7.1: two conflicting operations "not related in causality order and
  ... not morally strong" are a data-race; 8.7.2: one that overlaps partially is a mixed-size
  data-race, and "The axioms in the memory consistency model do not apply if a PTX program
  contains one or more mixed-size data-races". Observation order (8.9.2: "R and W are morally
  strong and R reads the value written by W") and release / acquire synchronization (8.9.4)
  run along morally strong pairs only.
  - Until 2026-11-11 `morally_strong` checked scopes only: fixtures/e_scope_mixed MIXED (a u8
    `ld.acquire.gpu` of a u32 `st.release.gpu` flag, then a plain read of the data) and WIDE (a
    u64 acquire) were clean on the PTX front, and e_warp_order_mixed MIXED (a u8 load of a byte
    of a u32 store on the next instruction of a converged warp) was nondeterministic.
  - Now, on the PTX front at the strict level, two strong thread instructions are one location
    when their scalar elements are the same size (`same_location`, `elem_bytes`: the ld / st
    element, the atom / red operand, `.v2` / `.v4.f32` per element, `bf16x2` per half, the
    `multimem.ld_reduce` and `multimem.st` lane). Both cover the byte being checked and each
    element is naturally aligned (S-ALIGN), so equal sizes are one location. A partially
    overlapping strong pair is a race (the message says mixed-size data race); a partially
    overlapping read does not synchronize with the write (`sync_observe_cell`), its own thread's
    included, and does not continue its release sequence (`sync_publish`); a strong write no
    longer drops an ordered earlier strong access of another size from the shadow (`access_x`
    `keep`).
    e_scope_mixed VEC (a relaxed v2.u32 load whose first element is the flag, then
    `fence.acq_rel.gpu`) stays clean. A packed `multimem.st` (`.f16x2`, `.e4m3x4`) is one
    location per value (8.2.5), as `multimem.ld_reduce` is per lane; until 2026-11-11 it was
    one location of its register width, so an f16x2 store and an unordered f16x2 reduction of
    the word were a mixed-size race (fixtures/e_scope_mm_lane good, a false alarm;
    nondeterministic now; MIXED, a .b32 store against the f16 lanes, stays a race).
  - Not decided (scopes only, as before): the SASS front (an instruction's width is not the
    PTX element size: ptxas merges a vector's elements into one access, `ld.relaxed.v2.u32` is
    one 64-bit `LDG.E.64.STRONG`), accesses of asynchronous units (bulk and TMA reductions,
    `st.async`), and instructions without a known element size. The NIC's accesses are decided
    since 2026-11-12 (below). A synchronization source is still keyed by its first byte: a read
    that starts at another byte of the write does not observe it (no synchronization: races
    only added).
  - The NIC (MISS 194, 2026-11-12). At the strict PTX level an access of the NIC is one location
    of its element's size on the byte compared (`overlap_with_nic`, `NicState::elem`): a NIC
    atomic's aligned 8-byte word (S-NIC-ATOMIC), a lone flag write (S-NIC-FLAG), the naturally
    aligned 8- or 4-byte chunk of RDMA write data that holds the byte (S-NIC-WORD; its plain
    edge bytes are not strong), and a CQE field, bytes 56-59, 60-61, 62 or 63 of the CQE
    (S-NIC-CQE; two CQE writes of one CQE are one location). A thread's strong access of
    another element size, or a NIC access of another size, overlaps it partially: a mixed-size
    data race when unordered, no observation (8.9.2), and no continuation of a release
    sequence (`nic_publish`: a NIC atomic reading a 4-byte release write). A thread's access
    that spans or splits a CQE field, or covers a CQE byte outside them, counts as one location
    and is reported `unmodeled` (`nic-overlap`) when its scopes make the pair morally strong:
    the NIC writes the 64 bytes at once, and the fields are the model's (the bytes it publishes
    as synchronization sources). Until 2026-11-12 every pair with the NIC was one location
    (`same_location` holds for an actor that is not a thread). fixtures/e_nic_cta (one GPU, a
    loopback QP; PTX front, model): PART and PART_OTHERCTA (a 4-byte `ld.acquire.sys` poll of
    the fetch-add's 8-byte word) were clean and race; PART_SRC (PART, then a read of what the
    doorbell thread stored before its release fence) was clean and races on that read, since
    the poll does not acquire the release the fetch-add carries; FLAGHALF (the same with a lone
    8-byte flag write polled 4 bytes at its first byte, the shape of DeepEP's notify) was clean
    and races; WORDPART (a 4-byte poll of an 8-byte chunk) was clean and races; CQEPART (a
    4-byte read of bytes 60-63 of a CQE) was clean and is `unmodeled`. WORDFULL, WORD4 and
    FLAGFULL (polls at the element's own width) stay clean, and CQECTA (CQEPART at `.cta`
    scope, which races either way) stays a race with no `unmodeled` report.
    fixtures/e_nic_rseq SYSREL_PART (the head write a 4-byte `st.release.sys` of the signal
    word) stays a race and `unmodeled` (the head write and the receiver's 8-byte poll are a
    mixed-size race between threads either way), and d2 races now: the fetch-add no longer
    continues the head write's sequence (the two writes are a mixed-size race too). The SASS
    front and the GB300 profile re-run are unchanged (`overlap_with_nic` decides the strict PTX
    level only; the GB300 profile re-runs of the new races are clean). A mixed-size race with
    the NIC stays `race` whatever its racing loads' values reach (E-RACE-DEAD, MISS 226: PTX ISA
    9.5 section 8.7.2, the memory model's axioms do not apply to a program with one); until
    2026-11-12 one whose values reached nothing was `race-dead` and clean (fixtures/e_nic_cta
    WORDDEAD, a WORDPART read masked to 0). Repro: probes/nic_overlap (`bash
    probes/nic_overlap/run.sh`). A/B (model; the fix against int7 7aa66d42, `--certify`, 2000
    states, 1200 s): the 44 kernel_db NIC records keep their verdicts and findings (kind and
    signature) on their front; 19 have a verdict in both arms (2 complete, 17 at the bound,
    each with one deterministic run to the end), 25 time out in both, and no run reports a
    partial overlap with a NIC access. DeepEP's dispatch polls 4-byte halves of 8
    bytes (`ld.acquire.sys.u32` by two lanes, static) that this launch posts as one lone 8-byte
    RDMA write (WQE 5 of qp_r0_0 / qp_r1_0, rung at ptx 6721; the captured send queue also holds
    the previous launch's identical WQEs; record data, model): FLAGHALF's shape. The bounded runs
    did not reach it; a deterministic run of a diagnostic build (a deterministic-scheduler policy
    change only) does, on the record as captured, in cuda.k_hybrid_dispatch.w2, and reports the
    two read races the fix adds there (ptx 6966 and 7026) on a path whose verdict already carries
    race (model; no class change). Source mutants
    nic-overlap, nic-overlap-word4, nic-overlap-cqe, nic-overlap-scope, nic-overlap-rseq and
    scope-overlap-sync (PART_SRC, FLAGHALF). The state hash covers the element each NIC access

    ISA text applied to the NIC's accesses, whose element sizes are the model's (S-NIC-WORD's
    chunks, S-NIC-FLAG's write, S-NIC-CQE's fields), at the strict level of the PTX front; the
    SASS front and the GB300 profile do not decide overlap.
  - Fixtures e_scope_mixed (good, VEC clean; MIXED, WIDE race on PTX, clean on SASS),
    e_warp_order_mixed (good nondeterministic, MIXED race on PTX; both clean on SASS) and

    source mutants scope-overlap, scope-overlap-race, scope-overlap-sync, scope-elem-vector,
    scope-elem-mmst.
  - A/B (2026-11-11, model; the fix against its parent, PTX front, `--certify`): 65 kernel_db
    records whose PTX has strong accesses of two sizes, triaged at 2000 states, and the 39 that
    hit the bound rerun at 20000 states; 23 fixture checks. No record flips (46 unchanged, 11
    of them complete verdicts; 19 without a verdict in either arm), and no record's run
    compares two strong accesses of different sizes on one byte. The fixture flips are the
    three hazards above.
  - Placement: ISA text, so the strict level (`ptx_contract`) of the PTX front. The gb300
    profile (E-HW-L1, `Launch::hw_order`) keeps treating any two strong accesses as morally
    strong, partial overlaps included: whether GB300 synchronizes through a byte of a wider
    flag is not measured, and a hardware run cannot decide a contract question (the races
    are classified latent there). The SASS front's strict level does not decide overlap
    (above).
- A strong write is the location's synchronization source. It releases the writer's clock
  (release write), or the clock at its last release fence (relaxed write after
  `fence.acq_rel`/`MEMBAR`, at the narrower of the two scopes). A read-modify-write continues
  the release sequence; a plain write ends it. A release store ticks its thread's clock after
  publishing it (2026-11-04), as fences and atomics already did: before, a plain write after
  `st.release` in the same clock window looked ordered before every reader that acquired
  the release, so a payload written after its flag was published was reported clean (PTX
  front-end; SASS `st.release` is `MEMBAR` + a relaxed store; fixture e_ring R1). Across the
  65 other PTX fixtures, no verdict changes; explored states grow by up to 2.7x
  (r1g_allreduce good: 119,899 to 326,045 states, clean either way).
- Release sequences through read-modify-writes (MISS 100, 2026-11-11): a read-modify-write
  continues the release sequence of the write it reads only when the two are morally strong
  (`sync_publish`: the same thread, or scopes that include each other's thread, and complete
  overlap). PTX ISA 9.5 section 8.9.2: "A write W precedes a read R in observation order if: R
  and W are morally strong and R reads the value written by W, or For some atomic operation Z,
  W precedes Z and Z precedes R in observation order". Until 2026-11-11 every read-modify-write
  continued it: a `.cta` release continued through a relaxed atomic of another CTA, and the
  thread that acquired the atomic's value synchronized with the release (fixtures/e_rseq_scope
  CTAREL: clean on both fronts, now a race; good, a `.gpu` release, stays clean). Under the
  hardware ordering every strong pair is morally strong (E-HW-L1), so the hardware model is
  unchanged; the GB300 profile re-run (`sass_gb300`) keeps the strict memory model and reports
  the race too. A/B (both fixes against their parent, 2026-11-11, model: every kernel_db
  record and fixture with a read-modify-write outside shared::cta memory and an
  acquire-capable access, 516 check pairs): the check refused a continuation in 4 records
  (cute ReduceScatterFusion w2 and w4, dg_cute_fused w2 and w4) and in fixtures/r1h_nvls B63,
  none of whose verdicts changed; CTAREL's are the only flips. Source mutant rseq-scope. A NIC
  atomic continues a sequence by the same rule since 2026-11-12 (S-NIC-ATOMIC).
  Placement: ISA text, the strict level of both fronts (the SASS front takes the release scope
  from `MEMBAR`).
- The first operations of a continued release sequence (MISS 112, 2026-11-11): the release
  patterns a read-modify-write continues stay apart from its own (`SyncCell::cont`, merged per
  thread and scope), and a read synchronizes with each only when the pattern's first operation
  and the read's acquire are morally strong (`sync_observe_cell`, `acquire_pending`): the
  release's scope includes the reader, and the scope of the acquiring read, or of the acquire
  fence after a relaxed read, includes the thread that made the release. PTX ISA 9.5 section
  8.9.4: "A release pattern X synchronizes with an acquire pattern Y, if a write operation in X
  precedes a read operation in Y in observation order, and the first operation in X and the
  last operation in Y are morally strong". Until 2026-11-11 a continued release took the
  read-modify-write's thread and scopes: a `.cta` fence heading the pattern (fixtures/e_rseq_head
  FREL) was clean on both fronts, and a `.cta` acquire fence after the poll (e_rseq_facq
  CTAFENCE) or a `.cta` acquire read of the atomic's value (CTAACQ, whose flag read races in any
  case) synchronized on the PTX front; their data reads race now. The `.gpu` variants stay
  clean. When one pattern fails and another passes, the read synchronizes with the passing one
  only (TWOHEAD: the `.cta` fence's pattern and a `.gpu` release atomic's; OWN: the reader's own
  atomic continued the pattern; e_rseq_twopat CTAFENCE: a `.cta` acquire fence after a relaxed
  poll takes the pattern of its CTA only); the patterns' join (`SyncCell::cont_join`) stands
  for them only when every one passes, and the SASS front's single pending entry for them
  (`CCTL.IVALL` takes every entry) is not used on the PTX front. Under the hardware ordering
  every release is at system scope and they join into one clock (E-HW-L1), so the hardware model
  is unchanged; the GB300 profile re-run (`sass_gb300`) keeps the strict memory model and
  reports the races too. A/B (the 516 check pairs of MISS 100's, model): no verdict changed
  outside the fixtures above, whose CTAACQ and REL_CTA also gain the data read's race. On the
  261 checks that continued a release sequence the cached join and per-pattern joins give the
  same classes, levels and findings on 231 and differ on none (2 have a verdict with the cached
  join only, 28 with neither). One node, interleaved, the slowest records: wall time 1.02 to
  1.27 times the parent's (per-pattern joins: up to 4.56), peak RSS 0.99 to 1.08 times. Source
  mutants rseq-head-rel, rseq-head-acq, rseq-head-fence, rseq-head-join, rseq-head-cache,
  rseq-head-own and rseq-head-shortcut. Placement: ISA text, the strict level of both fronts; on
  the SASS front an acquire fence is `CCTL.IVALL`, unscoped (none for `.cta`), so only the
  release side is decided there.
- A morally strong read whose thread the release's scope includes acquires it at once
  (acquire read) or at its next acquire fence (relaxed read; `fence.acq_rel.<scope>` acquires
  observations whose writer its scope includes, and SASS `CCTL.IVALL` acquires all of them).
- `membar.cta` / `.gl` / `.sys` are `fence.sc.cta` / `.gpu` / `.sys` (PTX ISA; ptxas emits the
  same `MEMBAR.SC.<scope>` [+ `ERRBAR` + `CCTL.IVALL`]) and are modeled as `fence.sc` is (as
  `fence.acq_rel` at that scope: no total SC order beyond the interleaving, which is weaker
  than PTX, not stronger). `fence.acquire.cta` / `.cluster` / `.gpu` acquire only
  observations whose writer the scope includes (`.sys`: all); ptxas emits nothing for `.cta`
  and `CCTL.IVALL` for `.cluster` / `.gpu`, so the SASS front is exact for the code (an
  all-scope acquire after `.cluster` / `.gpu`, none after `.cta`: LDG.STRONG.SM is read as
  relaxed, so a CTA-scope acquire pattern is reported there, weaker than the hardware).
  probes/fence_scopes (2026-11-07): cross-CTA and in-CTA message passing; acquire narrowed to
  `.cta` / `.cluster` or release to `membar.cta` across CTAs is reported on the PTX front;
  GB300 50/50 on the good variant.
- `red.global.add.v2` / `.v4.f32` (SASS `REDG.E.ADD.F32x2` / `F32x4.FTZ.RN`) is one FADD.FTZ
  atomic per element, each on its own (the PTX ISA gives no atomicity across elements;
  2026-11-07, probes/red_vec = GB300 on both front-ends). `atom.global.add.v2` / `.v4.f32`
  (SASS `ATOMG.E.ADD.F32x2` / `F32x4.FTZ.RN`; Triton's `atom.global.gpu.acq_rel.add.v2.f32`)
  is the same per element and returns each element's old value; a destination overlapping a
  later source element is refused (2026-11-07, probes/atom_vec: specials and subnormals in
  addends and starting values, GB300 20/20, both front-ends bitwise).
- SASS: `ATOMG` / `REDG .E.<op>.STRONG.SM` (PTX `atom` / `red.global.cta`) are CTA-scope
  atomics (2026-11-07; probes/generic8 = GB300 on both front-ends, with generic `LD.E.U8` /
  `.S8` and `ST.E.U8`).
- SASS: `LDG/STG.E.STRONG.<SYS|GPU|SM>` are relaxed strong accesses; `MEMBAR.*.<scope>` is a
  release fence; `CCTL.IVALL` is an acquire fence (ptxas: `ld.acquire` = `LDG.STRONG` +
  `CCTL.IVALL`, `st.release` = `MEMBAR` + `STG.STRONG`, `fence.acq_rel` = `MEMBAR` +
  `CCTL.IVALL`).
- `fence.sc` is treated as `fence.acq_rel`, plus the Fence-SC edges every execution has at
  gpu / sys scope (S-FENCE-SC, since 2026-11-12). mbarrier `.release.cta/.cluster` and
  `try_wait.acquire.cluster` scopes are still treated as sufficient.
- Scope defaults never strengthen the model (2026-11-06 audit). A PTX `fence.sc` /
  `fence.acq_rel` without a scope, and a SASS `MEMBAR` without one, are refused (before: `.sys`,
  the strongest). A SASS atomic or `.STRONG` access without a scope token takes `.cta`, the
  weakest (before: `.gpu`); ptxas prints a token on every global and generic form in the
  corpus, and the only token-less forms are `ATOMS.*` (shared memory, CTA scope anyway) and
  `ATOM.E.CAST.SPIN` (the shared-memory leg of a generic atomic). Weaker readings that remain:
  `MEMBAR.SC` and `fence.sc` act as `MEMBAR.ALL` / `fence.acq_rel` plus only the forced part
  of the Fence-SC order (S-FENCE-SC), and
  `atom` / `red` without a scope are `.gpu`, the PTX ISA default.
- Where: `exec.rs` `morally_strong`, `scope_includes`, `sync_publish`, `sync_observe`,
  `acquire_pending`, `same_location`, `overlap_with_nic`, `elem_bytes`, `SyncCell::cont`;
  `nic.rs` `NicState::elem`, `nic_publish`; `ptx` `mem_sync`; `sass` `sass_strong`,
  `sass_scope`.
- Status: **validated** for `.gpu` vs `.sys` across two GPUs (`fixtures/r1f_pingpong`): B20
  (relaxed poll, no acquire) is a race in both models and **wrong 1000/1000 on GB300** (a stale
  L1 hit on the payload); B19 (release at `.gpu`) is a race in both models and latent on GB300
  (20,000 runs). B56 (`fence.acq_rel.gpu` as the acquire) is a race in PTX and clean in SASS:
  only the release half of the fence is scoped.
- If wrong: *miss* of mbarrier scope bugs (a remote arrive with `.release.cta`). *Miss* for
  SASS-derived contracts (records checked on the SASS front only): the SASS front does not
  decide overlap, so a mixed-size race between strong accesses is not reported there, and its
  acquire fence `CCTL.IVALL` has no scope, so a `.gpu` acquire fence of another GPU's release
  synchronizes there (B56 above). *Miss* of a mixed-size race with an access of an
  asynchronous unit (bulk and TMA reductions, `st.async`) on either front, and with the NIC's
  accesses on the SASS front and in the GB300 profile: overlap is not decided for them, so a
  partial overlap counts as one location there (no race, and a partial read observes the
  write). The NIC's element sizes are the model's (S-NIC-WORD's chunks, S-NIC-CQE's fields):
  an RDMA write that lands as other units than the chunks moves its races (*miss* or *false
  alarm*); a CQE access the fields do not decide is `unmodeled`, not a verdict.
- Retire: scopes on mbarrier operations.

### S-FENCE-SC · code
**The model orders two SC fences when every Fence-SC order of the execution does.** PTX ISA 9.5:
"The Fence-SC order is an acyclic partial order, determined at runtime, that relates every pair
of morally strong fence.sc operations" (8.9.3); "A fence.sc operation X synchronizes with a
fence.sc operation Y if X precedes Y in the Fence-SC order" (8.9.4); Fence-SC axiom (8.10.2):
"For a pair of morally strong fence.sc operations F1 and F2, if F1 precedes F2 in causality
order, then F1 must precede F2 in Fence-SC order"; Coherence axiom (8.10.1): "If a write W
