precedes an overlapping write W' in causality order, then W must precede W' in coherence
order." Moral strength (8.7): same thread, or "each operation is strong and specifies a scope
that includes the thread executing the other operation", same proxy, and memory operations
overlap completely; a memory fence is a strong operation (8.4).
- Rule. SC fences F1 and F2 at gpu / sys scope, morally strong (both `.sys`, or on the same
  GPU), F1 before F2 when: F1 happens before a global atomic A whose result is used (`atom`
  with a destination; SASS `ATOMG` with one other than `RZ`), and such an atomic B morally
  strong with A, after A in coherence order (the order the model performs them in), happens
  before F2. Then F2 acquires the clock at F1 (F1 synchronizes with F2). Proof: in
  any execution with that coherence order, the Fence-SC order relates F1 and F2; if F2 came
  first, F2 synchronizes with F1 and B precedes F2 precedes F1 precedes A in causality order,
  so the Coherence axiom puts B before A in coherence order, a contradiction.
- Only these forced edges are added; a Fence-SC edge some executions have and others lack is
  not (an under-approximation of happens-before: at most a false race, never a missed one). An
  edge is forced only for a coherence order the tool branches on, so the rule reads only pairs
  whose order is one: A and B by threads of different warps (DPOR and the stateful explorer
  branch on the order of dependent writes; the certificate fixes it with C-ORDER, and C-TICKET
  runs each claim order with its own happens-before), or A known to B. Excluded, since one
  order stands for all there (forum post 74 review, rounds 1 and 2):
  - A by a lane of B's warp that B does not know of, at any instruction: the lanes of one
    converged PTX step run in lane order only (MISS 140), and lanes of a converged warp at
    different instructions in step order only (E-WARP-ORDER); a lane-step write also orders a
    later write of another lane. fixtures/e_fence_sc_lanes good, INDIRECT (lane 1's later atom
    at another pc) and PCS (the two claims at consecutive instructions; it was certified clean)
    race on PTX; they were clean when the exclusion keyed on one instruction. Lanes of a
    diverged warp are explored in both orders, so leaving them out costs precision only. On
    SASS E-LOCKSTEP orders the lanes of a converged warp, so their writes are known.
  - Claims on a declared C-TICKET-ADDR counter in the certificate's runs and reruns, which fix
    one claim order and stand for every order (wellsync/perm.rs: a claim creates no edge;
    fixtures/e_ticket_addr_fence SC certified as clean up to permutation on PTX).

  With those exclusions there is no new schedule choice and no new state branching, and the
  certificate's monotonicity holds (more happens-before gives more edges). The log is part of
  the state. Fences are kept by (thread, clock), so the order unrelated fences ran in does not
  split states. Only atomics whose result is used are logged: that is a state-count
  restriction, and soundness does not depend on it (any morally strong pair forces the order;
  dropping a pair only drops edges). Logging every read-modify-write split the states of
  commuting signal atomics: the 4-rank reduce-scatter sm_rs_w4 went from 321,836 states to over
  2,000,000; with the restriction it has 321,836 again.
- Equal widths. A and B must have the same access width per element (`exec.rs` `atom_width`,
  `elem_bytes`: a vector atomic is one operation per element, 8.2.4). On PTX
  `same_location` already requires complete overlap; on SASS it holds for any two accesses at
  one address (the instruction width is not the PTX element size), and a 64-bit and a 32-bit
  atomic are not morally strong (8.7; fixtures/e_fence_sc_mixed good was clean on SASS).
- Not covered (no edge, possibly a false race): plain strong stores, reductions and atomics
  with unused results as A or B; B a read that reads from A (the Causality axiom, 8.10.6, would
  force the same order); pairs of lanes of one PTX step (above, also a last arriver chosen by
  its ticket among them); fences at CTA or cluster scope; `.sys` fences on different GPUs; more
  than 2^14 fences or 2^12 writes in one execution; and the GB300 profile's hardware order
  (`Launch::hw_order`, which orders these writes by itself).
- Which fences (`exec.rs` `sc_fence_scope`): PTX `fence.sc.gpu` / `.sys` and `membar.gl` /
  `.sys` ("On sm_70 and higher membar is a synonym for fence.sc", 9.7.15.4); SASS
  `MEMBAR.SC.GPU` / `.SYS`. ptxas 13.0 (sm_103a) lowers `fence.sc.gpu` and `membar.gl` to
  `MEMBAR.SC.GPU; ERRBAR; CGAERRBAR; CCTL.IVALL`, `fence.sc.sys` to `MEMBAR.SC.SYS; ...`,
  `fence.sc.cluster` to `MEMBAR.SC.GPU; ...`, `fence.sc.cta` to `MEMBAR.SC.CTA`, and
  `fence.acq_rel.gpu` / `fence.release.gpu` to `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU; ...`: `MEMBAR.SC` is what
  ptxas emits for `fence.sc` only (CUDA's `__threadfence()` is `membar.gl`). A SASS
  `MEMBAR.SC.GPU` from `fence.sc.cluster` gets the gpu-scope rule, as the instruction ptxas
  uses for `fence.sc.gpu`. The strict SASS level models `MEMBAR` as a release only and
  acquires at `CCTL.IVALL`, so a SASS `MEMBAR.SC` is an SC fence only when the lowering's
  `CCTL.IVALL` follows within three instructions under the same guard, with only `ERRBAR`
  and `CGAERRBAR` between (`sass_sc_acquires`; no memory access or branch in between, so
  acquiring at the MEMBAR equals acquiring at the CCTL). Without it there is no acquire at the
  strict level and no edge (fixtures/e_fence_sc_publish NOCCTL, the consumer's CCTL.IVALL NOPed:
  a race; it was clean).
- Where: `exec.rs` `sc_fence`, `sc_note_write` (from `sync_publish`), `sc_fence_scope`,
  `sass_sc_acquires`, `atom_width`, `has_sc_fence`; `machine.rs` `ScLog` (`Machine::sc`, part
  of the state hash).
- Status: **argued** (PTX ISA text above; ptxas lowering checked by compiling each form). On
  PTX it uses only the ISA text. On SASS the rule itself adds no GB300 behaviour, but the
  happens-before it reads ("F1 happens before A", "B happens before F2") is the SASS front's,
  which includes E-LOCKSTEP and E-WARP-ORDER edges (GB300-validated, not PTX): a SASS edge is
  as good as those.
- Evidence: fixtures/e_fence_sc_publish, ATen reduce_kernel's global_reduce publication
  (forum post 74, MISS 126): every thread stores a partial, `membar.gl`, `bar.sync`, thread 0's
  relaxed `atom.add` on a semaphore; the last CTA's threads `membar.gl` again and load every
  partial. good is clean on both fronts and certifies (before: a race, the producers' partials
  of threads other than thread 0 reach the last CTA only through the Fence-SC order); NOCFENCE
  (the consumer's fence removed: the code before pytorch#128455), NOPFENCE, ACQREL (both
  fences `fence.acq_rel.gpu`) and CTASCOPE (the semaphore atomics at CTA scope, so not morally
  strong across CTAs; the test checks the partials race, not only the semaphore) race on both
  fronts. Forum post 74 review: e_fence_sc_lanes (good, INDIRECT, PCS: a race on PTX, the
  READER0 controls clean; while MISS 220 is open the E-WARP-ORDER strong-pair report also flags
  INDIRECT's and PCS's two dead-result adds, nondeterministic on PTX, a false alarm for the
  READER0 controls),
  e_fence_sc_unforced (SC fences without atomics: a race on PTX), e_fence_sc_mixed (good: a
  race on both fronts, SAME32 clean), e_fence_sc_publish NOCCTL / ACQREL_NOCCTL,
  e_ticket_addr_fence SC / SC_SWAP (the certificate refuses). Source mutants, all caught:
  `sc-any-write` (writes that are not morally strong force the order; the CTASCOPE partials
  check), `sc-drop-forcing` (fences ordered as executed: e_fence_sc_unforced), `sc-lane-step`,
  `sc-lane-pc` (the exclusion keyed on one instruction: INDIRECT, PCS),
  `sc-ticket-addr`, `sc-membar-acq`, `sc-width`.
- If wrong: *miss* (an edge the hardware does not give hides a race). The edges follow from the
  ISA text by the proof above.
- Retire: never (PTX semantics); extend to reads (8.10.6) and narrower scopes if needed.

### S-RED-ASYNC · code
**`red.async.release.{gpu,sys}.global.add` is a red of that semantics and scope
that has completed before the issuing thread's next instruction. SASS
`UREDGR.E.ADD.NA.STRONG.GPU|SYS` releases the issuing thread's earlier accesses at its
scope.**
- ptxas 13.0's lowering is a per-lane ELECT loop: `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; UREDGR [UR], UR; DEPBAR.LE
  SB, 0`. DEPBAR waits for the reduction, hence "completed". On its own, MEMBAR.ALL.CTA does
  not order global stores before a gpu-scope flag (control below), so the release rests on
  UREDGR.
- Where: `ptx` atom / red arm (`async`), `sass` `UREDGR` (executed once per warp, by its first
  active thread, which releases only that thread's clock; ptxas's loop runs one elected lane
  per iteration).
- Refused: other operations (`.min` / `.max` / `.or` / `.and` / `.xor` / `.inc` / `.dec`).
  ptxas 13.0 and 13.1 compile them to `UREDGR.E.ADD`, and GB300 adds: `100 min.s32 6` = 106.
  Also refused: other types, other spaces, `atom.async`, and UREDGR with other modifiers.
- Refused as well (2026-11-09): `.relaxed` on `.global`. The PTX ISA (9.5, red.async) defines
  the `.global` form as `red.async{.mmio}.release.{gpu,sys}{.global}.add.{u32,s32,u64,s64}`
  only; `.relaxed` needs `.cluster` scope, `.shared::cluster` and an mbarrier, and `.mmio`
  needs `.sys` (not modeled). ptxas 13.1 / 13.2 accept `.relaxed` and the other operations on
  `.global` without a diagnostic and emit the release's `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` + `UREDGR.E.ADD`, so
  the SASS front runs them as the release add; probes/red_async_ops (GB200, sm_100a, ptxas
  13.1): `.min.s32` 10 with 3 gives 13, `.inc.u32` 7 with 5 gives 12, `.or.b32` 0x11 with 0x10
  gives 0x21, i.e. every op added; GB300 (sm_103a build, probes/gb300_runs.toml) gives the
  same output bit for bit. A PTX kernel with one of these forms is refused, so a
  wrong-result bug behind them is reported as a lift gap, not missed.
- Status: **probed** (hardware evidence, probes/redasync_litmus, 2026-11-08). The test is message
  passing between CTAs on different SMs: weak payload stores, the form on a flag,
  `ld.acquire.gpu` polls, then weak reads. In the three configurations in which controls were
  stale, `red.async.release.gpu` gave 0 stale reads in 1,689,600,000. MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + REDG
  gave 21,730,362 stale reads; `red.relaxed.gpu` gave 461,790 in 153,600,000. Totals:
  2.72e9 reads under the async form, 0 stale. probes/red_async: GB300 50/50 scrubbed, both
  front-ends bitwise; its `relaxed` variant is refused on the PTX front (not an ISA form) and
  clean on the SASS front (ptxas emits the release).

### S-SMEM-STRONG · code
**SASS `LDS`/`STS` of the CTA's own shared memory are relaxed strong accesses at CTA scope;
an `LDS` whose scoreboard is waited on before the warp issues any later non-ALU
instruction is `ld.acquire.cta`.** This is the hardware-faithful model of the binary. The PTX
front-end keeps the PTX model, where a weak shared access can race.
- **Root pairs** (2026-11-06): under this model an unsynchronized `STS` / `LDS` pair of two
  warps is not a race; its consequence (a nondeterministic output, a global race
  downstream) is what the verdict reports. When `check --certify` falls back to exploration
  and the verdict has a race or nondeterministic outputs, the certificate run's unordered
  shared-memory pairs (C-ORDER) are listed first as findings of kind `unordered` (sig
  `unordered-smem:<pc>:<pc>`, not a verdict class), so the place where a barrier is missing is
  named (mslk moe index_shuffling: `STS` 0x08f0 / `LDS` 0x0940 behind a global write-write
  race at `STG` 0x1280; GB300 delay replay wrong 1000/1000). They come from one run and are
  candidates: the verdict does not show that each one reaches the consequence.
- **Evidence:**
  - ptxas emits bit-identical `LDS`/`STS`/`ATOMS` for weak, `.volatile` and `.relaxed`
    shared accesses at every scope, and flipping encoding bits shows no strength or scope
    field (`docs/smem-order-mapping.md`). Strength only steers ptxas's optimizer (weak spins
    are deleted, weak loads merged).
  - `ld.acquire.cta.shared` is `LDS` plus a wait on its scoreboard; `st.release.cta` is
    `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` + `STS`.
  - About 3.1e12 one-CTA litmus instances on GB300 (MP, SB, LB, CoRR, CoWR, IRIW, tearing
    at 32/64/128 bits, the merged `STS.64 {flag,data}`) showed no non-SC outcome, while the
    allowed outcomes appeared billions of times and a global-memory control did show stale
    reads (`docs/smem-litmus.md`, `probes/smem_litmus`).
  - An aligned `.64`/`.128` access is one access.
  - The acquire reading (2026-11-10): `fixtures/s_smem_acquire`, message passing in one CTA
    through a shared flag (`st.release.cta.shared`, i.e. `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` + `STS`) that guards
    global data. `good` (`ld.acquire.cta.shared` spin) is clean on both fronts; `RELAX`
    (`ld.relaxed.cta.shared` spin, the same `LDS` + wait from ptxas) races on PTX and is clean
    on SASS; `NOREL` (no release) races on both. GB300 50/50 scrubbed: `good` and `RELAX`
    correct, `NOREL` wrong in 50/50 (3 of 4 words stale). Without the acquire reading the SASS
    front reports `good` and `RELAX` as races (source mutant `smem-noacq`).
- **Cost:** strong accesses are scheduling points. A verdict is therefore computed in two
  passes (`smem.rs`):
  - first with `LDS`/`STS` plain. Without a race that is also the strong model's verdict:
    strong accesses only add happens-before, and race-free plain accesses commute (E-DRF);
  - with a race, the strong kernel decides.

  So a missing `bar.sync` between warps shows up on SASS as `nondeterministic` output, not
  as `race` (or not at all if the values agree). The same holds for an `LDS`/`STS` against an
  `ATOMS` (shared atomics are strong; fixtures/e_lds_atoms). Strong reads are recorded as reads for POR
  (they commute).
- Where: `sass` `SMEM_RELAXED`, `smem_acquires`; `sim` `smem.rs`; `exec.rs` `access_x`.
- Status: **validated** (litmus, above); zero observations is not a proof.
- If wrong: *miss* of reorderings of shared accesses within a CTA that the hardware does
  perform.

### S-CLUSTER-LIFE · code
**A CTA's shared memory exists only while one of its threads runs.** An access to another
CTA's shared memory (remote mbarrier arrive, multicast TMA delivery, `tcgen05.commit` to a
peer, `shared::cluster` load/store) after the whole target exited is a violation, and the
access is dropped. Independently of the schedule explored, every remote arrive / TMA issue /
commit into CTA X must happen-before the exit of *some* thread of X (checked at terminal
states, like async-after-exit), since otherwise a schedule exists in which X exits first. A
thread of X that observed the mbarrier phase the operation completed into (a successful wait)
counts too, though the wait need not synchronize with it (`Thread::landed`: a real-time
observation order, argued at S-MBAR-SCOPE `Cover::Order`). The same holds for
async-after-exit.
- Where: `exec.rs` `check_alive`, `dead_target`, `note_remote`, `exit_checks`.
- Status: **argued** (PTX ISA: a CTA's shared memory must not be accessed after it exits;
  CUTLASS ends cluster kernels with a cluster barrier for this reason). A multicast delivery
  is checked by its issue, not its landing: if the target syncs with the issuer after the
  issue but never observes the landing, a late landing is missed. Remote `ld/st.shared::cluster`
  get only the immediate check, not the terminal one.
- If wrong: *false alarm* if hardware keeps the memory alive until the whole cluster exits.
- GB300 (`probes/remote_arrive_exit` rae.cu / window.cu, 2026-11-07): it does not. A remote
  mbarrier arrive or `st.shared::cluster` that reaches an exited peer fails the launch
  (`cudaErrorLaunchFailure`). Successor CTAs already resident on the exited CTA's SM were
  never written. A violation of this rule is therefore a crash on GB300, not a silent
  corruption.
- A thread's own access to another CTA's shared memory (ld / st / atom / red through
  shared::cluster) is checked at the end of the run like remote arrivals, multicast TMA and
  commits (`note_remote` from `access_x`; one entry per target CTA and thread, its latest
  access). Before 2026-11-09 only the exit-time check saw them, in schedules where the
  target exited first, so the certificate's run certified a missing final barrier.cluster
  (fixtures/e_cluster_life NOFINAL).

### S-REMOTE-INFLIGHT · code
**A remote mbarrier arrival (`mbarrier.arrive[.expect_tx] .shared::cluster` to another CTA,
SASS `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED`) and an `st.async` into another CTA (with its complete_tx) are
in flight from issue until delivered.** Deliveries are separate steps the explorer schedules
at any time, in any order among the issuer's remote operations (also to different
mbarriers), except that a release of the issuer at cluster scope or wider delivers all of
them first: `barrier.cluster.arrive` (not `.relaxed`), `fence.acq_rel` / `fence.sc` at cluster
/ gpu / sys scope, `mbarrier.arrive.release.cluster`; SASS: `CGAERRBAR`, which ptxas emits
after `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` for each of those (until 2026-11-09, `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` / `.SYS`
itself). `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` alone (`fence.proxy.async[.shared::cluster]` lowers to
`MEMBAR.ALL.GPU; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`) drains nothing: a stale read of a weak remote store
followed by `fence.proxy.async.shared::cluster` and a remote arrive was measured on GB200
(reported by others; SASS `ST.E; MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; MEMBAR.ALL.GPU; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S;
SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0`). A `CGAERRBAR` right after `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` (and `ERRBAR`)
extends that fence's release to the drain point. SASS weak stores into another CTA's shared
memory (`ST.E` to a shared::cluster address, 4-byte aligned, at least 4 bytes, not
multicast) are in flight too, as their own async actor whose clock the issuer gets only at
the drain, so the race with a reader is found whatever lands first. So does an in-flight
`st.async`: its write carries its own async actor, not the issuer's clock, and the release
its mbarrier phase publishes carries that actor's epoch (until 2026-11-12 it wrote under the
issuer's clock, so the issuer's later releases covered it before it landed: the
certificate's one schedule saw no race, MISS 184, `fixtures/e_dpor_nonhead` good). Such a
store (st.async or `ST.E`) is ordered before its own thread's next drain, whether it lands in
that drain or before it (as its own step, or in an earlier operation of its warp's pipe that
another lane's drain lands first): its actor joins the thread there (`Thread::remote_landed`, recorded at the landing),
so the verdict does not depend on whether the store was still in flight at the release.
Until 2026-11-12 only a store landed by the drain itself was joined: with a step break
between the st.async and its issuer's release, DPOR and the stateful explorer without local
reduction reported a race that the local reduction and the certificate did not
(`fixtures/e_stasync_early_land` FENLD). Another thread's release does not drain it, a lane
of the same warp instruction included (below), but the per-warp pipe order can still land it
before that release (MISS 249, under Order). PTX
`st.shared::cluster` still lands at issue (its ordering is decided by S-MBAR-SCOPE). A
thread reading back its own in-flight remote store is not modeled (a false race).
`.release.cta` and `.relaxed` arrivals deliver nothing. The issuer's exit delivers nothing
either. Arrivals and st.async to the issuer's own CTA land at issue, as before.
- Violations (S-CLUSTER-LIFE): the target CTA's last thread exits while one is in flight to
  it; a delivery after the target exited; at the end, a delivery the target never waited for
  (no successful wait on the phase it counted toward or a later one) unless a later cluster
  release of the issuer (which would have drained it) happens-before a target thread's exit.
  The last one decides it order-independently, so the certificate (E-WELLSYNC) refuses such
  a run. Either cover suffices (`Machine::remote_drained`). Until 2026-11-12 the issuer's
  later release replaced the wait as the only cover: CTAs that st.async-store into each other,
  each wait for the packet they receive, then run `fence.acq_rel.gpu` were a cluster-lifetime
  violation per packet on both fronts (fixture e_stasync_drain, internal tree).
- A wait covers deliveries into the mbarrier object it waited on only: an inval or an init
  at the address (`mbarrier.inval` / `SYNCS.CCTL.IV`, `mbarrier.init` / `SYNCS.EXCH.64`)
  restarts the phase numbering, discharges the deliveries the old waits covered and forgets
  those waits (`mbar_reset_seen`). Until 2026-11-12 a wait on the old object's phase k
  covered a delivery into the new object's phase k, and `--certify` called it clean on both
  fronts where exhaustive exploration found the violation (MISS 203;
  fixtures/e_mbar_reinit_drain, probes/mbar_reinit). On SASS an `STS.64` of a state word
  over a live object re-initializes it the same way (S-MBAR-MEM; since 2026-11-12, MISS 218).
- Why: a FusedRMSNormBwd bug: the pre-fix epilogue waited only on the last stage's
  empty barrier; the peer's `.release.cta` arrive on the other stage's barrier, issued earlier,
  could still land after the exit. With arrivals landing at issue, program order made it
  look ordered (the reporters' case was clean on both fronts). Now: fixtures/e_rmsnorm_cluster_drain
  `bug`/`bug_k3` are violations, `good`/`good_k3` clean, on both fronts.
- SASS evidence for the drain: ptxas emits `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU; ERRBAR; CGAERRBAR` before a
  `.release.cluster` arrive and before `barrier.cluster.arrive`, and nothing before a
  `.release.cta` arrive (sm_103a, ptxas 13.0); `CGAERRBAR` presumably waits for the CTA's
  outstanding cluster (CGA) operations.
- One pending operation per warp instruction and target mbarrier: the lanes of one
  instruction that arrive on (or st.async into) the same mbarrier land together, in lane
  order (`push_remote`), but each lane keeps its own part (`RemoteLane`: its words under its
  own async actor, its clock at issue, its transaction bytes and arrivals, what it releases).
  A lane's drain lands only its own part: the operation's other parts stay in flight in its
  place (same pipe position, under their first lane; `split_remote_lane`), so another lane's
  drain does not land them, and each part landed outside its lane's drain carries that lane's
  own S-CLUSTER-LIFE obligation (`remote_obs`; per lane, which no verdict distinguishes from
  the first lane's alone: srcmut EXCLUDED remote-obs-first-lane). Known misses (both older
  than the split):
  - The parts left together still land as one step, their transaction bytes and arrivals in
    one mbarrier update and their releases joined into the phase it lands in; and the only
    other splits are drains, which a converged `barrier.cluster.arrive` runs in lane order. So
    a phase that other lanes' parts could complete without the first lane's is never explored
    (MISS 248: lanes 0..2 arrive `.release.cluster` in one instruction on a count-2 mbarrier,
    the reader reads lane 0's word after phase 0: PTX races, the model reports clean; the same
    with transaction bytes). The mbarrier phase orders the parts, so landing together hides
    more than outcomes behind a race on them.
  - A lane's drain lands its own later operation on the same mbarrier only behind the other
    lanes' remainder ahead of it in the warp's pipe (Order), so that remainder lands before
    the release (MISS 249).
  On SASS this
  does not assume `CGAERRBAR` waits for the other lanes' operations (warp-wide or per lane is
  not measured). `fixtures/e_stasync_coalesce` C0 (lane 0 alone releases, the reader reads
  lane 1's word: a race, the word possibly unwritten), C1 (lane 1 releases, reads its own:
  ordered); `fixtures/e_stasync_lanes` (test_wait of the st.async's mbarrier and the other
  lane's word after one lane's release: either outcome; D0XB: lane 1's word can outlive the
  target although lane 1's issue is ordered before its exit). Until 2026-11-12: the operation
  carried the first lane's actor for every word, so the first lane's drain ordered the other
  lanes' words (C0 [contract], a wrong-clean, once landings before the drain were joined too)
  and another lane's drain ordered none (C1, a false race); and a lane's drain landed the whole
  operation before its release (MISS 227 for the first lane, drained, since the coalescing; for
  another lane briefly with the per-lane actors), so the other lanes' words and bytes were never
  in flight after it (`fixtures/e_stasync_lanes` D0 / D1 clean, D0XB PTX clean).
  Deliveries read the target's exit key (space 4, index 1), which the
  exit of its last thread writes, so deliveries to one CTA commute with each other; the
  TMA-completion reduction (`sync_ample`) takes them as candidates too.
- State space (stateful explorer): the reporters' 2-CTA case 6k -> 20k (PTX), 0.2k -> 0.6k
  (SASS); r1c_cluster PTX 3.7k -> 11k, SASS 1.1k -> 2.3k; r1c_2sm SASS 99k -> 358k (ptxas's
  peer `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED` for cta_group::2 TMA); c_smm_nvf4 SASS 991 -> 832.
- Where: `exec.rs` `Op::MbarArrive`, `Op::StAsync`, `complete_remote`, `drain_remote`,
  `Op::Exit`, `exit_checks`, `mbar_reset_seen`; `machine.rs` `AsyncKind::Remote`,
  `remote_obs`, `mbar_seen`.
  `PTXV_REMOTE_ATOMIC=1` lands them at issue (the old model).
- Status: **argued.** Not observed on hardware: a late arrival into an exited CTA leaves no
  visible trace on GB300 or GB200 (the reporters saw nothing even with no drain). The FIFO-free order
  among one issuer's remote arrivals is the conservative reading of the PTX memory model
  (`.release.cta` does not order them for another CTA).
- Order (2026-11-07): one warp's remote operations on one mbarrier land in issue order
  (`AsyncOp::fifo` = `remote_pipe(warp, cta, mbar)`). PTX: two arrivals by one thread on one
  mbarrier are program-ordered morally strong read-modify-writes of one location, so
  coherence order follows program order (PTX ISA memory model, Coherence axiom over base
  causality order). Operations on different mbarriers stay unordered (`.release.cta` orders
  nothing for another CTA). Ordered per warp, not per thread: two instructions of one warp
  with disjoint lane sets on one mbarrier are also kept in order, which the PTX model does
  not require (a *miss*, MISS 249: lanes 0 and 1 st.async in one instruction, lane 0 then
  st.asyncs again on the same mbarrier and releases; its drain lands lane 1's remainder,
  ahead in the pipe, before the release, so a reader's test_wait and read of lane 1's word
  never race; remote arrivals are normally issued by one elected lane).
  Remote operations in such an order are not TMA-completion reduction candidates.
  The order is the issue order of the explored schedule (`AsyncOp::seq`, the op's position in
  its pipe). Until 2026-11-12 the head was the pipe's op with the lowest (actor, clock), so
  with several lanes' ops in one pipe the lowest lane's landed first whatever the issue
  order: a false race when a later-issued op had to land first (MISS 154,
  `fixtures/e_remote_pipe_order` good; REV, the first-issued store on the other word, races).
  A drain lands each of its thread's ops behind the ops ahead of it in its pipe: another
  lane's op there lands first, as its own delivery would (not ordered before the release;
  MISS 184, `fixtures/e_remote_pipe_order` DRN). Until 2026-11-12 the drain took the
  thread's ops in pending order, ahead of another lane's earlier op. E-REMOTE-FIFO's delivery
  before a landing (`deliver_fifo_before`) does the same: a pending head of another lane, not
  ordered before the landing, lands first, not drained (`fixtures/e_remote_fifo_nonhead`;
  until 2026-11-12 it landed the ordered op behind it, against this order). So every op
  removed from a pipe is its head at that moment, and DPOR's backtrack of a pipe whose op
  behind the head was consumed (`dpor.rs` `Alt::nonhead`) no longer arises.
- DPOR and the issue order: issuing a new op into a remote pipe writes the pipe's issue key
  (`SPACE_REMOTE_PIPE` id 2, `push_remote`), so two splits' issues into one pipe are
  dependent and DPOR schedules both orders. The issue order matters outside a phase boundary
  too: a drain lands the pipe up to the last op carrying its thread's words, so whether another
  lane's op is still in flight at the release depends on which was issued first (MISS 222,
  `probes/dpor_pipe_issue_order` SWAP: lane 0 issues X and leaves, lane 1 issues Y and
  drains; only Y,X leaves X in flight). An issue commutes with the landing of an op already in
  its pipe (it enters behind it) and with a drain (which lands only the prefix up to the
  drainer's own ops), so the issue key is not the landing key (id 0). Until 2026-11-12 an
  issue recorded no footprint: this bullet first argued the order mattered only across a
  phase boundary (the over-arrival fallback), then listed it as a known DPOR gap; DPOR gave
  SWAP [clean] for the stateful [nondeterministic], hidden until then behind MISS 221 (the
  observable is a test_wait). SASS: ptxas if-converts that shape (the warp stays converged
  and issues in one order), so the probe is clean in every explorer there.
- If wrong: *false alarm* if hardware delivers one thread's remote arrivals in order across
  mbarriers, or keeps a CTA's shared memory until its inbound arrivals land; *miss* if a
  cluster-scope release does not wait for earlier remote arrivals.
- GB300 (`probes/remote_arrive_exit`, 2026-11-07): remote *stores* issued before a barrier
  and another warp's arrive can still be in flight when the target exits (the launch fails,
  every process). Remote *arrivals* were never seen out of happens-before issue order (0 of
  401,200 clusters, `order.cu`), which is the opt-in E-REMOTE-FIFO.
- Retire: an NVIDIA statement on remote-operation ordering.

### S-REMOTE-RESERVED · code
**A remote arrival on an mbarrier in the reserved shared-memory prefix (offset < 0x400) is
ptxas's or the driver's protocol, not the kernel's.** ptxas implements
`tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` with a handshake on the reserved mbarrier at 0x48: the peer
waits on its own 0x48 and arrives on the leader's (`SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ,
[R13+URZ], RZ` after `ATOMS.OR` into the allocator words). The last such arrival is never
waited for, so S-REMOTE-INFLIGHT's lifetime checks (`remote-unobserved`,
`remote-inflight-exit`, a delivery after the target exited) fire on every cta_group::2
kernel. For reserved-prefix mbarriers they are `contract` findings instead of violations.
- Where: `exec.rs` `remote_reserved` (exit_checks, `Op::Exit`, `complete_remote`).
- Status: **argued** (2026-11-07). Evidence: msl_ops FlashAttentionForwardSm100 2-CTA
  (cases-MN `cute.FlashAttentionForwardSm100.bf16.1x384x1x128`): the third of MN's three
  S-REMOTE-INFLIGHT violations, sass 0x2330, is this handshake; GB300 runs of cta_group::2
  kernels show no effect. Whether a late handshake arrival can disturb the next CTA on the SM
  (which reuses the reserved prefix) is not probed.
- If wrong: *miss* of a ptxas / driver protocol bug.
- Retire: a GB300 probe that observes a late remote arrival (e.g. into a CTA that a
  co-resident successor reuses).

### S-NIC-DB · code
**The doorbell of an IBGDA queue pair is a strong system-scope store (`st.mmio.relaxed.sys`,
SASS `STG.E.64.MMIO.SYS`, or `st.relaxed.sys`) to the QP's doorbell register; the WQE and
payload stores the NIC reads for the WQEs it announces must happen-before it through a release
of GPU scope or wider** (`fence.release.gpu` / `.sys`, `fence.acq_rel` / `fence.sc` at those
scopes, SASS `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` / `.SYS`, or a release store).
- Model (nic.rs `nic_store`): a store to a declared doorbell announces WQEs up to the 16-bit
  producer index it carries; their reads use the ringing thread's release clock (its last
  release fence, as `sync_publish`), or an empty clock when that fence is narrower than GPU
  scope or absent. A WQE or payload byte whose last write is not ordered before it is a race
  (`nic-wqe-unordered`, `nic-src-unordered`); the WQE then executes with the bytes as they are.
  A weak store to a doorbell, or a store to the doorbell page that is not an 8-byte ring
  (BlueFlame), is `unmodeled`. The doorbell record (DBR) store is plain memory; the NIC acts
  on doorbell rings only.
- Source: DOCA GPUNetIO `doca_gpu_dev_verbs_submit_db` / `ring_db` / `mark_wqes_ready`
  (fence.release.gpu, then `st.mmio.relaxed.sys`), mlx5 PRM doorbell format (ctrl segment
  dword 0: WQE index << 8; dword 1: QPN << 8). Fixture r5a_ibgda_putsig N1 (no fence), N2
  (`.cta` fence), N5 (a WQE segment written after the doorbell).
- Status: **argued.** Hardware (probes/ibgda P3, 20 configurations x 1e5 iterations): with no
  fence, or a `.cta` fence, between the WQE / payload stores and the doorbell, no stale WQE,
  stale payload, error CQE or hang was observed. The requirement follows DOCA and the PTX
  model (the NIC is an observer outside the GPU); on this hardware a fence-less doorbell
  verdict may be a false alarm.
- If wrong: *miss* if a GPU-scope release does not order stores in GPU memory before the
  NIC's DMA reads; *false alarm* if a narrower fence also suffices.
- Retire: probes/ibgda P3 with and without each fence.

### S-NIC-ORDER · code
**The NIC executes a queue pair's WQEs one at a time, in posting order; nothing orders WQEs
of different queue pairs. Only IBTA ordering is modeled.**
- Model: one pending `AsyncKind::Nic` op per QP, completing the oldest announced WQE; a QP
  declared with another `ordering` (out-of-order data placement) gives `unmodeled`.
- Source: IBTA RC transport (requests of one QP are processed in order); DOCA
  `0001-gpunetio-dp-ordering-ooo.patch` (dp_ordering off by default).
- Status: **validated** for the cross-QP half: probes/ibgda P2 observed stale data after a
  signal on another QP in 1e5 / 1e5 iterations (1 MiB writes; not observed at 8 B / 4 KiB).
  In-order execution within a QP: argued (P1, P4 consistent).
- If wrong: *miss* if WQEs of one QP can take effect out of order under IBTA ordering.
- Retire: probes/ibgda P2 / P4.

### S-NIC-SIGNAL · code
**An RDMA atomic (fetch-add / compare-swap) takes effect after the same queue pair's earlier
RDMA writes are placed, and an observer that acquires the atomic's value sees them**
(put-with-signal without a WQE fence bit).
- Model: each WQE's clock includes the QP's previous WQE's clock; the atomic is a release.
- Source: DOCA `doca_gpu_dev_verbs_put_signal_thread` and mscclpp `putWithSignal` post the
  write and the atomic with no fence bit; NVSHMEM `put_signal` semantics. Fixture
  r5a_ibgda_putsig N3 (the signal posted first).
- Status: **validated** (not refuted): probes/ibgda P1, put of 8 B / 4 KiB / 1 MiB then a
  fetch-add signal on the same QP, stale data not observed in 1e5 iterations per size and
  receiver variant (15 configurations).
- If wrong: *miss*.
- Retire: probes/ibgda P1.

### S-NIC-WRITE · code
**RDMA write data synchronizes with nothing directly and has no placement order**, within or
across writes (aligned words are single-copy atomic, S-NIC-WORD; a lone aligned 4- or 8-byte
write is a release, S-NIC-FLAG). A reader that polls a word of write data and then reads
other words of it races with them.
- Status: **argued** (conservative: no ordering or single-copy atomicity is assumed).
  probes/ibgda P4: a flag write after a large write on one QP was never seen before the data
  in 1e5 iterations (4 KiB, 1 MiB), so polling a write's last word may be a false alarm here.
- If wrong: *false alarm* for kernels that poll the last word of a write (not observed in the
  target kernels).
- Retire: probes/ibgda P4 would only support a weaker model, not a stronger one.

### S-NIC-WORD · code
**Each naturally aligned 8-byte word of RDMA write data (4-byte at the edges of a write) lands
single-copy atomic: a relaxed system-scope write of the NIC.** Unaligned edge bytes are plain
writes. No order between words and no release (S-NIC-WRITE). A strong load of such a word,
at its width, does not race with it; DeepEP's hybrid notify relies on this (`recv_and_reduce`:
each count of a multi-int put is polled with `ld.acquire.sys` and decoded on its own).
- Source: PCIe writes do not tear naturally aligned qwords; nothing in IBTA.
- Where: `nic.rs` `complete_nic` (`OP_RDMA_WRITE`).
- Status: **validated** by probes/ibgda P2 (1 MiB) and P6a (4 KiB, 1 MiB): the receiver read
  8-byte words with `ld.relaxed.sys` while a write was landing; 6.03e9 (P2) and 1.3e10 (P6a)
  words held the old or the new tag, none a mix of both (`other` = 0).
- Complete overlap (MISS 194, 2026-11-12): at the strict PTX level each chunk is one location
  of its width (S-SCOPE, `NicState::elem`), so an unordered strong access of another width
  that shares a byte with it is a mixed-size data race (PTX ISA 9.5 sections 8.7, 8.7.2):
  fixtures/e_nic_cta WORDPART, a 4-byte poll of an 8-byte chunk, races; WORDFULL (8 bytes) and
  WORD4 (a 4-byte edge chunk read at 4 bytes) are clean. Until 2026-11-12 every access was one
  location with the NIC's. The probes read whole 8-byte words, so a 4-byte read of a chunk is
  not measured; the PTX model calls it a race in any case.
- If wrong: *miss* of a torn read of an 8-byte word.

### S-NIC-FLAG · code
**A WQE whose only data segment is a naturally aligned 4- or 8-byte RDMA write lands as one
strong system-scope write that releases the QP's earlier WQEs** (the same release a fetch-add
signal gets, S-NIC-SIGNAL). mscclpp's `PortChannelIbgda` signals this way: a 4-byte write of
the outbound semaphore token into the peer's inbound token, polled with `ld.acquire.sys` /
`LD.E.STRONG.SYS`.
- Source: IBTA RC executes a QP's writes in order; a PCIe write of an aligned dword / qword is
  not torn. Neither says the flag is placed after the earlier write's data (PCIe relaxed
  ordering may reorder them), so this is the probe's claim.
- Where: `nic.rs` `complete_nic` (`OP_RDMA_WRITE`).
- Status: **validated** by probes/ibgda P4 (8-byte flag) and P4b (4-byte flag): a 4 KiB or
  1 MiB write then the flag on the same QP, one or two doorbells, receiver `ld.acquire.sys` on
  the flag then the data: stale data not observed, 1e5 iterations each (8 configurations).
- If wrong: *miss* of a stale read after a flag (the probes saw none).

### S-NIC-ATOMIC · code
**A NIC atomic is a strong system-scope read-modify-write of an aligned 8-byte word whose
value is little-endian in memory; NIC atomics are atomic with each other only.** A GPU strong
write of a word that a NIC atomic then updates, or a GPU atomic on a word a NIC atomic updated,
unordered with it, is `unmodeled` (`nic-atomic-mixed`; `nic_atomic_mixed`, `nic_gpu_atomic`).
- Release sequences (MISS 166, 2026-11-12): a NIC atomic continues the release sequence of
  the write it reads as a GPU read-modify-write does (S-SCOPE, `sync_publish`): only when the
  two are morally strong, the write's scope including the NIC (`.sys`, or `.gpu` on the GPU
  of the doorbell thread; the NIC is in no CTA or cluster, MISS 193), and the write's own release
  pattern stays apart with its first operation's thread and scope (`nic_publish`,
  `SyncCell::cont`; PTX ISA 9.5 sections 8.9.2, 8.9.4), and at the strict PTX level the write
  must be one location with the atomic's 8-byte word (MISS 194, S-SCOPE complete overlap: a
  4-byte release write heads no sequence the atomic continues, fixtures/e_nic_rseq
  SYSREL_PART). Until 2026-11-12 every NIC atomic continued the
  sequence and joined the write's release into its own system-scope one. Where a NIC atomic
  heads the sequence, that was a wrong clean on the PTX front: in fixtures/e_nic_rseq NICHEAD a
  second NIC atomic, rung by a thread of the receiver's GPU, continues the first, and the
  receiver's `.gpu` acquire fence, whose scope leaves out the first one's doorbell thread on the
  other GPU, synchronized with the first one's release; now dst races (model). The SASS front
  and the GB300 profile re-run are clean before and after: the fence's CCTL.IVALL takes every
  pending release (model). Where a GPU write heads the sequence and the continuation matters,
  the write is not ordered before the NIC atomic (when it is, the atomic's own release already
  covers what the pattern releases), so `nic-atomic-mixed` reports the run `unmodeled` on both
  builds (argued; `nic_atomic_mixed` skips NIC writers, so it does not cover a NIC-headed
  sequence): a `.gpu` release on another GPU than the doorbell thread's (good) or a `.cta` fence
  heading the pattern (FREL) synchronized with a receiver outside its scope; now the receiver's
  read of d2 races in both beside that finding, on both fronts and at sass_gb300 (FREL was
  `unmodeled` only, with no GB300 profile re-run; good already raced on the signal word), and
  SYSREL and FREL_SYS (a `.sys` release or fence) keep the continuation (model). With
  `nic-atomic-mixed`'s report removed in a test build, FREL is clean before the fix and a race
  after it, on both fronts (model). kernel_db: 42 of the 44 NIC records (19 SASS, msl_ops
  nicdc_* and nichyb_*; 25 PTX, PX msl_ops), all but the two flush records, build fetch-add WQEs
  (static: the kernels OR the host-order opcode 0x12 into the control word and byte-swap it),
  and the captured send queues of the same 42 hold fetch-add WQEs of add 1 (record data); none
  builds a compare-swap or masked atomic. No verdict is expected to change (argued): their 774
  QPs all join GPUs in different NVLink domains and none is a loopback QP (record data), so the
  word a NIC atomic updates is on the QP's peer GPU, read only from that GPU's domain
  (S-NIC-DOMAIN), and its readers' `.cta`, `.cluster` and `.gpu` scopes hold none of the
  doorbell threads of the QPs that update it: a reader synchronizes with such an atomic only
  through a `.sys` acquire, whose scope holds every earlier doorbell thread too. Source mutants
  nic-rseq-moral and nic-rseq-join (NICHEAD catches the latter). Placement: ISA text applied to
  the NIC as a system-scope agent, the strict level of both fronts and the GB300 profile re-run
  (the hardware model joins every release at system scope, E-HW-L1); that the NIC is in its
  doorbell thread's `.gpu` scope is the model's (argued).
- Source: IB atomicity guarantee (IBV_ATOMIC_HCA: between QPs of one HCA).
- Status: **validated**: probes/ibgda P0 (fetch-adds of 1 leave 1, 2, 3, 4 as little-endian
  words; the fetched values come back little-endian); P7 (1e5 NIC fetch-adds and 16.8M GPU
  `red.add.sys` on one word: every NIC add landed, 4.9M GPU adds were lost).
- If wrong: values (not ordering) differ for kernels that compare the word's value.
- Retire: probes/ibgda P1 / P7.

### S-NIC-CQE · code
**With CQ update requested, the NIC writes the WQE's CQE (owner bit = pass parity over the
ring, opcode 0, WQE counter) after the WQE completed; for an RDMA write, completion means the
data was placed at the peer. The CQE write is a strong system-scope release of everything the
WQE and the QP's earlier WQEs did.** A poller that acquires the CQE may reuse the send buffer
and is ordered after the remote placement.
- Source: IBTA RC (a write completes once acknowledged); DOCA `poll_cq_at` (owner bit, then
  `fence.acquire.sys`). Fixture r5a_ibgda_putsig N4 (send buffer reused without polling).
- Status: **validated** (not refuted): probes/ibgda P5 (poll QP A's CQE, then signal on QP B:
  stale not observed in 1e5 per size, 8 B / 4 KiB / 1 MiB) and P6 (overwriting the source
  after the CQE poll: never received, 1e5; without the poll: the overwritten bytes arrived in
  1e5 / 1e5 iterations).
- Complete overlap (MISS 194, 2026-11-12): the model publishes the CQE's fields at bytes 56-59,
  60-61, 62 and 63 (`nic_publish`; mlx5's `sop_drop_qpn`, `wqe_counter`, `signature`,
  `op_own`). At the strict PTX level a strong access of one field at its width is one location
  with the CQE write; one that spans or splits a field, or covers another byte of the CQE, is
  `unmodeled` (`nic-overlap`) when its scopes make the pair morally strong (S-SCOPE;
  fixtures/e_nic_cta CQEPART, a 4-byte read of bytes 60-63). DOCA's CQ poll reads the owner
  byte (63) at its width (static, cute.A2aHybrid.w2; S-SCOPE, MISS 193).
- If wrong: *miss* if a completion can precede remote placement or the NIC's last read of the
  source.
- Retire: probes/ibgda P5 / P6.

### S-NIC-DOMAIN · code
**A GPU loads, stores and atomics only memory of its own NVLink domain; another domain's
memory (another node without multi-node NVLink) is reachable only through the NIC.** A direct
access is a fault (case `domains`).
- Where: `exec.rs` `resolve` -> nic.rs `nic_domain_check`. Fixture r5a_ibgda_putsig N8.
- Status: **argued** (a peer mapping across nodes does not exist without MNNVL).
- If wrong: *false alarm* on MNNVL systems if `domains` is set wrongly.
- Retire: n/a (configuration).

### S-ALIGN · code
**A load, store or atomic of `n` bytes (`n` a power of two; a vector counts its whole size,
`ld.v4.u32` = 16, SASS `LDS.128` = 16) must be `n`-aligned; a misaligned one is a `fault`.**
Global, shared, shared::cluster and generic addresses; parameter space is not checked.
- Where: `exec.rs` `check_aligned` (`Op::Ld`, `Op::St`, `Op::Atom`).
- Status: **validated.** GB300 traps with "misaligned address" on `st.global.u64` at +4,
  `ld.shared.v4.u32` at +8, `atom.global.add.u64` (ptxas: `REDG.E.ADD.64`) at +4 and
  `st.global.u32` at +2 (fixtures/e_misaligned, `ptxv probe` 2026-11-05). Found by AK.
- If wrong: *false alarm* only if some form tolerated a misaligned address.

### S-GLOBAL · code
**Global memory is touched only by this kernel:** buffers come from the case, and nothing else
reads or writes them concurrently. Addresses are synthetic (GLOBAL_BASE, PARAM_BASE).
- Where: `lib.rs` `build_launch`, `machine.rs` constants.
- Status: **argued** for single-kernel cases. Cross-kernel and cross-GPU sharing is rung
  1e/1f/4 work.
- Multi-process captures (rung 4a, `tools/capture_dist.py`): a rank's initial bytes include
  device copies it made before its first kernel (two-shot's `buf.copy_(x)`), and initial
  contents happen-before every kernel of every GPU. So whether a peer's start barrier orders
  that copy (two-shot's put is relaxed) is outside the verdict.

### S-GLOBAL-INIT · code
**Module data globals (`__device__` variables) start from the case's buffer, else from the
ELF.** A kernel reaches a global through a relocated constant-bank word (`LDC.64 R4,
c[0x4][0x0]`, `R_CUDA_64` against a `.nv.global` / `.nv.global.init` symbol). The launch backs
each (module, symbol, GPU) with one buffer: the case buffer declaring `symbol` (and `cubin`,
`device`), whose `init` is the captured contents, or else an automatic buffer holding the
`.nv.global.init` bytes (zeros for `.nv.global`). Launches of one module on one GPU share it, so
its state carries from launch to launch within the case. On hardware the buffer is the module's
own global (`cuModuleGetGlobal`), rewritten with the same bytes before every run. An
automatic buffer with neither captured bytes nor an initializer is listed in one note per
launch ("N module global(s) without captured bytes or an initializer, zero at module load
assumed: X, ..."; 2026-11-07), so the assumption shows per record. The PTX front reads the
module's `.global` declarations (`.visible` / `.extern` / `.weak`, scalars and arrays, integer
initializers as element bytes) and resolves a symbol operand (`mov.b64 %rd, sym`,
`[sym+off]`) to the same buffer, through a synthetic relocated word in bank 0x1f; a symbol with
any other initializer (`generic(...)`, floats) is refused where used (2026-11-08).
- Where: `lib.rs` `build_launch` (`global_buffers`), `exec.rs` `Op::LdConst`, `hw` `run_with`,
  `sass/src/elf.rs` `Elf::data_symbol`, `ptx/src/lib.rs` `parse_kernel` (module `.global`
  lines), `exec.rs` `SReg::GlobalAddr`.
- Status: **argued.** A captured case declares the globals its kernels' banks name, with their
  device contents at the snapshot (`tools/capture_dist.py`, `ptxv.capture`). An automatic buffer
  is right for a fresh module and wrong for a long-running process whose earlier kernels
  changed the global (DeepEP's `epSyncer` counts barrier rounds). fixtures/s_globals is
  bitwise equal to GB300; probes/ptx_globals (initialized, zero and scratch globals, PTX front)
  is bitwise equal to GB300 on both fronts (20/20, 2026-11-08).
- Not modeled: a global reached through a relocated instruction immediate (`32@lo(sym)`,
  relocatable code): address 0, as before. `__constant__` globals.
- If wrong: *miss* or *false alarm*: the kernels run from other initial state than the
  process had.
- Retire: capture every referenced global (done for capture_dist captures).

### S-CBANK · code
**Driver constants:** `c[0x0][0x0..0x14]` = block/grid dims, `0x348` = generic param base,
`0x110` = generic address of constant bank 0 itself (cuBLAS reads a tensor map at
`c[0x0][0x110] + 0x6c0`, i.e. cbank 0x6c0 = param offset 0x340; consistent with 0x348),
`0x358` (global descriptor for `desc[URx]`) ignored, `0x36c` = `%is_explicit_cluster` (1 iff
the launch names a cluster shape; `probes/cluster_flag` on GB300; ptxas skips
`barrier.cluster` unless it is 1), `0x37c` = stack pointer 0xfffc (no local memory), `0x2f8` = generic base of the local window
(an unmapped 0x7d00_0000_0000: DeepEP only builds vprintf argument pointers from it), params at
`constant0 size − param size`. Any other driver constant is an error.
- PTX front: `cvta.local.u64` adds the same base and `cvta.to.local.u64` subtracts it
  (2026-11-08); a local access whose address is not below 2^32 (a converted generic address
  outside the local window, undefined in PTX) is a fault. probes/local_cvta: GB300 50/50
  scrubbed, both fronts bitwise.
- A generic access or atomic through the local window faults on both fronts, the message
  naming the window (2026-11-12; before, "outside every allocation"). ptxas 13.0's fallback of a
  generic `atom.add.noftz.f16x2` / `.bf16x2` on a local address is an integer add (`LD.E;
  IADD3; ST.E`): GB300 gives 0x78007800 for 0x3c003c00 + 0x3c003c00, both forms, 3/3 runs.
  Modelling generic-to-local accesses must model that add, not N-F16X2. fixtures/e_atom_local.
- Reads past the parameters fault on both fronts: SASS `LDC` through `cbank` ("cbank read
  past params"), and the PTX front's `ld.param` through a register address (2026-11-09; until
  then the bytes past the end read as 0 there, while ptxas compiles the load to an `LDC` of
  bank 0). fixtures/e_rep_divzero LDC.
- Where: `exec.rs` `Machine::cbank`, `Machine::local_addr`, `Machine::resolve` (the local
  window), `access_x` (`Loc::Param`); `ptx` the `cvta` arms.
- Status: **validated** by bitwise agreement. Only param offset 0 has been exercised.

### S-CGA-SHAPE · code
**`SR_CgaSize` is the index of the CTA's cluster shape: 0 for the launch's regular cluster shape,
1 for its preferred one** (`cudaLaunchAttributePreferredClusterDimension`). ptxas reads the
cluster special registers from the driver table at `c[0x0][x - 0xa0 * SR_CgaSize]`, one table
per shape (S-CBANK). A launch with a preferred dimension runs each group of CTAs of the
preferred shape either as one preferred cluster or as regular clusters; one launch mixes both,
and every CTA's registers describe its own cluster.
- Evidence: `probes/cga_size` (2026-11-06, GPU 1): `SR_CgaSize` read raw (patched cubin) for
  clusters of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 without a preferred dimension: 0 in every CTA. With a preferred
  dimension (2 -> 4, 1 -> 2, 1 -> 4, 2 -> 8, 4 -> 8, 4 -> 16; 512 CTAs): 1 in preferred clusters,
  0 in regular ones; with 200 KB of dynamic shared memory 0-22% of the CTAs ran in regular
  clusters, without it none. Every group of the preferred size was wholly one shape.
  `%cluster_nctarank`, `%cluster_ctarank`, `%cluster_nctaid`, `%clusterid`, `%nclusterid` and
  `%cluster_ctaid` describe the CTA's own cluster in both. A preferred dimension without a
  cluster dimension fails to launch. `crates/sim/tests/cga_size.rs` replays all 14 recorded
  configurations on the SASS front-end (each CTA from the shape it ran in). Before, ptxv set
  `SR_CgaSize` to the CTA count (consistent with the table only through the matching offset);
  cuBLAS tests `SR_CgaSize != 0` to choose its preferred-cluster path (mm_4k_8k:
  `128x256_64x6_2x2f_2cta`, captured with preferred [4, 1, 1] and cluster [2, 1, 1]), which then
  multicast to rank 2 of a 2-CTA cluster. With the model, mm_4k_8k with its cluster launch
  control parameter (`c[0x0][0xd10]`) set to 0 certifies in all 384 slices of both shapes, and
  the assembled output equals the GPU's capture bitwise (2026-11-06). The captured launch
  itself (parameter 2) executes `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST`, which is unmodeled (E-CLC).
- Capture: `probes/launchcap` and the Python API's `ptxvcap.c` record the attribute
  (`preferred_cluster`), and `tools/capture.py` / `_casewriter.py` write it to case.toml; `ptxv
  hw` passes it to the launch.
- Model: `Grid::preferred`, `Grid::cga_shape`, `Launch::preferred_shape` (every cluster
  preferred). The preferred shape must be a multiple of the regular one and divide the grid.
  `ptxv check --slices --certify` slices both shapes; the cross-cluster check pairs clusters of
  the two shapes whose CTAs are disjoint (those can coexist), each preferred cluster must write
  the same global bytes as the regular clusters of its CTAs, and the two shapes' assembled
  outputs must be equal, so that every mix ends with the same memory. Other checks of such a
  launch report `unmodeled` (only the regular shape was checked).
- Where: `exec.rs` `sreg` (`SReg::CgaShape`), `cbank`; `wellsync.rs` `check_sliced_one`;
  `cli` `cmd_check`.
- Status: **validated** for 1-D clusters (above). Clusters with y or z > 1 were not probed.
- If wrong: a *miss* or a *false alarm* in kernels that branch on `SR_CgaSize`, if the
  hardware's choice of shape per group is not free of other constraints the kernel can observe.

### S-SAME-VALUE · code
**A plain write of the byte value the last (plain) write left there conflicts with nothing.**
Every access unordered with such a pair sees that value in either order, so the pair is not
reported as a race: it is a note (kind `note`, printed `NOTE:`, no verdict class, does not stop
the certificate). The PTX memory model still calls it a data race. Triton layout conversions
store a replicated value from several warps to one shared address (`STS [R10+UR4], R17` from
t0 and t64), which made the certificate refuse and the explorer run out of states.
- Rule (`exec.rs` `access_x`, per byte): the write is plain, the last write is plain, and the
  written byte equals the byte in memory. The unordered earlier writes stay in the shadow
  (`Sh::hw`) and the unordered reads stay in its readers, so later accesses are still checked
  against them. The same-value write is marked (`Epoch::sv`): later reads are not checked
  against it (they see the value in either order) but against the write before it, which
  stays in `Sh::hw` while ordered. A plain last write with uncovered earlier writes therefore
  implies they wrote the same value; launch groups' `demote` (strong writes made plain) moves the last write into
  them, so that the rule cannot apply there. Strong writes keep their own rules (C-ORDER).
- Per byte over whole shadow pages (MISS 69, 2026-11-11): the shadow stores a 512-byte page
  whose bytes are all alike as one element (`Pages`), and `Pages::for_run` updates such a page,
  when an access covers it, with one call at the page's first byte. Bulk and TMA copies write
  runs of 512 bytes and more. Until 2026-11-11 that byte stood for the page: a reload that kept
  the first byte and changed the others was a same-value write of every byte, so later reads
  were not checked against it and earlier unordered reads were not reported
  (fixtures/s_sv_page `PAGE`, a read ordered after the reload only by a relaxed flag, and
  `CONC`, a read concurrent with it: clean on both fronts); a reload that changed the first
  byte and kept others was a plain write of the kept bytes too. Now `access_x` splits a
  uniform page first when a write keeps the value of only some of its bytes (or carries an
  S-INIT mask, which is per byte too). The other `for_run` closures depend on the index only
  through what they report: launch groups' `demote`, TMEM allocation marks and TMEM accesses
  (lane and column in race messages); `access_x`'s reads use it for S-INIT's reserved prefix
  (page-aligned) and a tensor map's tolerated tail, where the page's first byte is the one
  that reports. Fixture `s_sv_page` (good, SAME clean; PAGE, CONC, SHIFT race), source mutant
  `sv-page-onebyte`. A/B (2026-11-11, model; the fix against its parent): 208 kernel_db
  records whose captured code writes shadowed memory with bulk or TMA copies, with their own
  check options (SASS front, `--certify`), 120 more bounded at 2000 states, and 415 fixture
  checks: the only flips are s_sv_page PAGE and CONC on both fronts (clean -> race); 484 pairs
  are unchanged (6 of them after a 3600 s rerun of a pair with a verdict in one arm only) and
  255 have no verdict in either arm. Only shared memory takes the uniform-page path: global
  writes reach `access_x` per element or per 16 bytes (an independent review found no
  same-value write onto a uniform page in 494 case dirs with async operations or a NIC, 427
  of them run to the end).
- Own store (2026-11-07, msl DeepEP `DeviceSyncer`: every CTA stores the next
  `currentCountIdx`, then reads it back): a plain read of a byte whose shadow holds the
  reader's own plain store is not checked against the shadow's writes; a note
  (`same-value:...:own`). By the rule above every write in the shadow stored the current value
  (a store of another value drops the others), so the own store did, and coherence lets the
  read return only the own store or a later one. Writes made later are checked against the
  read when they come: another value races with it, the same value takes the same-value path.
  A store of another value that happens before the read but is unordered with the own store
  is a write-write race with it, reported at whichever store comes second. Only plain stores
  of threads on the reader's GPU qualify: an async-proxy, NVLS-view, NIC, peer-GPU or DSMEM
  store in the shadow disqualifies the byte, as do strong writes demoted at a launch-group
  boundary (`Sh::mixed`). Only thread reads (not an async proxy's read). Per byte, so the own
  store must cover every byte read; other threads (same warp or SM) do not count. The read is
  still recorded in the shadow's readers, so later stores and landing async writes are checked
  against it. The shadow is keyed by allocation (`Loc::Global { alloc, off }`); further
  mappings of an allocation (`[[views]]`, multicast) reach the same shadow, and a byte last
  written through a mapping other than the primary one disqualifies it (S-VA-ALIAS). Fixture
  `s_sv_own` (good clean; `diff`, `noown`, `xhb` race).
- Not covered: read-modify-write sequences that happen to agree (FA4's idempotent row-max
  revert): those are reported as races.
- Certificate (E-WELLSYNC): one run shows equal values only for that schedule. The certificate
  accepts a same-value note only when the run has no strong accesses and no polls, so every
  value written is fixed by the launch inputs. Otherwise it refuses and the explorer decides.
  Without this restriction `fixtures/e_ring_warp` W1 (a warp ring whose writes carry values
  read through polls) certified clean while the explorer finds the race.
- Evidence: `probes/same_value` (2026-11-06): lane 0 of every warp stores the same word to one
  shared and one global address without synchronization, 1000 / 1000 runs with 2 CTAs x 4
  warps and 200 / 200 with 16 CTAs x 8 warps read back v. `probe_same_value_matches_hardware`
  replays it; its `differ` variant (warp w stores v + w) stays a race. Triton's
  `_kernel_fp32_to_lowp_sr` now certifies in 0.25 s with GB300's output (was: incomplete at
  2M states after 173 s).
- Status: **validated** (above; byte stores of equal value cannot produce another value).
- Placement: the per-byte comparison is the same at both levels (a write that changes a byte
  races with unordered reads under the PTX contract and on GB300 alike), so the page split
  applies to both. The rule itself turns same-value pairs into notes at both levels,
  `ptx_contract` included, although the PTX memory model calls such a pair a data race. Its
  evidence is GB300 measured (probes/same_value) and argued (stores of one byte value leave
  that value); by the placement rules that supports the gb300 profile, not the strict level.
  Reporting the pair as a race at `ptx_contract` is open.
- If wrong: a *miss* only if hardware could produce a value other than the one both writes
  store.

### S-SMEM-ADDR32 · code
**Shared-memory addresses are 32-bit: the parts of an address operand (`[R+UR+imm]`) add
modulo 2^32.** ptxas folds a uniform base and a per-thread offset into one operand; a negative
offset is a large unsigned register value. cuBLAS's nvjet mainloops index their mbarrier ring
as `[R8+UR30]` with R8 = -0x28 when the stage index wraps (mm_1k_4k, mm_4k_8k).
- Evidence: `probes/smem_addr_wrap` (2026-11-06): `LDS R7, [R4+UR4+0x28]` with R4 = 0xffffffd8,
  clusters of 2, 20 runs: every thread reads its own word. A 64-bit sum names CTA rank 256,
  which the model reported as an illegal-instruction fault (and a deterministic run retried the
  faulting step forever: the mm_1k_4k certificate run that did not finish).
  `probe_smem_addr_wrap_matches_hardware` (tests/fixtures.rs) replays it.
- Where: `exec.rs` `resolve`.
- Status: **validated** (above).
- If wrong: a *false alarm* (a fault) or a *miss* (an access resolved to the wrong offset) in
  kernels whose shared address parts overflow 32 bits.

### E-SMID · exec
**`%smid` is a launch-time nondeterministic choice per CTA in `[0, %nsmid)`, fixed for the
CTA's lifetime; a verdict covers the enumerated SM placements, not every assignment.**
`%smid` (SASS `S2R/S2UR SR_VIRTUALSMID`) reads the SM a CTA runs on; `%nsmid` (SASS: the driver
constant `c[0x0][0x2d0]`) is 152 (`PTXV_NSMID`). A kernel that reads `%smid` is checked once
per placement and the verdicts are merged (`crates/sim/src/smid.rs`): findings of every
placement (the message names it), complete only if every run was, outputs pooled (so an
output that depends on the placement is `nondeterministic`). Placements (`PTXV_SMID`, comma
separated, default `spread,same,rev,alt`): `spread` (CTA i of each grid on SM i mod 152),
`same` (every CTA on SM 0: CTAs that share an SM), `rev` (SM 151 - i mod 152: the top of the
range), `alt` (alternately bottom and top: both halves of the range with few CTAs),
`rand<k>` (pseudo-random, seed k). The concolic engine (symb.rs) keeps `%smid` a leaf, and
the symmetric slice check seeds position taint from it as from `%ctaid`.
- Evidence: `probes/smid` (2026-11-09, GB300, 3 runs of 1024 CTAs x 32 threads,
  `results/r1.bin`): `%nsmid` = 152 in every CTA; `%smid` takes every value 0..151 (up to 7
  CTAs per SM), CTA 0 on SM 148 and the order the same in all three runs; no CTA's `%smid`
  changed across a 20 us `%globaltimer` spin. PTX `%smid` compiles to `S2R SR_VIRTUALSMID`
  and `%nsmid` to `LDC c[0x0][0x2d0]`. `fixtures/smid_slot` (stores to `out[%smid % 4]`) is
  clean under `spread` and a race under `same` (`smid_placements_reach_shared_sm`).
- Completeness split (2026-11-09): `smid_reaches_control` taints registers from `%smid`
  through the arithmetic (and through memory: a stored value taints every later non-parameter
  load). When `%smid` reaches only data (no guard, branch, address, synchronization or other
  control operand: fixtures/smid_data), control and accesses are the same in every placement,
  the verdict stays complete, and the pooled outputs show any placement dependence
  (`nondeterministic`). When it reaches control (fixtures/smid_slot, smid_three), the
  placements are a sample and `%smid` may change mid-run: the merged verdict is **incomplete**
  ("smid-dependent control: placements sampled"), findings stand. The wellsync certificate
  refuses a kernel that reads `%smid` unless an enumeration fixed the placement
  (`Machine::smid_fixed`): a certificate of one placement is not a verdict. fixtures/smid_three races only
  with three CTAs on one SM and one on the next, which no class has (set by hand, it races).
- Status: **unvalidated**: the PTX ISA allows any SM placement, ids that are not contiguous,
  and a `%smid` that changes during execution (preemption, migration). Four (or more) classes
  reach collisions and both ends of the range, but a finding that needs some other
  assignment (three CTAs on one SM, a specific die split) is missed, and a value that
  changes mid-run is not modeled. `%nsmid` differs on other parts and under partitioning
  (MIG, green contexts).
- If wrong: *miss*.
- Where: `smid.rs` (`placements`, `explore_smid`, `check_placements`); `exec.rs` `sreg`,
  `cbank` 0x2d0; `l1_cores.rs` `explore_placements` and the CLI's `check` call it.

### E-BSYNC · exec
**`BSSY Bb` records the lanes executing it; `BSYNC.RECONVERGENT Bb` waits until all of them that
have not exited arrive, then orders them like `bar.warp.sync`** (their clocks are joined).
**A `BSYNC Bb` without `.RECONVERGENT` (plain or `.RELIABLE`), or a `.RECONVERGENT` one that a
lane of its region can reach after a `YIELD`, a `NANOSLEEP` or a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE`, is no
reconvergence point: the executing lanes leave the barrier as with `BREAK Bb`, and nothing is
ordered (MISS 81, gap G1).** ptxas
compiles `__syncwarp()` after a divergent region to the reconverging `BSYNC` alone (rung 3a:
lane 0 copies a tensor-map template to shared memory, then after `BSYNC` all 32 lanes read it).
- Where: `exec.rs` `Op::Bssy` / `Op::Bsync`, `bsync_holds`, `Warp::bmask`; `explore.rs`
  `bsync_parked`, `whole_or_parked`, `local_ample` (BSYNC arrivals and runs beside parked lanes
  expanded alone, see "BSYNC reconvergence" under E-DRF); `sass` lifter (`Op::Bsync::form`,
  `reconvergent_yields`: `BarForm::ReconvergentYield`).
- **MISS 81 (2026-11-11): the BSYNC forms.** ptxas 13.0 (sm_103a) emits three. `.RECONVERGENT`
  joins regions without a yield (10,943 of the scan's 10,989 `.RECONVERGENT` regions; the
  others below), and a `bar.warp.sync` right after such a region compiles to that `BSYNC`
  alone (fixtures/e_bsync_plain RECONV; `__syncwarp()` after a loop with a lane-dependent
  break: no `WARPSYNC`). The plain form (no modifier) joins regions that contain
  a `YIELD` (a spin loop), a `NANOSLEEP` or a `BRA.DIV` slow path's `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE`;
  where the PTX synchronizes the warp after such a region, ptxas adds a `WARPSYNC.ALL`
  (e_bsync_plain WARPSYNC; `__syncwarp()` after a nanosleep loop or a volatile spin loop).
  `.RELIABLE` joins loop regions left with `BREAK.RELIABLE`. Kernel_db scan (1,414 record case
  directories; entry functions and their callees; cuobjdump 13.0): 179 records have a plain
  `BSYNC` and 110 a `.RELIABLE` one (273 either). Of 4,544 plain regions (control-flow walk
  from the `BSSY` to its `BSYNC`), 2,041 reach a `YIELD` / `NANOSLEEP`, 2,495 a
  `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE` and no `YIELD` / `NANOSLEEP`, 8 neither (cutlass_fmha forward: a
  division slow path, ALU only; barrier and mbarrier waits were not counted); none
  of the 179 `.RELIABLE` regions reaches a `YIELD` / `NANOSLEEP` (evidence: compiler output).
  - GB300 (measured): probes/mbar_init_diverge late_sleep_reconv (264 x 128 threads, 256
    rounds): the waiting lanes pass ptxas's plain `BSYNC B0` while the elected lane sleeps
    and read the slot before its init, 10,000 of 10,000 runs wrong; probes/bsync_coll: lane 0
    passes a plain `BSYNC B3` while lane 16 waits at a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE`
    (E-HW-BSYNC-COLLECTIVE). The SASS front took both as reconvergence points (clean; a
    deadlock).
  - Fixture: fixtures/e_bsync_plain (grid 1, block 32, 2 rounds; the probe's kernel): good
    SASS clean before, race after (PTX race on both builds); RECONV, WARPSYNC clean and
    LATE_RECONV SASS clean on both builds, NOBSYNC race on both. tests/fixtures.rs
    `e_bsync_plain_is_no_reconvergence_point`; source mutants `bsync-plain-holds` (every form
    holds) and `bsync-form-plain` (the lifter drops `.RECONVERGENT`) are killed by it.
  - The explorer's BSYNC reductions (the arrival in `local_ample`, `bsync_parked`, the
    look-ahead's elected body, `la_rejoin`) and the certificate's C-WARP mask check apply to
    reconvergence points only.
  - **Gap G1 (closed 2026-11-11): a `.RECONVERGENT` `BSYNC` around a region that can yield.**
    GB300 lets the waiting lanes pass `BSYNC.RECONVERGENT` as well while a lane of its mask
    sleeps: probes/mbar_init_diverge late_sleep_reconvform (late_sleep_reconv with ptxas's
    `BSSY B0` / `BSYNC B0` set to the `.RECONVERGENT` form, bits 72-73 = 2) is wrong in 10,000 of
    10,000 runs, as late_sleep (measured, positive). It also passes one while the rest of its
    mask waits at a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE`: fixtures/e_bsync_parked_collective RECONV (the join's
    `BSSY` / `BSYNC` patched the same way) completes 10,000 of 10,000 runs, bitwise equal to
    good (measured, positive; the strict level deadlocked there). Without a yield in the region
    it holds: late_reconv (the clock spin, ptxas's `.RECONVERGENT` join kept), 0 wrong in
    10,000 runs (a null result, a bound at the GB300 level only). ptxas relies on the form after
    regions without a yield (a `bar.warp.sync` right after one compiles to it alone, above), and
    also after regions whose yields the whole mask runs together: msl_ops
    FlashAttentionBackwardSm100 varlen calleracc has full-warp `SHFL.DOWN` / `SHFL.UP` right
    after `BSYNC.RECONVERGENT B1` (0x12b30, no `WARPSYNC`), and its region's `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS`
    sits only in try_wait retry loops that the converged warp enters (compiler output). The
    measured passes need a lane of the mask asleep or at the collective while others of it wait,
    which such loops never give; the walk does not tell the two apart (that needs a convergence
    analysis), so the rule takes both as the plain form (precision cost below). Rule (both
    levels): a `.RECONVERGENT` `BSYNC` that a region walk meeting a `YIELD`,
    an executable `NANOSLEEP` (not `@!PT`) or a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE` reaches is taken as the
    plain form (`BarForm::ReconvergentYield`): the strict level holds no lane there, the GB300
    profile holds until a lane of its mask yields or blocks (E-HW-BSYNC-YIELD). The walk
    (lifter `reconvergent_yields`) starts after each `BSSY Bb` and each `BMOV.32 Bb, Ra`
    restore; follows every branch edge, jump table and call (into the callee, and on after the
    call); and ends a path at a `BSYNC Bb` (which it then reaches), an unguarded `BREAK Bb`,
    `EXIT`, `BPT.TRAP` or `BMOV.32.CLEAR` of Bb, a guarded `BREAK Bb` followed by a branch on the
    same guard (ptxas's loop exit: the breaking lanes take the branch), and the `RET` of a
    followed call (the region's own function's `RET` goes on at every return site).
    - Kernel_db (1,414 record case directories, cuobjdump 13.0, the walk above): 46
      `.RECONVERGENT` regions in 41 records (ads_mkl 2, flashinfer 17, mslk 4, msl_ops 18; CuTe
      DSL and CUTLASS warp-role branches of 158 to 3,389 instructions) reach a
      `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS` (36), a `YIELD` (10), a `NANOSLEEP` (4) or a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE` (4,
      msl_ops ReduceScatter.w4). The lifter itself, over all 1,496 loadable records (exact:
      its own demotions after loading every launch's cubin), demotes 48 `BSYNC`s in 45
      records: 44 for those 46 regions (ReduceScatter.w4's 4 regions end at 2 `BSYNC`s), one
      in a flashinfer fmhaSm103a record whose region holds a `BRX` with targets that reach a
      `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS` (the scan stopped at `BRX`), and one in each of 3 records whose case
      directories the scan did not read. The A/B below covers the 41 records; the other 4
      keep their classes (model). The first count (56 regions in 42 records, and 177 in 15
      where the walk also met a plain `BSYNC`) walked on past `BPT.TRAP` (the
      assertion-failure paths' `CALL.ABS.NOINC`) into unrelated code: 10 of the 56 and all of
      the 177 were such paths.
    - Fixture: e_bsync_plain SLEEP_RECONV (the probe at one warp): SASS clean before, race at
      both levels now, refused by the certificate at both (tests/fixtures.rs
      `e_bsync_plain_is_no_reconvergence_point`; sass `reconvergent_bsync_region_walk` for the
      walk). e_bsync_parked_collective RECONV: strict deadlock before, clean at both levels now
      (`bsync_releases_beside_a_parked_collective_under_the_gb300_profile`). Source mutants
      `bsync-g1-off` (no demotion), `bsync-g1-nocall` (callees outside the region),
      `bsync-g1-nocoll` (a collective does not count) and `bsync-g1-break` (any guarded `BREAK`
      ends a path).
    - Precision cost (A/B of the 41 records' SASS plus 16 whose first-scan regions lay past a
      `BPT.TRAP`, 57 pairs, triage then heavy reruns): 1 false alarm at the strict level only
      (the FlashAttentionBackwardSm100 varlen calleracc record above: the non-elected lanes
      leave `BSYNC B1` before the elected lane's `SYNCS.ARRIVE` tail, so the `SHFL`s read lanes
      not executing them, a fault, and the warp reaches a `BAR.SYNC` apart, a deadlock; argued
      false: the warp runs the sleeping loops converged; the profile verdict is unchanged), 3
      certificate refusals with the same verdict by exploration (msl_ops
      BlackwellCompressionLseDecode: C-WARP checks reconvergence points only) and 1 at the time
      budget; 10 unchanged; 42 without a verdict on both builds. Fixtures (189 pairs, 14 without a
      verdict on both builds): only the two variants above flip.
  - **Residual G2 (open, argued): a lane recorded in another region of the barrier.** A `BSSY`
    adds its lanes to the barrier's mask, so a `BSYNC.RECONVERGENT` that still holds also
    waits for a lane left behind in an earlier region of the same barrier, one its other lanes
    left early (through a `BSYNC` that holds no lane, or a `BREAK`) and in which that lane may
    still yield; GB300 would let the waiting lanes go at that yield (late_sleep_reconvform), or,
    if a `BSSY` sets the mask rather than adding to it, not wait for that lane at all. The lane
    leaves its own region through a `BSYNC` that holds no lane, which joins no clocks, so races
    between it and the lanes released later are reported either way: the hold restricts
    schedules only (the order of atomics, a wait's outcome, the outputs). Static exposure (same
    barrier in one function, control flow not ordered): 4,684 holding regions in 178 records
    share a barrier with such a region (3,748 in 106 records with a `WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE` in
    it). Probe to settle it: an elected lane's nanosleep spin in a plain region of B0, the other
    lanes then in a `.RECONVERGENT` region of B0, reading after its `BSYNC` what the spinning
    lane writes with an atomic.
  - Placement: the strict level holds no lane at a `BSYNC` without `.RECONVERGENT`. The plain
    form is measured not to hold under a yield or beside a collective, and ptxas does not rely
    on it for a warp sync. That it holds while no lane it waits for has yielded or blocked is a
    measured null (GB300 never ran lanes ahead without a yield: probes/split_yield;
    mbar_init_diverge `late` and `nobsync`, with no `BSYNC` at all, 0 of 10,000 runs each),
    which ptxas's uniform-register allocation relies on (argued, E-HW-BSYNC-YIELD): so a GB300
    profile rule (E-HW-BSYNC-YIELD), never strict. A static form (regions without a yield) would
    reach 8 plain regions of the scan, ALU only; the dynamic one reaches every plain region.
    `.RELIABLE` is neither measured nor relied on by ptxas for a warp sync, so it is not
    assumed either; the case for it (the no-yield counterpart of the plain loop form, as
    `.RECONVERGENT` is of the plain join) is argued only.
  - Consequences: fixtures/e_bsync_parked_collective strict: deadlock before, clean after,
    bitwise = GB300; E-HW-BSYNC-COLLECTIVE releases nothing there any more. MISS 52's
    deadlock (probes/warpsync_pairs SASS) is gone at the strict level. The certificate refuses
    where lanes leave a plain `BSYNC` apart and meet again (r1a_tcgen05_tile, r1c_cluster,
    r1c_2sm and warpsync_pairs SASS: C-WARP; explored instead). fixtures/s_warpcoll: its
    outputs differ from GB300's in the words computed from the second divergent section's
    `__activemask()` only. e_warpcoll_bin HISKIP: the deadlock is gone, the fault stays.
    e_mbar_scope PFC, PFCW, NOF and PCTA SASS: race, now also nondeterministic (the racing
    read's stale outcome; the rev before reaches it with `PTXV_NO_BSYNC_POR=1`: a racy
    kernel's outputs are not complete, E-DRF). e_mbar_lww WAR / WARF under the GB300 profile:
    clean by exploration instead of certified. Precision costs: fixtures/s_lift_l's
    exploration (complete in 4,624 states before) does not complete in 3M states (a
    deterministic run and a bounded exploration now); probes/coll_split's cubin: the
    certificate refuses (C-WARP; its exploration did not complete before either);
    probes/syncwarp_fast
    strict: faults and a deadlock from switches inside a uniform-register window (MISS 52's
    kind; GB300 profile clean, bitwise).
- `BMOV.32[.CLEAR] Rd, Bb` copies barrier b's lane mask into Rd (`.CLEAR`: and empties
  it); `BMOV.32 Bb, Ra` sets it from Ra (Triton's parallel_attn_bwd_dkv: `BSSY B11`,
  `BMOV.32.CLEAR R2, B11`, a region, `BMOV.32 B11, R2`, `BSYNC B11`). The mask encoding in
  the register is the model's: a kernel whose saved register is read by anything but a
  restore is refused (`l2::check_bmov`). A `.CLEAR` by part of a warp while the barrier
  records lanes outside that part, and a restore whose lanes disagree, are unmodeled (the
  case clears its spare B10, empty, from two parts of a warp). Not probed in isolation; the case's output is the evidence.
- Rung 4 (nested regions, ptxas's division slow path inside a loop body): a lane parked at
  another barrier register (or at a `WARPSYNC`) is not waiting at this `BSYNC`; parts of a
  warp that execute one `BSSY` separately add their lanes to its mask, and a release removes
  the released lanes; lanes already parked at the `BSYNC` take part in it. (Before, a release
  counted lanes parked at any convergence barrier, and a second part's `BSSY` overwrote the
  mask: s_alu2 deadlocked and faulted in some schedules.) `BREAK Bb` (`BREAK.RELIABLE`, torch's
  elementwise loops leaving a region early) removes the executing lanes from Bb's mask, and
  lanes already parked at Bb's `BSYNC` are released if the rest of the mask is now there.
  `BREAK Pc, Bb` (`@!P0 BREAK.RELIABLE !P2, B2`, ptxas's div.rn.ftz slow path, paired with
  `@!P0 BRA !P2, ...`) removes only the lanes where the guard and Pc hold, as S-BRA-COND's
  branch takes them (`probes/div_ftz`: div.rn.ftz.f32 on every pair of 32 edge patterns =
  GB300 on the SASS front-end, `probe_div_ftz_matches_hardware`, 2026-11-06).
- A lane's `EXIT` re-checks the lanes of its warp parked at a plain `WARPSYNC` or a `BSYNC`
  (`exit_warpsync_release`; each barrier lanes are parked at, since nested regions park at
