### N-BULK-RED · code
**`cp.reduce.async.bulk.global.shared::cta.bulk_group.add.f32` (SASS
`UBLKRED.G.S.ADD.F32.RN [URg], [URs], URn`) is the bulk store's asynchronous operation
(issuer's bulk group, URn 16-byte units, shared memory read by the bulk actor) with each f32
added to its global word as an atomic read-modify-write at GPU scope**: round to nearest,
subnormals kept (no flush, unlike `RED.ADD.F32.FTZ`), the canonical NaN 0x7fffffff, an
exact zero sum +0 unless both are -0. Concurrent bulk reductions of one word do not race;
their order is a schedule choice, and errdist records each word as an atomic add (the
summation order of FA4's dQ accumulation).
- Where: `exec.rs` `bulk_red_f32` (from `complete_tma_store`); `num.rs` `num_bulk_add`;
  `sass/src/l2.rs` (UBLKRED); `ptx/src/l2.rs` (`cp.reduce.async.bulk`).
- Status: **validated** on GB300 by `probes/bulk_red` (4096 edge / tie / random pairs; four
  CTAs reducing the same 1024 words, 20/20 runs identical; both front-ends bitwise,
  `probe_bulk_red_matches_hardware`), 2026-11-06. Atomicity per word under contention is
  observed (no lost update in the four-CTA region), not proven; other reduction ops and
  types are refused.
- Tensor reductions, `cp.reduce.async.bulk.tensor.<N>d...add.tile.bulk_group` (SASS
  `UTMAREDG.<N>D.ADD`), add each element in the tensor map's type the same way: f32 as above;
  f16 / bf16 round to nearest even, subnormals kept, NaN 0x7fff (`fp.rs` `add16`); other
  element types are unmodeled at run time. **Validated** by `probes/tma_red` (bf16, f16 and
  f32 tensors, every pair of 64 edge patterns each, both front-ends bitwise,
  `probe_tma_red_matches_hardware`), 2026-11-06. 16-bit sums are `AtomAdd16` nodes of the
  errdist graph, and two 16-bit bulk reductions of one element by different asynchronous
  operations, neither happening before the other, follow N-RED16 (until 2026-11-09 they were
  reported `unmodeled`: a single-order "clean" verdict once disagreed with the GPU,
  moe.scatter_add_along_first_dim with duplicate rows, where GB300 gives 92 distinct outputs in
  200 runs).
- If wrong: *miss* (a real race between bulk reductions and other writes is still
  reported; a lost-update hazard between two bulk reductions would not be) or a wrong
  errdist ordering.

### N-RED16 · code
**Two or more f16 / bf16 bulk reductions (`cp.reduce.async.bulk.tensor...add`, SASS
`UTMAREDG.<N>D.ADD`) of one element from asynchronous operations that do not happen before one
another leave the element at the result of some sequential order of the adds, each add one
round-to-nearest-even 16-bit rounding (N-BULK-RED's per-element rule). Which order is not
promised, per element.** Reductions from one thread in one bulk group were applied in issue
order on GB300, but no rule relies on that: unordered means any order.
- Verdict: the launch is `nondeterministic` (a `red16-order` finding for every such pair the
  exploration meets, whether or not the explored orders give different outputs, and the
  cross-cluster note as for N-ATOMIC), never "deterministic" or "clean". Within a box the
  explorer runs whole operations in either order; GB300 mixes orders per 128-byte chunk,
  which the bound covers (every element is some order of its own adds).
- Bound: each element's chain of S adds (start value plus S values) is an `AtomAdd16`
  chain. `equiv` and `out_rec` put every value under d roundings (d = S, or S - 1 when the start
  is +0: adding to +0 is exact), relative u = 2^-8 (bf16) / 2^-11 (f16) each, plus d absolute
  errors of 2^-134 / 2^-25 where a partial sum is subnormal. That is the worst case of any
  order, so the bound holds for every order and every per-chunk mixture. If (|start| + sum
  |values|) grown by d roundings could reach the format's overflow threshold, the form is
  untracked (no bound). A chain does not change format (`num_bulk_add16` restarts it at a
  constant or an opaque value); `equiv` reports one that did as unordered (not L0) rather than
  cutting it short. errdist's Tier 3 DAG adds in the simulator's order (N-ERRDIST-DAG),
  each add an f32 add then a 16-bit rounding (the same value: double rounding through 24
  bits is innocuous for a p <= 11-bit sum).
- Refused (`unmodeled`): unordered bulk reductions of different element types into
  overlapping bytes (f32 with 16-bit, or bf16 with f16), in one cluster or across clusters.
  Any other access of a reduced element by an unordered actor is a race as before.
- Where: `exec.rs` `bulk_red` (`red16`, `red_kind`), `num.rs` `num_bulk_add16` /
  `NodeKind::AtomAdd16` / `out_rec`, `equiv.rs`, `errdist/chain.rs`, `machine.rs` `GFoot`
  (per-kind reduction bitsets), `explore.rs` `explore_sliced`.
- Status: **validated** on GB300 by `probes/tma_red_order` (2026-11-09; per element (g, a0,
  a1) with the a0-first, a1-first and single-rounding sums three different bf16 words). In 300
  launches of two CTAs adding a 64 x 64 box each at once (after a cluster barrier), every
  element was one of the two orders, never the single rounding or anything else. Orders
  switched at 128-byte row boundaries, and every element was seen in both orders. One thread
  issuing both reductions back to back: issue order in 300 of 300 launches.
  `red16_order_bound_covers_gb300` checks the following, on both front-ends:
  - the verdict is `nondeterministic`;
  - every explored output element is one of the two GB300 values;
  - every observed value is inside the element's bound. The largest observed error is 0.82
    of the bound, against 1.0 for the worst element of the worst-case model;
  - a fused single rounding would put no element among the observed values;
  - a bound for the simulated order only is exceeded by observed values (10 elements).
- If wrong: *false proof* (an order or a rounding outside the bound) or a missed refusal.

### N-MUFU · code
**`MUFU.EX2/RCP/RSQ/LG2/SIN/COS/SQRT/TANH/RCP64H/RSQ64H` (f32, `.F16`, `.BF16`, `.F16x2`, `.BF16x2`) and
the PTX `ex2/rcp/rsqrt/lg2/sin/cos/sqrt/tanh.approx[.ftz]` (and `rcp/rsqrt.approx.ftz.f64`) ops are
modeled bit-exactly.** Each
unit is a 64- or 128-segment quadratic interpolator (truncated squarer, 26/16/10-14-bit
coefficient tables) reconstructed from the hardware's outputs; TANH is the same form per
input binade 2^-8..2^2 (51 segments on an input truncated to 17..21 mantissa bits); each PTX op is modeled as ptxas's expansion around the unit (probes/mufu/README.md).
- Where: `mufu.rs`, `mufu_tables.rs` (generated by probes/mufu/gen_tables.py from
  probes/mufu/fits), `sass` lowering of `MUFU.*`, `ptx` lowering of `*.approx`, `exec.rs`
  `Op::Mufu`; numerics: `num.rs` `NodeKind::Mufu` (error bound per op), `equiv.rs`
  (MUFU pseudo-leaves).
- Status: **validated** (2026-11-03, GB300 GPU 1, CUDA 13.0, driver 580). Every op was run on
  all 2^32 f32 inputs (16-bit forms: all 2^16; packed forms: all 2^32 lane pairs) and
  `ptxv mufu-sweep` found 0 differences from the model: `MUFU.EX2/RCP/RSQ/LG2/SQRT`
  (= the `.ftz` PTX ops), `MUFU.TANH` (= `tanh.approx.f32`), bare `MUFU.SIN/COS` (a patched cubin), `ex2/rcp/rsqrt/lg2/sqrt.approx.f32`
  (denormal expansions), `sin/cos.approx.f32`, `ex2.approx.f16/.ftz.bf16` and their x2
  forms, `tanh.approx.f16/bf16` lanes. Replay without a GPU: fixtures/mufu/samples.json
  (specials, 2^20 random inputs per op, every 16-bit input; the full 2^32 replay is an ignored
  test), fixtures/s_mufu (SASS) and probes/mufu/approx_ptx (PTX front-end) against recorded
  GB300 outputs, and the rung-4 softmax / layer_norm / rms_norm kernels (expected/).
- Error against the true function (f64 reference), maxima over the sweep, used as each MUFU
  node's error bound (|hw - f(x)| <= r ulp(f(x)) + a):
  - EX2 2.056 ulp; RCP 0.975 ulp; RSQ 1.515 ulp; SQRT 0.944 ulp (plus, for the `.ftz` forms,
    a = 2^-126 where a result flushes to 0, and 2^-63 for SQRT of a flushed denormal);
  - LG2 1 ulp + 2.62 * 2^-24 (a fixed-point unit; relative error is unbounded near x = 1);
  - bare SIN/COS (revolutions) 1 ulp + 5.46 * 2^-24; PTX `sin/cos.approx` (radians)
    (8 + 2.7 |x|) * 2^-24 for |x| <= 1024, no useful bound beyond;
  - TANH 134 ulp.
- **f64:** `MUFU.RCP64H/RSQ64H` (= `rcp/rsqrt.approx.ftz.f64`) are modeled bit-exactly: they read
  only the f64 high word, so all 2^32 high words were swept (0 differences); the mantissa is the
  f32 RCP/RSQ unit's, truncated to 20 bits. Bounds (f32 ulps of f(x), any low word): RCP64H
  16.6, RSQ64H 9.1. Replay: fixtures/mufu/samples.json, probes/mufu/f64_ptx (both fronts).
  The f64 sequences built on them (`div.rn.f64`, `sqrt.rn.f64`, `rsqrt.approx.f64`) still fail to
  lift (`DFMA` / `DMUL` / `DADD` / `DSETP` are not lowered; PTX `div/sqrt.rn.f64` neither).
- Other formats: not lowered.
- Bounds an output violates (MISS 206, defense in depth): where an analyzed element's error
  exceeds its Cor 1a or running bound, every element of the output reports that bound as unknown
  (N-NUM-NONFINITE, aggregates). probes/mufu_bound_top (GB300 == simulator bitwise, 20 of 20
  runs): PTX rcp.approx.f32 of 0x00200001 / 0x00200002 gives 0x7f7ffff8 / 0x7f7ffff0, where the
  printed bound was 2^-126 against |GB300 - 1/x| = 7.7e25 / 3.1e26 (the summary said
  cor1a_ok=false); now unknown.
- At the 16 largest finite magnitudes |hw| (1 + 2^-20) rounds to infinity in f32 and f(x) may lie
  at or above 2^128: the bound takes the spacing of the binade above FLT_MAX in an f32 format
  without an exponent limit, 2^105 (MISS 206, `mufu_local_bound`; until then ulp_f32 of infinity,
  2^-149, gave 2^-126). Of the modeled ops only PTX rcp.approx.f32 (no .ftz) reaches them, at
  the subnormals +-(2^-128 + 2^-149) and +-(2^-128 + 2^-148) (0x00200001 / 0x00200002 give
  0x7f7ffff8 / 0x7f7ffff0; ptxas's expansion scales a subnormal operand by 2^24): GB300, all 2^32
  operands of each of the 15 PTX f32 .approx ops (probes/mufu_range, re-measured on a second
  GB300 with the same records). ex2 with and without .ftz peaks at 0x7f7fffa8 (x = 128 - 2^-17),
  87 encodings below FLT_MAX, rcp.approx.ftz at 2^126, rsqrt at 0x64b504f2 (.ftz: 2^63), lg2,
  sqrt, sin, cos and tanh far below; the .ftz forms compile to the bare MUFU units (SIN / COS
  after FMUL.RZ by 1 / 2pi; the probe's SASS listing), so their rows are the SASS MUFU units' f32
  ranges [GB300 measured, exhaustive; ISA: SASS listing]. Until then the reach was argued from the
  ops' ranges. fixtures/c_num_mufu_top_f32
  (GB300 == simulator bitwise): bounds 3.96e31 at those two elements against |GB300 - 1/x| =
  7.7e25 / 3.1e26, every claimed element's bound above its GB300 error, cor1a_ok on the PTX front
  (`tests/num_untracked.rs` `mufu_bound_at_the_top_magnitudes_covers_gb300`, mutant mufu-top-ulp).
- PTX `.approx.ftz` results are one-instruction slices in `ptxv num` (`num_mufu`: the slice keeps
  the flush in its evaluation) and carry the same bound as a MUFU node, plus |f(x) - f(+-0)| where
  the flushed operand x is subnormal (MISS 207, `out_rec`; until then such a node was a plain term
  with no bound of its own, its operand's bounds not propagated, so `ptxv num` claimed bound 0).
  The swept bounds are those of the `.ftz` forms (MUFU = the `.ftz` PTX ops, above); the flush
  term matters for sqrt (0 against sqrt(x) up to 2^-63), the relative and absolute terms cover
  ex2, sin and cos of a subnormal. rcp of a subnormal, and rsqrt and lg2 of a positive one, are
  infinite against a finite exact value: an infinite error, so every bound of that element's own
  output is unknown (MISS 206's check, N-NUM-NONFINITE), while elements past an operation that
  maps the infinity to a finite value are analyzed with finite bounds, which covered the exact
  error in each of the independent review's 17 chains (through rcp, rsqrt, lg2, ex2, sqrt, sin,
  tanh, add, sub, min and max, positive subnormal operands) [model against exact values]. sqrt,
  rsqrt and lg2 of a negative subnormal have no real value:
  such an element is not analyzed (N-NUM-NONFINITE, MISS 258; until then num_mufu made up the
  exact value 0, probes/mufu_nan_exact). probes/mufu_ftz_bound
  (GB300 == simulator bitwise, 20 of 20 runs): the PTX
  front's bound was 0 at 35 of 38 claimed elements below their GB300 error (ex2.approx.ftz of

  and sqrt .approx.ftz, every result finite; GB300 == simulator bitwise): every claimed element's
  bound covers its GB300 error on both fronts (`tests/num_untracked.rs`

- If wrong: *miss* or *false alarm* in outputs and numerics of kernels using these ops (a

### N-MULTIMEM · code
**`multimem.ld_reduce` arithmetic.** Measured on GB300 (`probes/multimem/mm.cu` `ldr`, 4
GPUs, inputs: random bit patterns plus narrow-exponent, subnormal, zero, inf and NaN classes;
65536 16-byte vectors per type; `analyze.py`):
- results are bitwise identical whichever GPU issues the load, across 4 repetitions, across
  processes, and when the member-to-GPU mapping is permuted: the reduction is a symmetric
  function of the members, not schedule-dependent;
- integers (`add` 32 / 64 bit, `min.s32`, `max.u32`, `xor`): exact (262144 lanes each);
- `f32` add (scalar, `.v4`, `.weak`; MISS 225, 2026-11-12): each operand truncated toward zero
  to a multiple of 2^(16 floor(eB / 16) - 207), eB the largest operand's biased exponent (a
  window aligned to 16 binades, 57 to 72 bits below the largest operand's last mantissa bit),
  the truncated values summed exactly; a sum whose leading bit lies below
  2^(16 floor(eB / 16) - 198) is +0, any other sum is rounded to nearest even, subnormals kept;
  a sum of zeros is +0, every member -0 included (2 and 4 members). GB300 (`mm ldr`, outputs
  identical from every issuing GPU and repetition) matches it on every modeled lane of three
  random sweeps (mm's own fill, MM_SEED 1, 2, 3: 2359296 lanes of add.f32, add.f32 .weak and
  add.v4.f32; 1534 with several distinct NaNs are not modeled), of a cancellation sweep
  (B, -B, R, 0 with R 16 to 72 binades below B, eB 40 to 230: 3450 lanes each of add.f32 and
  add.v4.f32), of the zero lanes and of the 2026-11-06 sample (`results/ldr`). Until MISS 225
  the model kept 63 bits below the largest operand's last mantissa bit, with no flush, and gave
  -0 for all -0 members: it differed from GB300 on 524 of the random lanes, on 425 of each
  form's 3450 cancellation lanes (80 of them with no operand bit below its window, 3 where
  GB300 gave +0) and on every all -0 lane (probes/multimem_f32_window, which replays them;
  `crates/sim/tests/multimem.rs` `f32_sums_follow_the_window_sweeps` replays its lanes and the
  sweeps' cancellation and zero lanes; mutants mm-f32-window and mm-f32-flush caught).
  Lanes where some operand bit falls below the window are still reported `inexact` (the
  simulator does not use the flag: every lane's value is taken as GB300's). Earlier fits: no
  fixed window (0 to 136 bits) and no window with sticky bits is exact; the plain exact sum
  misses 3 to 16 of 4000 sampled lanes; no fixed summation order (24 folds, 3 trees, with or
  without FTZ) fits;
- `f16` / `bf16` `min` / `max`: IEEE minNum / maxNum (NaN operands ignored, -0 < +0), 524288
  lanes each, 0 mismatches;
- NaN in an add: the result is one of the NaN operands, quieted (with two different NaNs not
  always the first; not modeled); inf + -inf: the canonical NaN (`0x7fc00000`, `0x7fc0`);
- f16 / bf16 add (with and without `.acc::f32`; MISS 208, 2026-11-12): each operand truncated
  toward zero 63 bits below the largest operand's last mantissa bit (the former f32 window), the
  truncated values summed exactly; a sum whose leading bit lies below
  2^(16 floor(eB / 16) - 23 - bias) (eB: the largest member's biased exponent; bias 15 / 127)
  is +0, and no member is dropped (members below that bound are kept when the sum is above it:
  bf16 1338 of 1338 lanes, f16 45 of 45); a sum of zeros is +0, every member -0 included (2 and
  4 members). GB300 (`mm ldr` with MM_IN): every eB of both formats with 4 members
  (cancellations B - B + R with R around the bound; pairs R1 + R1 2^-6 with R1 above it and
  R1 2^-6 below it); with 2 members no sum is that small. Until MISS 208 the model kept such
  sums and gave -0 for all -0 members (probes/multimem_add16_rules: 629 and 680 bf16 lanes of
  the 4-member vectors, the 13 random-sweep lanes where GB300 gave 0, every all -0 lane).
  `crates/sim/tests/multimem.rs` `half_sums_follow_the_flush_sweeps` replays the sweeps
  (probes/multimem_add16_rules/sweep; gen1.py and gen2.py write their inputs); mutants
  mm-zero-sign, mm-half-flush and mm-align16 caught. Rounding of the kept sums:
  N-MULTIMEM-ROUND16. `f64`, fp8 (`e4m3`, `e5m2`) and f16 overflow: not modeled
  (`unmodeled`).
- `.acc`: `.acc::f32` on 16-bit float `ld_reduce` adds is accepted and changes no modeled value
  (the measured results are the same with and without it, N-MULTIMEM-ROUND16; the simulator
  ignores the flag). `.acc::f16` (PTX ISA 9.5 section 9.7.10.15: an f16 accumulator, for the
  fp8 types) and `.acc` on any other op or type are refused (MISS 25, 2026-11-09); before,
  `.acc::f16` was lowered as `.acc::f32`. That reached no wrong verdict (argued from code and
  ptxas 13.0 / 13.3, 2026-11-10): an fp8 `ld_reduce` add is `unmodeled` at run time
  (`multimem::reduce`), and on `ld_reduce` ptxas rejects `.acc::f16` on f16x2 / bf16x2 / f32
  and `.acc::f32` on f32, fp8 or `min`. `red` and `st` accept `.acc::f32` and `.acc::f16` on
  u32, f16x2, bf16x2 and f32 and assemble them to the same REDG / STG as without it
  (2026-11-11), so their refusal is a precision loss. Corrected 2026-11-11: this said ptxas
  rejects `.acc` on f16x2 / bf16x2 / f32; that holds for `ld_reduce` only. GB300 fp8 accumulation is not
  measured: kernel_db's only `.acc` uses are `ld_reduce ... add.acc::f32.v4.bf16x2` (6 PTX files,
  still accepted).
- Status: **validated** for the items listed (f32: bitwise on every recorded lane since
  MISS 225); `crates/sim/tests/multimem.rs` replays a sample of the recorded lanes

### N-MULTIMEM-ROUND16 · code
**f16 / bf16 `multimem.ld_reduce` add rounding.** The result is always one of the two
neighbours of the sum (all random lanes), with or without `.acc::f32`, but not the
nearest-even one in 3% (bf16) / 20% (f16) of random lanes. The direction depends on the other
lanes of the 8-byte group: controlled sweeps (`mm sr3`, `results/sr3`) give "up" exactly when
frac + r >= 1, with frac the sum's position between the neighbours and r the truncated
mantissas of lanes l+1, l+2, l+3 (mod 4 in the group) interleaved most significant bit first;
with every other lane zero the sum is truncated. The rule reproduces 99.7% of non-representable
random bf16 lanes and 96.7% of f16 lanes; misses include groups with a NaN lane.
- Model: `add16` applies the rule and reports each lane it rounds (`Reduced.calibrated`). Only
  output bytes that hold such a lane may differ from the captured GPU bytes by one unit in the
  last place. For a case with `[[multicast]]` objects, `ptxv check` runs one deterministic
  schedule more (`explore::run_once`) with provenance on (`Machine::round16`,
  `multimem::Round16Shadow`): the ld_reduce puts each rounded lane, with its format and the side
  of its other rounding (`Round16`: the next or the previous encoding), into its
  destination register; a register move copies it; a store writes it into memory (into every
  location a multicast store reaches); any other write of the register or of the bytes ends it,
  and a load does not carry it. A terminal output equal byte for byte to that run's output is
  compared with the tolerance on those bytes: each differing element must be a pair of adjacent
  finite encodings of the buffer's dtype (`ulp_class`; a NaN on either side never is, NaN
  against a NaN with another payload included) with every byte holding a lane of that dtype, and
  the captured value the other rounding of the lane's sum (the model's: the operands truncated
  to its window, then added exactly), on the side its mark gives: the encoding past the
  simulated value, away from that sum, is no rounding of it (MISS 162; until then either
  neighbour passed); any other difference is a mismatch (`gpu_compare` `mismatch`), and any
  other terminal output
  is compared bitwise (`Case::expect_compare_tol`, `Round16`; `PTXV_RUN_ONCE` uses the marks of
  its own run, and `ptxv equiv`'s check of each kernel's simulated output against its capture,
  MISS 98's `sim_gpu_mismatch`, those of its numerics run, tracked for such cases). Until
  2026-11-11 the tolerance covered every output of a case with `[[multicast]]` objects, so an
  f32 sum one ulp off, data computed from a rounded lane and a lane overwritten by other data
  passed too, and `ulp_class` passed NaN against a NaN with
  another payload (MISS 110; `gpu_compare` counted them `within_ulp`, no match). The marks come
  from one schedule: where schedules differ (a race or divergent verdict, never clean), another
  schedule's output with the same bytes is compared with them [argued]. Adjacency alone puts
  +-inf next to +-max, a NaN next to inf and the largest NaN encoding (0x7fffffff, the GPU's
  canonical f32 NaN) next to -0, so until 2026-11-11 an overflow or a NaN on either side could
  pass as one ulp (MISS 67). Unit tests (`ptxv-case` `one_ulp_tolerance_needs_finite_values`,
  `expect_report_tol_never_crosses_an_infinity`) cover f32, bf16 and f16, both signs, including
  -inf against -max, NaN payloads, unmarked bytes and the other 16-bit format.
  fixtures/r1h_nvls_inf (expected/ constructed, not captured): before MISS 67, both outputs
  within one ulp (2 of 4 elements) on both fronts; after, MISMATCH. Mutant ulp-tol-nonfinite
  (the plain bit-difference test) caught. The route on real hardware is argued: rounding up at
  the top binade overflows to inf where rounding down keeps the largest finite value [argued].
  MISS 110: `crates/cli/tests/gpu_compare.rs` `only_calibrated_bf16_lanes_are_within_one_ulp`
  (fixtures/r1h_nvls_bf16, captured outputs written from the simulated ones with one element
  one encoding up, both fronts): within one ulp only in the rounded lanes of the output stored
  as reduced and of the one broadcast by `multimem.st`; a mismatch in an exact lane, in the pair
  doubled in its register and in the pair overwritten by an exchange. `review_probes_are_mismatches`:
  fixtures/r1h_nvls_ulp and r1h_nvls_nan (expected/ constructed) mismatch on both fronts
  (before, within one ulp); in `ptxv equiv` (`crates/cli/tests/equiv.rs`
  `multimem_probes_differ_from_their_captures`, fixtures/c_equiv_round16) both differ from
  their captures on both fronts (before, neither difference was reported); an exact lane of
  fixtures/r1h_nvls_bf16 one encoding off a capture written from the simulated output
  (`exact_multimem_lane_one_ulp_off_differs_from_its_capture`) differs on both fronts, which
  pins the marks `sim_gpu_mismatch` takes from the numerics run. Mutants round16-* caught
  (tools/mutate/srcmut.py; round16-equiv-fab, every byte taken as a calibrated bf16 lane in
  equiv, only by the exact-lane test). MISS 162: in the recorded GB300 sweeps

  mark gives (bf16x8 9 of 4096 lanes, bf16x8a 9 of 4088, f16x8 112 of 3688, f16x8a 93 of 3712)
  [GB300 measured, recorded]. `crates/cli/tests/gpu_compare.rs`

  on the new marks.
  kernel_db (MISS 162; f16 / bf16 multimem ld_reduce in 4 of the 1311 case directories,
  LDGMC.E.HPADD.BF16x8 in dg_cute_fused_w2 / w4 and dg_cute_multimem_w2 / w4): in PTXV_RUN_ONCE
  of each with and without MISS 162 every output is bitwise equal to its captured GPU output, so the

  Evidence [model]: GB300 multicast runs are not available
  to the hardware runner, so no captured output exists for these fixtures.
- Status: **unvalidated** (partial fit).
- Where: `crates/sim/src/multimem.rs` `add16`, `Round16Shadow` (hooks in exec.rs `wr`,

### N-MMA · code
**One `tcgen05.mma.kind::f16` (bf16 × bf16 → f32) step is
`g16-f25-rz-accin-tzero-einputs`.**
- Where: `fp.rs` `DEFAULT_MMA`, `exec.rs` `complete_mma`.
- Status: **validated, and enforced at its edges.** It is the unique match of 820 candidates
  on 49,152 GB300 outputs (docs/rung1a.md). That calibration covers finite normal inputs only;
  subnormal/Inf/NaN f16 / bf16 inputs and f32 accumulators follow N-MMA-SPECIAL (tf32 ones,
  scaled accumulators and non-default models give `unmodeled`). f16 and tf32 operands: below;
  other formats (f16 D, mixed A / B) are rejected by the idesc check; the narrow kinds are N-MMA-F8 / N-MMA-BS. Shapes (PTX ISA table 48, the
  layouts in S-TMEM / E-PAIR): `cta_group::1` M = 64 or 128 with N = 8..256 in steps of 8
  (M = 128 N % 16 != 0 only with A in shared memory, and with block scaling only N = 8:
  measured forms), `cta_group::2` M = 128 or 256 with N = 16..256 in steps of 16; anything else is
  `unmodeled`. The arithmetic does not depend on N or the layout: `probes/tc_m128` random-operand
  configs (M = 128 N = 8 / 24, pairs N = 32 / 64 / 256, e4m3 for N-MMA-F8) equal the model
  bitwise.
- **scale-input-d** (2026-11-08; `tcgen05.mma ..., enable_input_d, s`, SASS `UTCHMMA ...,
  UPd, s`, s = 1..15, kind::f16 / kind::tf32 only): D = A B + D * 2^-s is the same step with
  the accumulator D * 2^-s, exact. `probes/mma_scale_d` (bf16 and tf32, s = 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8,
  9, 12, 15, twice in a row, and with enable-input-d = 0) = the model bitwise on 32,768 GB300
  outputs per input set, 9 random input sets (one committed). Accumulators whose scaled value
  is not a normal f32 or zero are `unmodeled`. GB300 truncates a value that falls below 2^-126
  (toward zero, e.g. 0x807fffff * 2^-1 = 0x803fffff), -0 gives +0, NaN gives 0x7fffffff and Inf
  stays Inf; this was measured on data/C_special inputs (gen.py) but is not modeled. The
  numerics shadow restarts a scaled accumulator cell as a leaf, with a warning when its old
  node carried rounding error (`num_tmem_rescale`). Other kinds with a scale are refused. Both
  front-ends lower it (the PTX front since 2026-11-08); `probes/mma_scale_d` is bitwise on both.
- **f16 and tf32 operands** (2026-11-07): kind::f16 with f16 A / B (instruction descriptor
  format 0) is the same model over 16 products (unique match of 820 candidates, `ptxv
  calib-mma probes/tc_f16`, 6 input sets / 49,152 GB300 outputs; f16 subnormal inputs:
  N-MMA-SPECIAL); kind::tf32 (format 2; PTX `kind::tf32` = SASS `UTCHMMA` with that descriptor)
  is `g8-f25-rz-accin-tzero-einputs` over 8 products with the low 13 mantissa bits of each f32
  word dropped, as `mma.sync` tf32 (N-HMMA; unique with g16 among 2,460 model x conversion
  candidates, `ptxv calib-mma probes/tc_tf32`, 49,152 outputs). A tf32 K slice is 8 elements of
  4 bytes (16-byte core-matrix rows of 4), A in TMEM one element per column. MN-major tf32
  (idesc bit 15 / 16; KA: MHCRoutingBackwardStream, idesc 0x8088910) is read only through
  smem descriptor layout 1, SWIZZLE_128B_BASE32B: element (r, k) at swz32(start + (r % 32) 4 +
  (k % 4) 128 + (r / 32) LBO + (k / 4) SBO), swz32(a) = a ^ (((a >> 7) & 3) << 5) (4-row
  atoms of 128 bytes, 32-byte granules); GB300 returned all zeros for MN-major tf32 through
  layouts 0 / 2 / 4 / 6, which stay refused, as does layout 1 anywhere else (K-major,
  16-bit, tcgen05.cp, narrow kinds). probes/tc_tf32_mn (A MN-major, then B MN-major; layout
  recovered by solving each D row for the elements read): GB300 20/20, both front-ends
  bitwise (2026-11-07). probes/tc_f16 and probes/tc_tf32 (D[128x64], 4 / 8 MMAs) are
  bitwise = GB300 on both front-ends (50/50 scrubbed), and probes/mma_zero's kind::f16 f16 and
  kind::tf32 configs (signed zeros, subnormal results) now replay bitwise too.
- **Finite overflow** (2026-11-07): a step whose truncated sum is 2^128 or more gives Inf of
  its sign, not FLT_MAX as a literal round toward zero would (`sum_round_terms`, all models).
  probes/tc_mma_ovf (kind::f16 bf16, inputs of magnitude 2^[58, 65)): 1,647 Inf words on
  GB300; the earlier model gave FLT_MAX there under a `clean` verdict (4,938 bytes differed).
  Both front-ends now bitwise, 20/20 scrubbed; HMMA likewise (N-HMMA, probes/hmma_special).
- **Error contract** used by numerics and equivalence (`MmaModel::eps_terms`, docs/equiv-mma.md
  §1). A step adding n terms (products and the accumulator) satisfies |computed - sum| <=
  ((n - 1) 2^-25 + 2^-23 (1 + (n - 1) 2^-25)) sum |terms|, which is about 10u for n = 17. It
  follows from the model: every alignment exponent e has 2^e <= |term|; the term at emax is
  exact (at most 24 significant bits <= 26); each other term loses < 2^(emax - 25); the final
  rounding is toward zero. MMA steps are `NodeKind::Mma` nodes (`num_mma`), whose operands are
  any tracked values (input elements, or bf16 roundings of computed nodes: N-ROUND, N-HALF-LEAF).
  An f32 result below the normal range is rounded toward zero, less than 2^-149 off. The
  canonical forms add that to the absolute part of every MMA step (the relative contract
  alone does not cover it).
- **Signed zeros: every zero result is +0** (validated, `probes/mma_zero`, GB300, CUDA 13.0,
  2026-11-05). It holds whether the sum is exactly zero (all products ±0, also all -0 with
  C = -0; exact cancellation) or a nonzero sum below 2^-149 that rounds to zero (one product
  or a cancellation residue, either sign), with C disabled, C = +0 or C = -0. Subnormal
  results keep their sign. Measured on tcgen05 kind::f16 (bf16 M128 / M64, f16 M128),
  kind::tf32, kind::f8f6f4 (e4m3, e2m1; f32 and f16 D), mma.sync m16n8k16 bf16 / f16 and
  m16n8k8 tf32 (C from registers and RZ). Before 2026-11-05 the models followed IEEE
  (-0 for an underflowing negative sum, or when every term was -0), which differed from
  GB300 on up to 12% of a probe config's outputs (all -0 vs +0) and in the reported case
  (witness: K = 16, one product bf16 0x16b2 x 0x96e5 = -40762 * 2^-178, GB300 +0). Where: `fp.rs`
  `round_int_to_f32` / `sum_round_*`, `mma_lp.rs` `round_int` / `sum_round` / `round_exact` /
  `Fp4Model::step`, `errdist/chain.rs` `step`; `crates/sim/tests/mma_zero.rs` replays the
  probe bitwise (both front-ends for tcgen05, SASS for mma.sync).
- **Overflow is signed infinity, including with RZ mantissa rounding** (validated,
  `probes/mma_overflow`, GB300 SM103, driver 580.126.20, ptxas 13.1.115, 2026-11-06).
  One BF16 product `0x7f00 * 0x4000` is exactly 2^128 and gives `0x7f800000`; the
  negative case gives `0xff800000`. Products are not individually clamped to FP32:
  2^128 - 2^127 gives 2^127, and 2^254 - 2^254 gives +0. Alignment can itself cross the
  overflow boundary: 2^128 - 2^102 gives infinity, while 2^128 - 2^103 gives the largest
  finite float. All inputs and input accumulators in this probe are normal or zero.
  Six configurations cover BF16 tcgen05 M128 N16 K16, BF16 HMMA, and TF32 HMMA, with
  accumulation enabled and disabled. Before this fix, `fp::round_int_to_f32` saturated
  RZ overflow to the largest finite float; the full simulator differed on 95,744 of
  243,712 replayed words. The corrected model matches all eight PTX/SASS replays.
  This does not extend the numerical error bounds to overflowing computations or
  establish the overflow behavior of the separate narrow-format models.

### N-MMA-SPECIAL · code
**`tcgen05.mma.kind::f16` (f32 D) on subnormal, Inf and NaN f16 / bf16 operands and f32
accumulators is N-HMMA's special-value step** (`fp.rs` `mma_special_step`, `exec.rs`
`complete_mma`): subnormal operands are exact and align at their format's smallest normal
exponent (f16 -14, bf16 -126; the exponent field's minimum, not the true exponent), subnormal
accumulators at -126; subnormal results are kept (round toward zero); a NaN operand (any
payload, either sign), Inf * 0 or Inf - Inf gives 0x7fffffff; otherwise an Inf product or
accumulator gives that Inf; a finite sum of 2^128 or more gives Inf of its sign. A step with no
special value is N-MMA unchanged. Before (2026-11-09), every such MMA was `unmodeled`: the
INT4-KV attention kernels' f16 P x V MMAs (softmax probabilities below 2^-14) stopped there.
- Evidence: `probes/tc_special` (2026-11-09, GB300): probes/tc_f16's kernel (4 MMAs of K = 16,
  the first overwriting D, so MMAs 1-3 read the special results of earlier ones as
  accumulators) on 17 input sets (gen.py; f16: sub_alone, sub_mixed, sub_align, sub_rand,
  infnan_in, sub_inf, acc_special; bf16 also res_sub, acc_sub, overflow), 139,264 outputs.
  - Three evidence classes: (1) an exact-arithmetic Python scorer of 64 model variants (flush
    subnormal inputs / accumulators / results, true or field-minimum subnormal exponent, NaN
    0x7fffffff or 0x7fc00000, overflow to Inf or FLT_MAX) on the GB300 outputs: only this
    variant matches all 139,264; every dimension is decided by at least one set (the f16
    subnormal exponent by f16_sub_align, the accumulator / result flushes by the bf16 sets,
    since f16 operands cannot produce f32 subnormals; the accumulator path is the f32 one for
    both formats). (2) ptxv itself, both front-ends: bitwise on all 17 sets
    (`probe_tc_special_matches_hardware`). (3) `ptxv hw --runs 50 --scrub` per set: 50/50
    runs bitwise equal to the simulator.
  - Gaps: the sub_inf sets mostly multiply Inf by zero elements (NaN everywhere); subnormal x
    Inf is decided by infnan_in instead. N = 64, M = 128, cta_group::1 only (the arithmetic
    does not depend on the shape, N-MMA). kind::tf32 special values, f16 D, scale-input-d
    with special accumulators and the narrow kinds (N-MMA-F8: non-finite inputs) stay
    `unmodeled`.
- Numerics: a special step's outputs drop their nodes (`num_tmem_forget`), as N-HMMA.
- Status: **validated** (the measured forms above).
- If wrong: *miss* of a wrong output value on special inputs.
