### N-IMMA · code
**`IMMA.16832.S8.S8.SAT` (`mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.satfinite.s32.s8.s8.s32`) is
D = sat_s32(C + Σ_{k<32} A[m][k] B[k][n]) in exact integers.** Fragments as in the PTX ISA
(g = lane / 4, t = lane % 4): a_j byte i = A[g + 8 (j & 1)][4 t + i + 16 (j >> 1)], b_j byte
i = B[4 t + i + 16 j][g], c_j / d_j = [g + 8 (j >> 1)][2 t + (j & 1)].
- Where: `exec.rs` `imma_s8` (`Op::Hmma { s8: true }`); the PTX front lowers only this
  `mma.sync` integer shape, the SASS front only `IMMA.16832.S8.S8.SAT` (other IMMA modifiers
  are outside modset.rs and refused).
- Status: **validated**: probes/imma_s8 (one warp, 4 chained steps, 512 outputs: random
  bytes, all -128 x -128, -128 x 127, C within 2^19 of both s32 limits; 9 outputs saturate at
  INT32_MAX and 24 at INT32_MIN, later steps start from saturated C) is bitwise equal to
  GB300 on both front-ends (50/50 scrubbed runs, 2026-11-07). On the same inputs a wrapping
  sum differs from GB300 on 87 outputs, a clamp after each product (k order) on 36.

### N-TF32 · code
**TF32 operands and the 3xTF32 split (`num.rs` `NodeKind::Tf32`, `equiv.rs` `tf32_chain`;
docs/equiv-mma.md §6).** For an f32 value x (a node's hardware value):
- hi(x) = x with the low 13 mantissa bits cleared. Nodes: a TF32 MMA operand read from a
  tracked register (the MMA truncates it, N-HMMA), and a `LOP3` whose LUT computes x & 0xffffe000
  bit for bit from one tracked register and input-independent operands. For x zero or normal,
  |hi(x) - x| < 2^-10 |x|: in the canonical forms one rounding node of unit 2^-10.
- lo(x) = x - hi(x): `FADD d, x, -h` (round to nearest, no other modifier) with h = hi of the
  same node. Exact: x and hi(x) share sign and exponent, so the difference is x's dropped bits
  (checked against the result). |lo(x)| < 2^-10 |x| for x normal.
- lo'(x): CUTLASS's round_half_ulp_truncate, the bits of lo(x) plus an input-independent
  0x1000 (`IMAD s, 1, k`, `LEA s, k, 0`), truncated by the MMA. That is lo(x) rounded half
  away from zero to 11 significant bits (a carry into the exponent is the correct rounding):
  |lo' - lo| <= 2^-11 |lo| for lo normal. lo(x) read by the MMA unrounded: <= 2^-10 |lo|.
- A step's products and accumulator follow N-MMA's contract with the TF32 model (`TMMA_MODEL`,
  n = 9 terms, about 6u): its derivation needs significand products of at most 26 bits, and a
  TF32 product has 22.
- 3xTF32: along one MMA accumulator chain (each step's value a term of the next, coefficient
  1), a product hi(a) hi(b) with one lo'(a) hi(b) and one hi(a) lo'(b), a and b equal canonical
  forms, is one term a b (1 + theta):
  hi_a hi_b + lo'_a hi_b + hi_a lo'_b - a b = (lo'_a - lo_a) hi_b + hi_a (lo'_b - lo_b) - lo_a lo_b,
  so |theta| <= 2^-20 + 2^-10 (d_a + d_b) (2^-19 for CUTLASS's split). Below the last of the
  three steps the products are rounded separately: |t1| + |t2| + |t3| <= (1 + w_a + w_b) |a b|,
  w = 2^-10 (1 + d), under those steps' growth h; the term enters at the last step with
  multiplier theta + (1 + w_a + w_b)(h - 1). An unmatched hi * hi product is hi(a) hi(b); an
  unmatched correction is untracked (no proof).
- Requirement: every value read as a TF32 operand or split is 0 or at least 2^-103 in
  magnitude. Then hi and lo are normal or zero (lo is a multiple of x's f32 ulp >= 2^-126), the
  relative bounds hold, and the MMA's operands are in N-HMMA's calibrated domain. Reported as a
  `condition:` of the bound.
- Where: `num.rs` (`num_tf32_hi`, `num_tf32_lo`, `num_tf32_lor`, `tf32_factor`, `num_hmma`),
  `exec.rs` (`Op::Lop3`, `Op::Fadd`, `Op::Imad`, `Op::Lea`, `hmma_tf32`), `equiv.rs`
  (`NodeKind::Tf32`, `tf32_chain`).
- Status: **argued.** theta is checked on 2,000,000 random pairs (exponents 2^-103 and up,
  mantissas at the rounding boundaries; `tf32_split_theta_holds`: within the bound, the worst
  above a quarter of it). Evidence: fixtures/c_equiv_tf32 (3xTF32 and 1xTF32 GEMMs against an
  f32 SIMT GEMM): L1, 239.31u / 183.42u (3xTF32) and 32895.59u (1xTF32) times sum |a_ik b_kj|;
  20 simulator trials each, at most 0.20 / 0.40 of the bound used.
- If wrong: *false proof* of a tolerance.

### N-FINITE · code
**A comparison of a value that finite inputs keep finite with an input-independent infinity or
NaN has the same outcome for every input with finite elements on which no operation
overflows (a taint precondition relaxation, `ptxv equiv`).** `num_fin_setp`: an `FSETP` (any
comparison, modifiers, combining predicate) whose one tainted operand is a node `fin` proves
finite, whose other operand is input-independent and not finite (+-inf, NaN), and whose
combining predicate and guard are input-independent, writes an input-independent predicate (its
taint is cleared). Typical: `FSETP.NE.AND P, PT, |x|, +INF, PT` = isfinite(x) (CUTLASS's TF32
small-part rounding), a comparison with a running maximum's -inf start.
- `fin`: input leaves; constants (leaves of input-independent values) that are finite; sums,
  FMAs, MMA steps (every product tracked), 16-bit roundings, `MUFU.EX2/TANH/SIN/COS` and TF32
  parts of `fin` nodes; a max (min) of `fin` nodes, or of one and a constant other than +inf
  (-inf). Not: untracked values, MUFU.RCP/RSQ/LG2/SQRT (finite arguments can give an
  infinity or NaN).
- Slices (`seg_val`, 2026-11-04): each slice value is abstracted as finite, one constant (an
  infinity allowed), or unknown, for admissible inputs: arguments that are `fin` are finite;
  an operation whose sources are all constants is evaluated (exec.rs's semantics); FADD / FFMA
  (FMUL) / FMNMX / FSEL / SEL / MOV / IMAD.MOV / MUFU.EX2, TANH, SIN, COS of finite values and
  finite constants are finite (FMNMX: or its identity infinity); an FADD of an infinity and a
  finite value is that infinity (exact in every rounding mode; .SAT clamps it to a constant);
  a selection or `Guard` by a constant predicate is the chosen value, otherwise the join; all
  else is unknown, which only predicates may consume. A slice is `fin` when its value is
  finite or a finite constant: online softmax's masked exponential exp2(-inf - mi) is the
  constant 0. A slice without arguments is one value for every input. Test
  `infinity_minus_finite_is_fixed` (negatives: an unknown argument, -inf times a finite value,
  a selection by an unknown predicate).
- An HMMA accumulator operand RZ is the input-independent constant 0 (it was an unmarked
  leaf, so MMA chains starting from zero were not `fin`).
- Argument: take an admissible input (finite elements, no operation of the dataflow DAG
  rounding a finite exact result to an infinity) and the first instruction where its execution
  would leave the captured trace. Up to there every node's value is the DAG's at that input, so
  by induction over the DAG every `fin` node is finite (finite operands give finite results
  unless an operation overflows). Comparing a finite value with an infinity or NaN does not
  depend on the finite value, so a relaxed comparison decides as captured, and every other
  guard, branch and address is untainted: no instruction leaves the trace. Hence the captured
  dataflow is every admissible input's.
- The verdict lists "relies on: N-FINITE (...)": the proof is for admissible inputs only. The
  numerics' bounds already assume them (N-REASSOC: no overflow; N-SOFTMAX: finite inputs).
- A value level that reads a select or FMNMX.NAN maximum of `fin` operands as the maximum of
  the values, or drops an FMNMX's identity infinity, relies on it too (N-EQUIV, MISS 197, 202):
  the verdict lists it with the count of such outputs.
- Negative tests: fixtures/c_equiv_tf32/neg.toml (a sign test `small > 0` of the split, and
  `isfinite` of the float whose bits are x's shifted left) still report data-dependent guards.
- Where: `num.rs` (`fin`, `num_fin_setp`, `taint_post`), `exec.rs` (`Op::Fsetp`),
  `cli/src/equiv.rs` (`prepare`).
- Status: **argued.**
- If wrong: *false proof* (a relaxed guard that decides otherwise for some admissible input).

### N-FMAX · code
**CUTLASS's float atomic max (`atomicMaxFloat`) is one float maximum whichever side its
branch takes (a taint precondition relaxation, `ptxv equiv`).** `num.rs` `fmax_diamond`
recognizes: `ISETP.GE.AND P, PT, v, RZ, PT` (or `.GT ... v, -0x1`), straight-line (no write
of P or v, no branch target) to `@[!]P BRA T`; the fall-through `ATOMS.MAX.S32 RZ, [a], v` or
`ATOMS.MIN RZ, [a], v` (unsigned), `BRA J`, the other at T, J right after it; the signed max
where v's sign bit is clear, the unsigned min where it is set. `fmax_seq` recognizes the
sequential form (CuTeDSL's `smem_fmax`, FA4 decode): `@P BRA A1; ATOMS.MIN RZ, [a], v; A1:`,
then only `NOP` / `BSYNC` / `BSSY`, then `@!P BRA A2; ATOMS.MAX.S32 RZ, [a], v; A2:`, with the
same sign test on P; exactly one atomic executes. Its data-dependent branches are not
violations; each of its atomics makes the shared word's node `Max(old, v)`.
- Argument: for non-NaN float bit patterns L (the word) and v: if v's sign bit is clear, every
  L with the sign bit set is a negative signed integer below v (and a float below or equal:
  -0 < +0), and non-negative floats order as signed integers; if v's sign bit is set, every L
  with the sign bit clear is an unsigned integer below v and a float above it, and negative
  floats order inversely to their unsigned bits. So either side writes max(L, v) in N-FALU's
  `FMNMX` order (-inf < ... < -0 < +0 < ... < +inf), exactly. Both sides access the same 4
  bytes atomically, with the same footprint (race verdicts unchanged), and the maximum is
  commutative and associative, so any order of the atomics gives the maximum of all values.
  The other input's path changes no register (RZ destinations) and joins immediately.
- Checked per atomic (else a violation): the word's previous value and v are non-NaN for every
  admissible input (an input-independent non-NaN constant, or `fin`, N-FINITE), and the result
  is the float maximum. The proof therefore holds for inputs with finite elements and no
  overflow ("relies on: N-FMAX").
- Negative test: fixtures/c_equiv_fmax `c_fmax_atomic_bad` (the choice made by `v > 0.5`)
  still reports its data-dependent branch.
- The first atomic of a word takes its old value as a constant when this thread's read found
  no input-derived bytes (it was the whole instruction's read: a later lane on another word saw
  an earlier lane's write). Slices cross the diamond (N-SEG): its sides write no register.
- Where: `num.rs` (`fmax_diamond`, `taint_pre`, `num_fmax_atom`), `exec.rs` (`Op::Atom`),
  `cli/src/equiv.rs` (`prepare`).
- Status: **argued.** Evidence: fixtures/c_equiv_fmax (row maxima through atomicMaxFloat into
  shared memory against a sequential fmaxf): L0.
- If wrong: *false proof*.

### N-ROUND · code
**A bf16 (f16) rounding of a computed f32 value is round-to-nearest-even: |rnd(x) - x| <=
2^-8 |x| (2^-11 |x|), plus 2^-134 (2^-25) absolute where the result is subnormal; f16 overflow
is outside the bound.** This covers `F2FP.BF16.F32.PACK_AB`, `F2FP.F16.F32.PACK_AB` and
`F2F.F16.F32` of a computed value (P before P.V in flash attention; PTX `cvt.rn.bf16.f32` /
`cvt.rn.f16.f32`) and the 16-bit rounding of an output before it is stored. These are
`NodeKind::Round { f16 }` nodes. Their bytes carry `N{node, b}` provenance, so the 16-bit
halves can be MMA operands (bf16 only: f16 nodes are marked) or outputs.
- In the canonical forms, the argument's multipliers grow by u16. In the weighted normal form
  (N-ATTN), every term record widens by (1 +- 2^-8). Every rounding node carries its operands'
  absolute parts through, times (1 + eps), and an FMA scales them by |k| when the other factor
  is an exact constant k.
- Outputs that are roundings to one 16-bit format of L1-equal values compare in the 16-bit
  output form (docs/equiv-mma.md §2). With each kernel's Cor 1a bound G_K(x) before the
  rounding, rounding is monotone, so |C - R| <= max(rnd(y + G_C) - rnd(y - G_R), rnd(y + G_R) -
  rnd(y - G_C)) (`round16_gap`: per input, y and G in f64 widened by 2^-49). For every input,
  |C - R| <= 2 u16 |y| + (1 + u16) sum_m |x_m| (g_R,m + g_C,m) + (1 + u16)(A_R + A_C) + 2 a16.
  C and R are equal or adjacent 16-bit values where (G_R + G_C)(1 + h) < h |y|, h = u16 / 2 (the
  spacing at v exceeds u16 |v|). The norm form peels the output rounding the same way. For
  attention, each kernel's bound becomes (1 + 2^-8) bound + 2^-8 V1 + 2^-134.
- Eager's 16-bit roundings between kernels are rounding nodes inside the value before the
  output: the pair is reported as rounding before the output (not the same function), and the
  bound above holds unchanged.
- Where: `num.rs` `num_f2fp16`, `halfin.rs` `half_out_node`, `equiv.rs` (Round canon,
  `compare`, `rnd16`, `round16_gap`), `norm.rs` (`NormBound::rounded`), `softmax.rs` (`wsum`).
- Status: **argued**. The rounding itself is exec.rs's `f32_to_bf16_rn` / `f32_to_f16_rn`.
  The bf16 GELU sweep validates the first bit for bit on all inputs against GB300, and s_alu2
  validates the f16 conversion. `rnd16` (f64) matches both on 2^20 values, and the interval and
  one-ulp claims hold on 400,000 random intervals (`round16_tests`). The bounds are the
  standard ones for round to nearest with 8 (11) significand bits. On the compile-vs-eager bf16
  pairs, GB300's differences reach the exact per-input bound (1.000 of it: one bf16 ulp) and
  never exceed it.
- If wrong: *false proof* of a tolerance.

### N-MMA-F8 · code
**One `tcgen05.mma.kind::f8f6f4` step is `g32-f25-rz-accin-tzero-efields`; with an f16 D it
rounds to nearest instead.** The step works as follows (GB300, sm_103a, 2026-11-03):
1. Take all 32 products of the instruction (K = 32) **and** the accumulator, and find the
   largest alignment exponent. For a product it is e_a + e_b, read from the exponent fields;
   a subnormal operand counts at its format's minimum exponent 1 - bias.
2. Truncate every term toward zero to 25 bits below that exponent.
3. Add the terms exactly and round once: toward zero to f32, or to nearest even to f16.

This is the kind::f16 structure (N-MMA) with one group of 32 instead of 16.
- Operand layout, K-major, in shared memory: each 16-byte core-matrix row holds 16 K elements.
  - FP8: one byte each.
  - FP6: 12 bytes, LSB-first bit stream; 4 bytes unused.
  - FP4: 8 bytes, low nibble first; 8 bytes unused.

  A K = 32 slice is two such rows, LBO apart (no swizzle), or contiguous (swizzled). An f16 D
  takes one TMEM column per element, in its low half, with the high half 0.
- Where: `mma_lp.rs` `DEFAULT_LP_MMA` / `DEFAULT_LP_MMA_F16`; `exec.rs` `complete_mma_lp`.
  Front-ends: PTX `kind::f8f6f4`; SASS `UTCQMMA` (with a sixth `tmem[URs]` operand it is
  block-scaled).
- Status: **validated.** `ptxv calib-mma probes/mma_f8` scores 3,624 candidates. Each
  configuration has 10 input sets of 8,192 outputs, 4 accumulating steps each:
  - sets: normal, uniformly random codes (subnormals included), log-uniform over the full
    range, cancellation, alignment and accumulator probes, a subnormal-alignment probe, f16
    ties below f32 precision, and wide-range first steps (e5m2 / e4m3 via idesc0) that leave
    large accumulators;
  - configurations: e4m3², e5m2², e4m3×e5m2, e2m3², e3m2², e2m1², e4m3×e2m1 (f32 D), e4m3²
    and e2m1² (f16 D).

  Results:
  - every f32 configuration matches exactly this model, or this model and the `einputs`
    variant where no subnormal decides the alignment. e5m2 and e4m3×e5m2 rule out `einputs`
    (4,547 and 2,215 of 8,192 outputs on the subnormal probe) and `eprod`;
  - e4m3² → f16 matches only the RN form (and its `einputs` twin). e2m1² → f16 is consistent
    with it: FP4 products cannot separate the candidates further.

  `probes/mma_f8/expected/` holds 9 of these runs, and `cargo test` checks both front-ends
  bitwise (tests/mma_lp.rs). Zero results are +0, as N-MMA (probes/mma_zero: e4m3 / e2m1,
  f32 and f16 D, C disabled / ±0).
- Not modeled, reported as `unmodeled`:
  - NaN / Inf operands or accumulators, subnormal f32 accumulators, f16 overflow, an f32
    result beyond the f32 range (N-MMA-BS, MISS 144);
  - MN-major FP6 / FP4 operands (8-bit MN-major and A in TMEM: S-TMEM), sparsity, negate.
- Numerics (this kind and N-MMA-BS): each step is a `NodeKind::Mma` node with the exact
  dataflow (exact specs such as `gemm_tn_mx` are checked on it). FP8 operands and ue8m0 scales
  are byte leaves (N-HALF-LEAF), and a block-scaled product is a b sa sb. The error contract
  (f32 D) is derived from the model (`mma_lp::lp_eps`, docs/equiv-mma.md §5):
  |computed - sum t| <= eps sum |t| + 2^-149, eps = tau + 2^-23 (1 + tau). A term that is a
  multiple of Q = 2^(emax - 25) loses nothing, any other less than Q. The setter is such a
  multiple. A normal setter has 2^emax <= |t_k|. A setter with a subnormal operand has
  2^emax <= 2^s |t_k| (s = the subnormal operands' mantissa bits), and `lp_trunc` counts the
  terms that can lose next to it by enumerating the formats' exponents. eps is 17.5u to 130u
  for FP8 (u = 2^-24), 17.5u to 34u for FP6 / FP4 operand pairs. Checked against the model on
  60,000 adversarial steps (error <= the data-dependent bound <= the contract) and reached
  within 0.9 (`mma_lp::contract_tests`). An f16 D is not tracked; FP6 / FP4 operands of this
  kind have no byte provenance (their products are untracked).
- If wrong: *miss* or *false alarm* in numerics on fp8 / fp6 / fp4 GEMMs.

### N-MMA-BS · code
**Block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` (`.block_scale`, kinds mxf8f6f4, mxf4, mxf4nvf4) computes what
`complete_mma_lp` computes** (GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.0, 2026-11-03).

Scale-factor placement in TMEM (all measured with `probes/mma_bs`, which writes SFA / SFB with
`tcgen05.st.32x32b` and varies them per lane and column):
- SFA for D row m (sub-partition w = m / 32) is the 32-bit word at lane m, column [sfa] + w.
- SFB for D column n is at lane 32w + n % 32, column [sfb] + n / 32; every sub-partition w reads
  its own copy, so all four must hold the same values (this is what
  `tcgen05.cp.32x128b.warpx4` writes).
- Within the word, the scale for K block b is byte sf_id (1X: one block per instruction),
  byte sf_id + b (2X, sf_id 0 or 2), byte b (4X, sf_id 0). The idesc sf_id fields select the
  bytes.
- The scale TMEM addresses must be 4-column aligned: unaligned ones fault with "misaligned
  address".
- Bits 30-31 of a scale-factor address (the top of the lane field) are ignored. CUTLASS puts
  the sf_id there as well as in the idesc. On GB300, setting them to 1 with idesc sf_id 0
  leaves D bitwise unchanged; idesc sf_id 1 changes it, again regardless of these bits. The
  simulator masks them.
- Illegal instruction on GB300: invalid sf_id for the vector size, mxf4nvf4 2X with ue4m3
  scales, mxf4 with A/B format code 5. The simulator reports these as faults.

Operand placement beyond K-major shared memory (2026-11-08; probes/mma_mxf8_tmem on GB300,
one CTA; probes/mma_bs/ts and mma_bs/mn on GB200, one CTA with M = 128 and cta_group::2 with
M = 256; 8-bit formats):
- A in TMEM: row m at lane m. Word c of the 8 columns at [a] holds elements 4c..4c+3, low byte
  first.
- MN-major SWIZZLE_128B, A or B: K-row k (128 M/N elements of a byte each) at
  (k / 8) SBO + (k % 8) 128, M/N atoms of 128 LBO apart, then the address swizzle.
- With A in TMEM / B MN-major (fa4 fwd P*V, idesc 0x08a10000) and with A MN-major
  (0x08a08000), D on GB300 equals the K-major shared-memory path on the same e4m3 operands
  and ue8m0 scales bitwise (four K = 32 MMAs). Both front-ends reproduce all three tiles
  bitwise.
- MN-major with the other layouts (S-TMEM, probes/mma_bs/mn): swizzled with span s (128 /
  64 / 32 B), element (r, k) at (r % s) + (r / s) LBO + (k % 8) s + (k / 8) SBO, then the
  address swizzle on the absolute address (a start 512 B into a 1024-byte SWIZZLE_128B atom
  reads the absolute phase); without swizzle, (r % 16) + (r / 16) SBO + (k % 8) 16 + (k / 8)
  LBO. cta_group::2: each CTA's A rows from its own TMEM or shared memory and the B rows
  (N/2) i.. (E-PAIR). Every D equals the K-major layout's bit for bit on GB200.
- Refused: these placements with 6- or 4-bit formats, MN-major A in TMEM, swizzled MN-major
  starts off a swizzle-row boundary, M = 64, and M = 128 with cta_group::2 (not probed).

Arithmetic:
- **mxf8f6f4** (scale_vec 1X, ue8m0, K = 32): the N-MMA-F8 model
  `g32-f25-rz-accin-tzero-efields` with terms a·b·sa·sb. The alignment exponent of a product is
  e_a + e_b + e(sa) + e(sb), from the exponent fields.
- **mxf4 / mxf4nvf4** (E2M1, packed 32 per 16-byte row, K = 64; 2X ue8m0 or 4X ue8m0 / ue4m3):
  `u16-f35-live-sfields` (`mma_lp.rs` `Fp4Model`). The steps:
  1. Sum the products of each unit of 16 K elements exactly. FP4 products are short, so the
     sum fits.
  2. Multiply each unit sum by its sa·sb.
  3. Compute emax: the maximum of the accumulator exponent and, over the *live* units only,
     e(sa) + e(sb) from the scale exponent fields. A unit is live if any of its products is
     nonzero.
  4. Truncate each unit and the accumulator toward zero at 2^(emax - 35), add them exactly, and
     round toward zero to f32.

  The alignment depends only on the scales, not on the product magnitudes. A targeted scan
  (two units, one large scale and one small, the small unit's product varied) showed that the
  point where the small unit is dropped depends only on the scale gap and the small product.
- Where: `mma_lp.rs` `DEFAULT_LP_MMA` / `DEFAULT_FP4_MMA`; `exec.rs` `complete_mma_lp`.
  Front-ends: PTX `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::1.kind::{mxf8f6f4,mxf4,mxf4nvf4}.block_scale
  [.scale_vec::NX]`; SASS `UTCQMMA` with a sixth `tmem[URs]` operand (mxf8f6f4), `UTCOMMA`
  (mxf4 and nvf4 2X), and `UTCOMMA.BLOCK16` (nvf4 4X).
- Status: **validated.** `ptxv calib-mma probes/mma_bs`, 4 chained steps × 8,192 outputs per
  set. Sets: normal, random codes, log-uniform, cancellation, alignment / accumulator /
  subnormal / mid probes, a scale gap set (per-block scales spread widely), and for ue4m3 an
  edge set (subnormal and maximum ue4m3 scales).
  - mxf8f6f4 (e4m3², e5m2², e2m1², e4m3×e2m3; 2,416 candidates): the only match is
    `g32-f25-rz-accin-tzero-efields`. Its g64 twin also matches, but with K = 32 it is the same
    function.
  - mxf4 2X ue8m0 (360 candidates): unit 16, frac 35. The live and fields choices cannot be
    told apart here.
  - mxf4nvf4 4X ue8m0: only the live variants match. With all scales instead, probe_sub
    matches 7,354 of 8,192 outputs.
  - mxf4nvf4 4X ue4m3: only the sfields variants match. The sprod variant matches 8,023 of
    8,192 outputs on ue4m3_edge, and unit 8 matches 7,180.

  `probes/mma_bs/expected/` holds 10 of these runs, and `cargo test` checks both front-ends
  bitwise (tests/mma_lp.rs). End to end, `fixtures/r3_cute_mxf8` (the CuTeDSL MXF8 GEMM,
  scales copied in with `tcgen05.cp`) equals GB300 bitwise through both front-ends, as does
  its B30 mutant.
- **cta_group::2** (`UTCOMMA.2CTA.BLOCK16`, 2026-11-04): the arithmetic is unchanged, and each
  CTA's D rows use the scale factors in that CTA's own TMEM, with the one-CTA layout: SFA for
  its rows and SFB for all N columns, so each CTA must hold all of SFB. A / B split as E-PAIR.
  Measured by `probes/tc_pair_bs` (mxf4nvf4 block16 ue4m3, M = 256, N = 64): every operand and
  scale word differs between the two CTAs. "Own SFA and SFB" matches GB300 on all 16,384
  outputs. SFB from the leader, SFB from the CTA that supplies B row n, and SFA from the leader
  each match only the half of the outputs where they coincide with it. Both front-ends equal
  GB300 bitwise (tests/mma_lp.rs). End to end: cuBLASLt's NVFP4 2-CTA kernel
  (`fixtures/c_smm_nvf4`) equals GB300 bitwise on the captured input and on 1,000 random ones
  (through `fixtures/c_equiv_nvf4_cublas`, docs/equiv-mma.md §5).
- Not modeled, reported as `unmodeled` / outside the model: NaN scales; NaN / Inf operands;
  subnormal f32 accumulators (D is f32 only for these kinds); MN-major FP6 / FP4 operands
  (8-bit MN-major and A in TMEM are modeled: S-TMEM, probes/mma_bs/mn and /ts); M = 64; a step
  whose scaled sum leaves the f32 range (`MMA f32 result overflow`). GB300 gives +-Inf there,
  never NaN, also when later steps of either sign follow (probes/mma_bs/ovf: mxf8 and mxf4,
  SFA 2^127 in every step or only the first; mxf8 every step: 1025 +Inf, 1023 -Inf of 2048).
  MISS 144: until 2026-11-12 the steps' round-toward-zero saturated such a sum to +-FLT_MAX
  (`mma_lp::round_int`) and the run was clean with outputs GB300 does not give; the rounding now
  overflows to +-Inf in both modes, which the tensor-core path reports.
- Zero results (also scaled sums that underflow) are +0, N-MMA's rule. Unmeasured for the
  block-scaled kinds themselves: probes/mma_zero covers kind::f8f6f4 and the other kinds,
  which share the rule; the code path is the same.
- Error contracts (docs/equiv-mma.md §5): mxf8f6f4 is N-MMA-F8's (one scale pair per step
  scales every product alike). mxf4 / mxf4nvf4 (`mma_lp::fp4_eps`): unit sums are multiples of
  2^(se - 2) (ue8m0) or 2^(se - 8) (ue4m3), so the setter is exact. A live unit has a product
  >= 1/4, so 2^se <= 4 (ue8m0) or 2^8 (ue4m3) times its terms. Up to 3 units and the
  accumulator lose less than Q = 2^(emax - 35): eps = 2.008u / 2.5u. **Requires** every ue4m3
  scale of a live unit to be nonzero: a zero scale sets emax while adding nothing to sum |t|, and
  no relative bound exists (a test truncates an accumulator to 0 that way). Steps with one get
  the loose contract; for inputs with one the contract is not claimed.
- If wrong: *miss* or *false alarm* in numerics on MX / NVFP4 GEMMs; a *false proof* of a
  tolerance if a contract is too small.

### N-MMA-K96 · code
**`tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf4nvf4.block_scale.block16` with K = 96 (instruction descriptor bit 31,
sm_103) is one 96-wide step of the N-MMA-BS FP4 model `u16-f35-live-sfields`, with these
operand and scale-factor layouts** (GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.0, 2026-11-09).
- Operands: 48 bytes (96 E2M1) per row and instruction. K-major without swizzle: three 16-byte
  chunks LBO apart. SWIZZLE_128B: contiguous within the row's 128 bytes; a slice that would
  cross the row end needs the absolute leading-dimension address mode (descriptor bit 52):
  the part past the row end is read at the same row of the matrix at address LBO (a slice 96
  bytes into the row: 32 bytes there, 16 at LBO; one at the row start: 48 contiguous bytes).
  Without bit 52 a crossing slice is refused.
- Scale factors (scale_vec::4X, six 16-element blocks): block b reads byte p = sf_id + b of
  the row's two TMEM words, p < 4 from column base + i, else byte p - 4 from column base + g
  + i. i is the D row's sub-partition for A (lane = row), n / 32 for B (lane 32 w + n % 32,
  every sub-partition its own copy); g = 4 for A (128 rows per CTA), max(4, N / 32) for B.
  sf_id 0 and 2 are measured; odd ids are refused. cta_group::2: each CTA's D rows use the
  scale factors in its own TMEM with this layout (as N-MMA-BS).
- Arithmetic: `DEFAULT_FP4_MMA` over 96 products and six scale pairs in one step.
- Where: `exec.rs` `complete_mma_lp` (`kn == 96`, `rb`, `sf_at`, `smem_desc_mode`);
  `calib_lp.rs` (K = 96 configurations, `sf_words_k96`, the 64 + 32 split candidates).
- Status: **validated** (hardware-measured; evidence classes kept apart):
  - Layout, exact arithmetic (all sums exact in f32, so D identifies every byte read):
    probes/mma_k96 id_sfa* / id_sfb* (each scale byte a distinct ue4m3 value per lane, column
    and byte), layout_* (random codes, scales 1), abs (bit 52), N = 64 / 128 / 256, without
    swizzle and SWIZZLE_128B, sf_id 0 and 2: 21 sets, every output of both front-ends equals
    GB300's (tests/mma_lp.rs `mma_k96_layouts_match_gb300`).
  - Rounding: `ptxv calib-mma probes/mma_k96/calib` (four chained K = 96 MMAs per output,
    8,192 outputs per set; deterministic over 3 runs): ue8m0 (9 sets) and ue4m3 (10 sets,
    incl. ue4m3_edge and scale_gap). `u16-f35-live-sfields` is the only member of the
    720-candidate family (360 one-step models and their 64 + 32 splits) that matches every
    output of both scale formats; the best split matches 1,825..8,192 per set. Six of the
    sets are replayed through both front-ends bit for bit (`mma_k96_both_fronts_match_gb300`).
  - cta_group::2, M = N = 256 (the CuTe DSL cascade GEMM's idesc 0x90400480): probes/mma_k96
    pair, every operand and scale word different between the CTAs, 65,536 outputs, both
    front-ends = GB300 (50 runs).
- If wrong: *miss* only for unmeasured shapes, which are refused (N other than 64 / 128 /
  256, M other than 128 per CTA, odd sf ids, K = 96 with other kinds or 2X).
- Retire: never (a hardware fact).

### N-CVT-LP · code
**Narrow-format conversions (`cvt` to / from e4m3, e5m2, e2m3, e3m2, e2m1, ue8m0, and the
`.rs` packs) compute what `lowp.rs` computes** (GB300, CUDA 13.0, 2026-11-03):
- Encodes (`F2FP...PACK_AB_MERGE_C`, `...UNPACK_B_MERGE_C` from f16x2 / bf16x2): round to nearest
  even from the exact value (f32 subnormals included); `.satfinite`: overflow and ±Inf give
  ±max. NaN gives the positive NaN code (e4m3 / e5m2 0x7f) or, for FP6 / FP4, which have no
  NaN, the positive maximum (0x1f / 0x7). `.relu` maps negative inputs and -0 to +0. ptxas
  requires `.satfinite` for these targets.
- ue8m0 (`.rz` / `.rp`, f32 or bf16x2): the exponent of |x| (sign ignored), rounded down /
  up; below 2^-127 gives 0. Without `.satfinite`, overflow and Inf give 0xff (NaN); with it,
  0xfe. NaN always gives 0xff.
- Decodes (`F2FP.<F16|BF16>.<fmt>.UNPACK_B`) are exact. NaN gives 0x7fff, and ue8m0 0 gives
  bf16 0x0040 (2^-127). FP6 codes are read from the low 6 bits of each byte (the top 2 bits
  are ignored). `.relu` maps negatives to +0. An e2m1x2 source byte other than byte 0
  (`UNPACK_B Rd, Ra.B1 / .B2 / .B3`, ptxas's lowering of `mov.b32 {c0, c1, c2, c3}` + `cvt` of
  `c1..c3`) reads byte k of Ra; `probes/e2m1_bytes` (2026-11-06) covers every byte value in
  every position, plain and `.relu` (`.relu` also maps -0 to +0).
- `.satfinite` on a bf16x2 decode (`cvt.rn [.relu] .satfinite .bf16x2.<fmt>x2`; ptxas 13.3 with
  PTX ISA 9.3 accepts it, 13.0 does not) is refused by both fronts: PTX ISA 9.5 section
  9.7.10.24 maps |x| > MAX_NORM to the sign-preserved MAX_NORM, so an e5m2 +-Inf gives
  +-0x7f7f, which the decode op does not model; f2fp_lp takes `UNPACK_B` only without
  `.SATFINITE`. GB300 (probes/cvt_lp_satfinite, every e5m2 code pair, 2026-11-10): the plain
  decode with that rule applied (and `.relu` first) equals the `.satfinite` outputs on all
  65,536 pairs; NaN codes give 0x7fff with or without it. Before (MISS 60) cvt_lp dropped
  `.satfinite` on decodes: 1,020 of 65,536 words differed from GB300, 511 with `.relu`. No
  kernel_db PTX has a `.satfinite` decode. Placement: the refusal is precision (the ISA
  defines the form; a model would be strict and gb300 alike).
- Forms ptxas 13.0 and 13.3 both reject are refused by the PTX front (2026-11-11, T2; the
  cvt enumeration of 466,400 single-instruction lines, each through both ptxas versions and
  the front): an f8 / f6 / f4 x2 encode takes `.rn.satfinite` (from f32 pairs, f16x2 or
  bf16x2), the ue8m0x2 encode `.rz` / `.rp` without `.relu` (from f32 pairs or bf16x2), an
  `.rs` x4 encode `.satfinite`; ue8m0x2 decodes only to bf16x2, without `.relu`. Operands
  have the register types some version accepts (8,718 lines with other register types and
  immediates, 13.0 at `.version 9.0`, 13.3 at `.version 9.3`): an x2 encode writes a .b16
  (e2m1x2: a .b8) from .f32 / .b32 values or immediates, or from a .b32 half pair (bf16x2
  into e2m1x2 or ue8m0x2: any 32-bit type); an x4 encode writes a .b32 (e2m1x4: a .b16) from
  .f32 / .b32 values or immediates with .b32 random bits; a decode reads a .b16 (e2m1x2: a
  .b8) into a .b32 (ue8m0x2: any 32-bit type). Before, cvt_lp lowered 384 lines of the
  enumeration (other roundings, missing `.satfinite`, 16-bit e2m1x2 registers, f16x2 ue8m0
  forms) and, until the operand types, 5,456 of the 8,526 lines of the other set that both
  reject, with the semantics of the accepted form. No ptxas output contains them; the
  refusal is precision.
- Scaled bf16x2 decodes (`cvt.rn [.relu] .scaled::n2::ue8m0 .bf16x2.<fmt>x2 d, a, scale`; ptxas
  13.3 with PTX ISA 9.3, not 13.0) are not modeled: the PTX front refuses `.scaled` (cvt_lp),
  and the SASS front lifts `F2FP [.RELU] .BF16.<fmt>.UNPACK_B d, a, s.H0` only with the
  immediate 0x7f7f.H0 that ptxas 13.3 gives the unscaled decodes (2^0 in both lanes; a register
  or any other scale is refused). The two-operand form `UNPACK_B d, a`, which ptxas prints for
  the F16 decodes and BF16.E8, is lifted as before. GB300 (probes/cvt_lp_scaled, every code pair
  of the five formats, plain and `.relu`, with mixed scale pairs, 2026-11-10): each lane is the
  decoded value times 2^(s - 127), rounded once to bf16, NaN codes and the scale 0xff 0x7fff; an
  exact reference outside ptxv differs in 0 of 655,360 words. Before (MISS 61) the SASS front
  ignored the scale operand: 562,392 of the 655,360 words differed. The identity scale of the
  unscaled decode: probes/cvt_lp_satfinite's `kernel_ptx.cubin` (ptxas 13.3, the plain e5m2
  decode) equals GB300 on all 65,536 pairs. No kernel_db cubin has a bf16 `UNPACK_B` with a
  scale operand (ptxas 13.0 prints none). Placement: SASS front only (GB300 measured); the
  refusal is precision.
- `.rs` (stochastic rounding): the random addend sits just below the result's last bit, and
  the result rounds up iff dropped bits + addend carry into it. The addend is 13 bits for
  f16 and 16 bits otherwise. Which bits of the random word feed which lane is in
  `lowp::rs_bits`:
  - f16x2 / bf16x2: the high lane takes r[16..], the low lane r[0..];
  - 8-bit lanes: per `F2FP...RS Rd, Ra, Rb, Rc`, b takes c[16..32) and a takes its 16-bit
    bit reversal;
  - e2m1: b takes c[24..32) · c[8..16), and a takes its bit reversal.

  For x4, ptxas chains two F2FPs, and the second takes the first's merged result as c. So
  the PTX lanes {a, b, e, f} get rev(r.hi), r.hi, rev(r.lo), r.lo for 8-bit formats.
- `MERGE_C`: d = c << (2 lanes) | lanes (8-bit lanes: c << 16; e2m1: c << 8).
- s2f6 (`cvt.rn.satfinite.scaled::n2::ue8m0.bf16x2.s2f6x2`, SASS `F2FP.SATFINITE.BF16.S2_6
  .UNPACK_B`; `lowp::cvt_s2f6x2_scaled`, `Op::CvtS2f6x2`): lane i takes byte i of the 16-bit
  code pair and byte i of the 16-bit scale pair; the code is a two's-complement 8-bit fixed
  point with 6 fraction bits (int8 / 64), times 2^(scale - 127); one round to nearest even to
  bf16, subnormals kept, overflow to +-0x7f7f (only -128/64 * 2^127 overflows); scale 0xff
  gives 0x7fff for every code. `probes/s2f6_cvt` (GB300, 2026-11-08): every (code, scale)
  pair of both lanes through register and immediate scales and either data half = the model
  bitwise (`cargo test`), and `run.sh` checks all 2^32 (data, scale) pairs against a C model
  on the GPU: 0 mismatches. PTX ISA 9.1: ptxas 13.1 assembles it, ptxas 13.0 does not. The
  PTX front lowers it to the same op (`a`, `scale` .b16, `hi` = false); `probes/s2f6_cvt`'s
  kernel.ptx is bitwise on the PTX front as well.
  The other forms, `cvt.rn[.relu][.satfinite]...s2f6x2` (SASS `F2FP[.SATFINITE][.RELU].BF16
  .S2_6.UNPACK_B`, `relu` / `sat` on the op): without `.satfinite` the one overflow gives
  -Inf (0xff80); `.relu` maps negative lanes to +0, and scale 0xff still gives 0x7fff.
  `probes/s2f6_cvt/forms` (gen.py): every (code, scale) pair in each of the four lane positions with
  independently varying neighbours, all four forms, 65,536 threads. Evidence, kept apart:
  - GB300-measured (sm_103a, ptxas 13.1, 2026-11-09): the full set's per-form hashes
    (sweep.json `gb300`) = the model (`s2f6_model_replays_gpu_sweeps`); the 1024-thread sample
    (gb300_out.bin) = both front-ends bitwise (`probe_s2f6_cvt_forms_match_hardware`).
  - GB200-measured (sm_100a, CUDA 13.1, an external sweep): the same full-set hashes (sweep.json
    `gb200`) and sample (gb200_out.bin), identical to GB300's.
  The PTX front refuses every other `.scaled` form (a `.scaled` dispatch ahead of the other
  `cvt` branches). Before this rule the `.relu` and non-`.satfinite` forms were refused too,
  not misread: the PTX front with "this cvt is not modeled yet" (`cvt_lp` has refused unknown
  modifiers since 2026-11-09), the SASS front for the instruction nvdisasm 13.0 prints nothing
  for (model: ptxv runs of `probes/s2f6_cvt/forms` before and after the rule). The SASS
  decoder (`undis.rs`) reads `.SATFINITE` from hi bit 13 and `.RELU` from hi bit 11 (nvdisasm
  13.3 on all four forms, register and immediate scales).
- Where: `lowp.rs`; `exec.rs` `Op::CvtPack` / `CvtRsX4` / `CvtUnpack` / `CvtS2f6x2`; PTX
  `cvt_lp`; SASS `f2fp_lp`.
- Status: **validated.** `ptxv cvt-sweep probes/cvt_lp` covers 51 PTX forms, each over every
  input, and finds 0 mismatches:
  - every 16-bit source value (2^16) in both lanes;
  - every 8-bit / 4-bit code pair for the decodes;
  - 2^20 f32 operand sets: every representable value and midpoint of each FP8 / FP6 / FP4
    format ±2 ulps, powers of two ±1 ulp, zeros, subnormals, Inf and NaN in both signs, then
    shaped random values, each with random bits.

  `probes/cvt_lp/sweep.json` holds the per-op hashes of the hardware outputs, and `cargo
  test` recomputes them from the model. `probes/cvt_lp/gb300_out.bin` checks both front-ends
  bitwise on 1,024 sampled threads.
- If wrong: a *miss* or *false alarm* in numerics on narrow-format data. Forms outside the
  probe stay unmodeled: scalar f16 / bf16 `.rn` with `.relu` / `.satfinite`, other SASS F2FP
  forms, and `.H1` sources of `UNPACK_B_MERGE_C`. The packed
  `cvt.rn[.relu].satfinite.{f16x2,bf16x2}.f32` encodes also go through cvt_lp; probes/cvt_f16
  measures them on both fronts (N-CVT-F16, 2026-11-10).

### N-BOUND · code
**The Cor 1a a-priori bound uses each rounding node's ε** (u for FADD, the model ε for MMA)
and is first-order.
- Where: `num.rs` `out_rec`.
- Status: **argued** (fp_noise THEORY). Thm 1 itself is checked exactly, not assumed. The
  bound has never been violated, but it is not a proof for inputs outside the run.

### N-NUM-TRACK · code
**`ptxv num` makes no error claim for an element whose value depends on an input-derived
value without a tracked derivation.** num's DAG (non-segment mode) has nodes for plain FADD,
fp32 atomic adds, MMA steps, conversions, MUFU, FFMA2 of the form x*1 + 0, and FMNMX without
modifiers or FTZ on non-NaN operands (exact `Max` nodes: Thm 1 does not hold through them, and
both children's terms bound their error). Every other instruction (FFMA / FMUL, a negated or
FTZ FADD, FMNMX of |x|, other FFMA2 / FMUL2 / FADD2, bit operations) drops the history of its
result. Input buffers are tainted, so such a result becomes an
`Opaque` leaf when a tracked node reads it, and an output word written from it is
input-derived without a node. Either makes the element `untracked`. num reports these
elements as not analyzed, and computes Thm 1, the bounds and max_err over the other elements
only. bf16 / f16 outputs are read per 16-bit element (the node from the 16-bit provenance,
N-HALF-LEAF; errors in that format's ulps). Outputs of other dtypes, and every output of a run that reported a fault or an
`unmodeled` finding (its threads stop early), are not analyzed.
The result of a rounding instruction that gets no node is input data whatever its operands
(`rounding_op`: floating-point arithmetic, MUFU and other approximations, narrowing and
integer-to-float conversions, f64 operations, HMMA, `multimem.ld_reduce`; an integer-to-f32
conversion with |result| < 2^24 is exact and spared), so a dropped rounding of kernel
parameters, special registers or constants is never an exact constant leaf. So is a value a
register operation computes outside the DAG from a node holding a rounding (`num_clobber`,
`NumState::rounded`: a bit operation or an untracked float operation of an FADD, atomic add, MMA
or MUFU result), and the value a float atomic add returns (f32, f64, bf16x2 and bf16x4, bf16: a
rounded partial sum of the location's updates without a node). Atomics other than f32 adds
carry the rule through memory (`Machine::num_atom_rounding`, MISS 114): the old value is input
data when a word the atomic read held a node with a rounding (or 16-bit provenance of one); the
word is input data when an integer, bitwise or min / max read-modify-write computes it from such
a value or from a register holding a rounding or input data, and after an f64 atomic add (a
rounded sum without a node). An exchange, and a compare-and-swap that swaps, store the new value
as a store does (its node, 16-bit provenance and taint). A compare-and-swap whose old or compare
value holds a rounding or input data makes its words and its returned value or swap flag input
data, swapped or not (the exact computation may decide the other way); one that did not swap on
exact values leaves the word as it was. A bf16 atomic lane without a node, a float atomic max
idiom (N-FMAX) that fails on an operand holding a rounding, and a 16-bit bulk reduction without
16-bit tracking leave input data. An atomic's words lose their nodes (a 64-bit atomic both
words, a 16-bit one the word holding it). Partial-width and rearranging accesses carry it too
(MISS 115): a register that gets bytes of a word holding a rounding without the word's node (a
16-bit or 8-bit load, ldmatrix .trans, unaligned or .b8: `num_ld`, `Machine::num_clobber_mem`)
is input data; so is a word a store or copy writes in part (a 16-bit or 8-bit store, stmatrix
.trans or .b8, a copy of 2-byte elements or a misaligned one: `num_st`, `num_copy_snapshot`)
when its old node or the stored register's node held a rounding, or a copied byte came from a
word whose node did. Local memory follows the same rules (MISS 158; `Machine::num_local_st_sub`,
`num_local_ld_sub`, `num_local_st64`, `num_local_ld64`): a 16-bit or 8-bit store (STL.U16 /
.U8, `st.local` of 16 or 8 bits) gives its bytes the stored register's taint and 16-bit
provenance, and its word is input data when it mixes bytes of a rounding (the register's node
or the word's old node) with other bytes; a 16-bit or 8-bit load takes its bytes' taint, and is
input data when the word holds a rounding without its node; the PTX front's 64-bit `ld` /
`st.local` of a 64-bit register moves both words' nodes and the 8 bytes' taint. Until MISS 158
the loads wrote a constant and the stores the merged word or each word as an immediate, so input
data and roundings passed through local memory as exact constants. A NIC atomic's 8-byte target
follows the same rule per 4-byte word (MISS 257, `Machine::num_nic_atomic`; the WQE's operands are
read from the send queue like the old value): a word is input data where what the atomic leaves in
it may differ in the exact computation: a word a fetch-add computes from a word or operand that is
input data or holds a rounding, the high word of a fetch-add whose carry such a low word decides,
both words of a compare-and-swap whose old value or compare operand is such (failed or not), and
both words of one that swapped in such an operand. Otherwise a word the atomic left unchanged keeps
its node, taint and 16-bit provenance, and a word it changed holds an exact integer result (no
node). From MISS 224's fix until MISS 257 both words lost their nodes without taint, so the rounded
value an unchanged word still held, and an integer result computed from a rounded word, were exact
constants: probes/nic_atomic_keeps_word (a compare-and-swap that fails, fetch-adds of 0 and 1 on a
word holding rn(0.1f + 0.2f), rn(1 + 1e-8f)) printed abs_err 0 and bound 0 on both fronts where the
exact errors are 7.45e-9 and 1.0e-8; before MISS 224 the nodes stayed, right for the unchanged
words, while the low word a fetch-add of 1 changed kept its old node. GB300: the payload, 20 of 20
scrubbed runs equal to the simulator's; the atomics do not run on the hardware runner (no queue
pair) [GB300 measured: payload; argued: a compare-and-swap that fails writes nothing, a fetch-add
of 0 writes the bits the word held; model: claims]. fixtures/c_num_nic_atomic_f32 (each case on
words holding roundings of constants, of input data, bf16 elements and exact constants):
`tests/num_untracked.rs` `nic_atomics_keep_unchanged_words_and_taint_decided_ones`; mutants
nic-atomic-keep, nic-atomic-untracked, nic-atomic-decided, nic-atomic-carry and nic-atomic-half
caught. And no output of a
run carries a claim when its control flow, effects or addresses depend on input data
(`Taint::control_pcs`): a branch, EXIT, store, atomic, barrier or asynchronous operation under
a data-dependent guard, or a data-dependent branch target, load / store / atomic address or
shuffle lane. num follows the run's path and addresses; the exact computation (the same
program in real arithmetic) may take another path or access other elements. The N-FMAX
diamond branch and comparisons fixed by finiteness (N-FINITE) are not input data. A selection
by a data-dependent predicate and a register write under a data-dependent guard lose their
node and are tainted (untracked), as before.
Control decided by a rounded value is refused as for input data. A rounding without a node is
input data (above); so is a value a register operation computes outside the DAG from a node
holding a rounding (`Machine::rounded_pre`, `num_clobber`: a comparison, a conversion to an
integer or bit operations of an FADD, atomic add, MMA or MUFU result of parameters, special
registers or constants, such as a float loop counter). A guard, branch, address, store guard or
shuffle lane computed from one is a refusal (`control_pcs`), and so is an address, branch target
or shuffle lane read directly from a register whose node holds a rounding. Two exceptions keep
index arithmetic out of the refusal, with no residual case: (1) ptxas's lowering of a 32-bit
integer division or remainder by a run-time value, matched structurally and checked per thread
(N-NUM-UDIV); (2) ptxas materializes a 32-bit constant as `HFMA2 R, -RZ, RZ, hi, lo`: a zero
product plus the immediate, exact in every lane (fma(+-0, +-0, c) = c). Only that form is spared
(every operand an immediate, one factor zero); any other all-immediate rounding instruction is a
rounding (ptxas 13.x keeps `MUFU.TANH R, 0.1000000015` unfolded). The PTX front has no such
exception.
The SASS front claims an element only where the PTX front claims it with the same exact value,
and no output the PTX front refuses (MISS 108, `main.rs` `cmd_num`); where the case has PTX
that the PTX front-end refuses, the SASS front runs without claims (MISS 160; until then it
claimed alone there, with no PTX claim to bound it). ptxas folds
roundings of constants (`mul.rn`, `add.rn`, `ex2.approx.ftz` of immediates) into immediates,
which the SASS front would take as exact constants; the PTX front has the roundings (one without
a node is input data, one with a node, an `add.rn`, carries its exact value). An immediate alone
does not tell a literal from a folded rounding: mul.rn(0.1f, 3) folds to 0x3e99999a, the
literal 0.3f, and add.rn(1, 2^-24) to 1.0. For a kernel given as SASS only (a cubin: every
kernel_db capture) the reference is the SASS program and its immediates are its constants; a
rounding ptxas folded before the binary existed is not seen.
- Where: `num.rs` `out_rec` (`untracked`), `rounding_op`, `effect_op`, `Taint::control_pcs`
  (`taint_pre`, `taint_post`, `num_store_origins`), `num_clobber`, `NumState::rounded`,
  `Machine::rounded_pre`, `NumState::rounding_taint`, `Machine::num_atom_rounding`,
  `Machine::num_old_rounded`, `num_ld`, `num_st`, `Machine::num_clobber_mem`,
  `num_read_snapshot` / `num_copy_snapshot`; `main.rs` `cmd_num`.
- Status: **enforced**. Before this check, `exact` took the simulated value of the untracked
  value as exact. A row sum of squares (FFMA chain) reported max_err = 0, Thm 1 exact, with
  no warning, while GB300 differs from the fp64 sum by up to 4.1 ulp
  (`fixtures/c_num_sumsq_f32`). The rounding and control parts (2026-11-10) close three
  holes the first check left, each a fixture whose expected/ is GB300's output (GB300 ==
  simulator bitwise, 20 of 20 runs), checked by `tests/num_untracked.rs` against the exact
  value:
  - `fixtures/c_num_param_f32`: x + rn(a*b), rn(a*b), x + rn(f32(%tid) * 0.1f) and
    x + ex2.approx(a) for f32 parameters a = 0.1f, b = 3. Before: max_err 0.50 ulp over all

### N-NUM-UDIV · code
**`ptxv num` takes the quotient and remainder of ptxas's 32-bit integer division by a run-time
divisor as exact where it checks them.** ptxas lowers `div` / `rem` `.u32` (and `.s32`, on |n|
and |d|, then the signs) by a divisor d that is not a constant to: a = I2F[.U32].RP d,
b = MUFU.RCP a, c = b + 0x0ffffffe (b times 2^32, less 2 ulp), e = F2I.U32.TRUNC c, the
Newton step q1 = e + hi(e (-e d)), and per dividend n the estimate q = hi(q1 n), the
remainder r = n - q d and up to two corrections (r >= d: r -= d, q += 1, in place under the
predicate or by a selection). Its rounded values are input data like any rounding without a
node, so the comparisons and selections inside it are tainted; `udiv_idioms` matches this shape
in straight-line SASS (no branch or branch target between its steps), and where an instruction
outside the instance reads a quotient (remainder), `Machine::udiv_resolve` checks it per thread
against n / d (n mod d) of the dividend and divisor the instance read: both untainted, d != 0
and the value equal, the register is exact and untainted; anything else stays input data. A
reciprocal no estimate reads, a division split by a branch, ptxas's uniform-datapath form (the
reciprocal moved to a uniform register by R2UR, the Newton step, estimate and corrections in
UIMAD / UISETP; Triton's persistent GEMMs), a step that reads a register copy of an
intermediate value (`IMAD.MOV.U32 R, RZ, RZ, -e` before the Newton multiply), and every other
use of a rounding of non-input values are not excepted (N-NUM-TRACK). The PTX front has no such
idiom: `div` / `rem` are integer operations there, and no claiming case's PTX has a float
division idiom.
- Why the quotient is exact [argued]: a >= d (RP), so e <= 2^32 / d as long as MUFU.RCP
  over-estimates 1 / a by less than the 2-ulp bias (e d <= 2^32 also keeps the Newton step's
  -e d from wrapping). With e = (2^32 / d)(1 - eps), the Newton step gives
  0 <= 2^32 / d - q1 < (2^32 / d) eps^2 + 1. RP, a reciprocal within 1 ulp and the bias give
  eps < 2^-21 + d / 2^32 (the last term from the truncation), so (2^32 / d) eps^2 < 1 for
  d <= 2^31 (for larger d, e is 0 or 1 and q = 0). Then for every n < 2^32,
  0 <= n / d - q < 3: q <= floor(n / d), r = n - q d < 3 d, and two corrections reach
  floor(n / d) and n mod d. The bound the correction needs: an over-estimate below 2 ulp and an
  under-estimate below about 2^-16 relative. MUFU.RCP is within 0.975 ulp of 1 / x on all 2^32
  inputs and modeled bit-exactly, so the simulator's quotient is GB300's [GB300 measured,
  N-MUFU: `ptxv mufu-sweep`, 0 differences, 2026-11-03]. The per-thread check makes each
  excepted value the exact computation's for this run [model].
- Where: `num.rs` `udiv_idioms`, `UdivStep`, `Machine::udiv_resolve`, `Taint::udiv_regs`.
- Status: **enforced**. `fixtures/c_num_index_f32` (u32 quotient deciding a load address, a
  store guard and an EXIT guard) and `fixtures/c_num_udiv_f32` (div / rem .u32 by 7 and .s32
  by -9 deciding load addresses and a store guard; the .s32 remainder corrected by a selection)
  keep every claim on both fronts, each |GB300 - exact| (GB300 == simulator bitwise, 20 of 20
  runs). `fixtures/c_num_udiv_data_f32` (the idiom on an input buffer, deciding an address) is
  refused. The independent review counted 364 decisions the former `rnd_only` exception excused
  in the claiming fixtures and kernel_db cases, all from 51 MUFU.RCP sites of this shape.
  Of the 10 kernel_db outputs that exception carried (a run without it refuses
  them), the match keeps 5 (cute.MatnormSegmentBroadcastKernel,
  triton._all_gather_transpose_kernel_nd, _reduce_scatter_transpose_kernel_nd,
  _triton_fsdp_chunk_cat.f32.8x512, _triton_matmul.bf16.48x32) and refuses 5
  (cute._ChunkCatGeneral.bf16.8x131600, triton._triton_fsdp_chunk_cat.bf16.8x131600 and
  .8x819200, _triton_fsdp_split_copy.bf16.16x524288, two outputs: a register copy of -e before
  the Newton multiply); fixtures/r2_triton_gemm's SASS front is refused (the uniform-datapath
  form) [model: num A/B of the two commits]. Mutants num-udiv-off (precision), num-udiv-taint (each caught).
- Evidence: GB300 measured (MUFU.RCP sweep, N-MUFU; the fixtures); model (num before / after,
  the A/B); argued (the error analysis above; ptxas's lowering read from its output).
- Placement: gb300. The exactness of the lowering rests on MUFU.RCP's measured accuracy and
  bit-exact model; a different unit could make the estimate leave the corrections' range (the
  per-thread check would then refuse, not claim).
- If wrong: a quotient taken as exact where the exact computation's differs: control, an
  address or a store decided by it follows the run's path (a too-small claim). Precision
  losses: forms the match misses refuse the control their quotient decides.

### N-NUM-NONFINITE · code
**`ptxv num` never leaves a non-finite element out of max_err.** An element whose simulated
(hw) or exact value is not finite is classified before any aggregate:
- exact value finite, hw not finite (an overflow to inf, or NaN from one): the error is infinite.
  The exact value of finite leaves is exact (f64 expansions), so the claim is definite.
- exact value not finite: it comes from non-finite leaves, and the f64 expansion arithmetic does
  not follow the extended reals (the expansion of inf + x is NaN, not inf; an overflowed value
  minus a true infinity gives NaN where the exact value is -inf). The exact value counts only
  where no rounding node in the tree holds a non-finite value against a finite exact value and
  none has a non-finite exact value from finite operands (`nonfinite_inside`). Then an identical
  hw value (the same infinity, or NaN for NaN) has error 0; anything else is not analyzed
  (`OutRec::nonfinite`, counted with the untracked elements, reported as "a non-finite value
  without a determined exact value").
- a MUFU / approx node whose true function has no finite value at its operand's exact value: no
  real value (sqrt, rsqrt, lg2 of a negative number), an infinity or a pole (lg2, rsqrt, rcp of

  x = 0 was claimed exact where its error is 1000, and a product of such a value under an MMA

An element that is not analyzed has NaN error fields and no finite exact value (MISS 258: one
flagged through a MUFU's operand printed the error of an exact value made up from it).
The aggregates follow: max_err and max_err_ulps take every analyzed element (an infinite error
makes them infinite); Cor 1a and the running bound count an infinite error as a violation; the
mean bound / error ratio takes every analyzed element with a nonzero error (an infinite error
counts 0); an output with a violation of a bound reports that bound as unknown for every element
(CSV "unknown", JSON null) and no ratio (MISS 206, defense in depth: a bound that one of the
output's own analyzed elements exceeds is no bound; `tests/num_untracked.rs`
`bounds_an_output_violates_are_unknown`, mutant num-bound-unknown); the spec match compares non-finite exact values by identity (expansions of
infinities do not subtract to zero); rel_err is infinite for a nonzero error at an exact 0.
An element's error in ulps is its absolute error over the spacing of the f32 encodings at its
computed value (`num.rs` `ulp_f32`); at +-FLT_MAX that spacing is 2^104, the distance below it
(MISS 161; until then it was the distance to +inf, infinite, and the figure 0 there).

(`abs_err > 0`), and rel_err printed 0 for a NaN error at an exact 0, so an overflow or a NaN
output reported a finite max_err over every element (MISS 63).

### N-ERRDIST-NONFINITE · code
**`ptxv errdist` compares an output with a NaN / Inf value wherever its reference is known.**
A single kernel's output against RN of its finite exact value in the output format (an
infinity where the exact magnitude rounds past the format's maximum; at the overflow tie, max
plus half its spacing, the exact value's low part decides, and below the tie RN is max):
equal only as the same infinity; NaN never is. Until MISS 66's follow-up `round_out` gave the
infinity at the tie whatever the low part (the fifth review's D1): with a point mass there
(const, discrete or mixture specs) Tier 3 headlined 0 [0, 1.22e-2] where GB300 differs on
1/6 of the bf16 / f16 outputs (rE_tieb, rE_tieh, the negative tie) and 1/12 at f32 (rE_tiefm),
and one FFMA's correct max was a false alarm of 0.0835 (rE_tief). A pair's C against R bit for
bit: equal only as the same infinity, an
encoding of its own, unlike any NaN or number; where both are NaN their bits are the NaN
payloads, which the DAG does not model (its validation matches NaN with NaN), so the output is
left out, out of the domain. A compared output counts in P(differ); its error stays out of the
error moments and the PMF's lattice (an equal one is at 0 ulp), and one that differs from its
reference exceeds every worst-case bound. An equal infinity is a correct overflow, outside the
bound's premise that no value overflows: neither checked nor over (until MISS 66's follow-up a
single kernel's was over: 9561 correct overflows flagged WORST CASE EXCEEDED on the tie
probes, the fifth review's D5). An output whose exact value is not determined (non-finite in
the exact arithmetic:
non-finite leaves, past f64's range, a non-finite scale) is left out of a single kernel's
P(differ), out of the domain; a pair compares C with R without it and leaves the moments out.
Tiers 1 and 2 other than the elementwise law are refused when Tier 3 has a NaN / Inf output
that differs from its reference: their laws model rounding errors, not an overflow or an
invalid operation. A validation of them whose observed run has one does not agree, nor does
one whose observed share left out lies above Tier 3's bound q (its 95% interval's lower end
above q; until MISS 66's follow-up the share was printed only, the D6 item). The
elementwise law compares such outputs itself, per element value. A Tier 3 whose compared
outputs are all NaN / Inf and equal to their reference saw no rounding and is refused (MISS
64), so a case where every output is NaN / Inf does not report P(differ) 0 on equal infinities
alone; one where some differ stands (MISS 64's follow-up: y = RN(RN(x 2^100) C + 2) at x in
[2^28, 2^29), Tier 3 1.0 [0.9855, 1] over 300 inputs, GB300 12800 of 12800 outputs differ,
was refused), and so does a validation's agreement on them: a validation run that compared
no finite output and no NaN / Inf output that differs (equal infinities alone) does not agree.
P(output NaN / Inf) (`p_nonfinite`) is reported apart
from the headline either way.
Outputs left out of P(differ) for want of a determined outcome (no determined exact value, an
instruction slice without an identified real function above them or whose alternatives
disagree there (MISS 147), a pair's NaN in both kernels; `mc::Obs::left`) move P(differ) over
every output by at most their share. Its one-sided bound q is taken as P(differ)'s interval
is, inputs as the unit (`mc::left_share`: the share per input, with the input-level bound at
any count since MISS 139), and every estimate's interval widens by q; an estimate, Tier 3
included, stands only while q is within 10% of its P (`widen_left`), as for MISS 57's unknown
share, which refuses the run. Until MISS 139, at 20 or more inputs with a left-out output q
was the batch-means interval, which a rare input that leaves out many outputs escapes: the
fifth review's rE_lmix (4096 outputs left out on 2e-3 of the inputs, pairs on most; share
2.2395e-3, P(differ) over every output 0.06490) held P in 0 of 35 runs, 21
headlines excluding it with q about 2.9e-4 (the D3 item). Tier 3's own interval and the bounds
that widen it (q, MISS 57's U) share the 5% by the union bound (`mc::level_share`: 97.5% each
with one bound); until MISS 66's follow-up each took 5%, about 92.5% jointly (D7). Tier 3's P
is over the
compared outputs. The elementwise law measures its own share without a determined outcome,
leaves it out and widens by it, and its exact form (Tier 0) is refused with any. Importance
sampling refuses inputs with outputs left out. Until 2026-11-11 such outputs moved neither
(MISS 66): P(differ) was conditional on the rest, with a note.
